eugeniosegala/mako.name: MAKO Decky v4.6.0
eugeniosegala/mako.body: > Looking for the standalone Vulkan layer? See [MAKO Renderer v4.6.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/render-v4.6.0). ## What's new in MAKO Decky v4.6.0 ### Release codename: Tempest > _“By dawn, the fleet understood: the tempest was a road with teeth.”_ > > **Mira Valen, _Charts of the Drowned Horizon_** --- Tempest brings faster, leaner Frame Generation and steadier pacing through the matching Renderer, alongside per-game shader tuning, smoother controller navigation and clearer support reports. _Native source-build comparison on AMD Steam Machine (NAVI33/RADV). Synthetic results; game FPS and Steam Deck gains were not measured. Buffer memory excludes model weights, shared images, driver memory and game VRAM._ - **GPU Headroom:** Under **Performance**, choose a 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% GPU reserve and adjust it live during Frame Generation. The matching Renderer gradually reduces real FPS using supported AMD utilization readings. Adaptive can add generated frames within its ceiling; Fixed can lower output FPS. Off by default, saved per profile and power mode, and mutually exclusive with Dynamic Cadence Recovery. Brief spikes can still reach 100%, and unavailable telemetry leaves normal pacing active. - **Faster Frame Generation:** The matching Renderer reduces CPU and GPU overhead in Fixed and Adaptive with FP16 or FP32. The chart above compares Quality and Lighter throughput and GPU time with v4.5.0. In-game gains depend on the game, hardware and settings. - **More efficient FP16 Quality:** The matching Renderer automatically uses a leaner compute path for supported native FP16 Quality models on AMD’s RADV driver, preserving model weights, precision and Flow Scale without adding image buffers. It applies to Fixed and Adaptive, bridge and non-bridge, with VRR on or off. Enable **Allow FP16** and leave **Lighter FG Model** and **Ultra Performance** off. Steam Deck and other AMD/RADV handhelds can use this path; their performance gains have not yet been measured. - **Lower overhead for Quality and Lighter:** The matching Renderer spends less CPU time submitting GPU work in Fixed 2× and Adaptive steps that produce one generated frame. This applies automatically with either model, FP16 or FP32, and bridge or non-bridge modes, preserving image quality and Flow Scale. - **Lower FG working-buffer memory:** Generated outputs share temporary image storage, reducing private buffer allocations at higher multipliers. The chart includes unchanged 800p 2× controls and measures FG working buffers rather than total MAKO or game VRAM. - **Less CPU work for Scaling and Shaders:** The matching Renderer reuses scaling preparation, and the bundled shader system reduces temporary allocations during frame presentation. Your scaling method, sharpness, shader effects and effect order are preserved. - **Adaptive and FIFO stability:** The matching Renderer preserves proven Adaptive workloads after brief image-availability misses and retains qualified Smooth Cadence pacing through short cadence dips. Sustained slowdowns and unsuccessful higher-multiplier trials still trigger the existing safeguards. - **More reliable multiplier checks:** Adaptive checks the real-frame cost after pacing settles and refreshes older comparisons when needed. Brief bursts of queued frames no longer repeatedly restart these checks. When both workloads reach the target, MAKO prefers the lower multiplier. - **Better use of frame-cap waits:** Eligible capped Fixed and Adaptive paths coordinate frame preparation with output timing, including supported Scaling and bridge paths, avoiding consecutive pacing waits while preserving your configured cap. - **Gamescope timing compatibility:** The matching Renderer improves bridge feedback handling, VRR timing interpretation and presentation deadlines. Newer Gamescope reports and optional Vulkan timing on non-bridge surfaces are used when supported, with existing pacing retained otherwise. This does not require replacing SteamOS’s Gamescope. - **Customize shaders per game:** Select **Customize shaders** to adjust selected bundled and compatible custom effects with sliders, toggles, choices and colour controls. **Reset shader to defaults** restores the selected effect. - **Live shader adjustments:** Changes save with the selected profile and are shared across its AC and battery modes. They apply live when Shaders was enabled at game launch; rebuilding an effect may cause a brief hitch. The editor opens beside the game, and **Hide controls** collapses it while comparing results. - **Clearer shader controls:** Palettes such as Nostalgia’s **Custom palette** use colour swatches, sliders and exact-value fields. Sliders follow the author’s step size with consistent controller increments. Numeric fields hide floating-point display noise without changing stored values or saving untouched fields. - **Smoother controller navigation:** Focused controls stay visible when entering settings tabs or leaving the effects list. Collapsing the list reveals the next focused action without restoring stale scroll positions. Unavailable actions are skipped, and closing the shader editor returns to the selected MAKO section in Decky’s Quick Access panel. - **Shared MangoHud layouts:** Profiles with MangoHud enabled can use an optional `~/.config/mako-render/mangohud.conf`, shared with the standalone Renderer launcher. Creating or removing it takes effect on the next game launch without resaving profiles. Keep the usual `mako-run %command%` launch option. Requires host-installed MangoHud; Flatpak games and simultaneous Shaders remain unsupported. - **Native FPS above the Adaptive target:** With **Fractional Adaptive** and **Automatic** Real Frame Priority, sustained native FPS can exceed **Target FPS** without generation when **Base FPS Cap** is off or at least the target. Manual caps remain enforced. - **More complete translations:** Performance, HDR, scaling and Remote Play controls have more consistent translated labels and explanations across MAKO Decky and the configuration app. Thanks to [Tak-attack](https://github.com/Tak-attack) for the Japanese improvements in [PR #91](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/91). - **Better support reports:** With diagnostics enabled, MAKO Decky retains ten launch sessions instead of five. Reports preserve Wayland errors and multi-line failure details in Steam’s timestamped logs, identify failed presentation waits and available timing capabilities, and keep MAKO Wiz’s guide links usable from GitHub issue comments. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try V-Sync on and off.** The smoother choice depends on the game, FPS cap, VRR, and compositor. Compare Fixed, Adaptive, and scaling-only modes one at a time. If a feature does not work, try Fullscreen, Borderless Fullscreen, and Windowed. For Scaling, test in-game resolutions and check that Live Status shows Input smaller than Display. - **Adaptive target:** Adaptive aims for an average frame rate; it cannot lower a game’s native rate or exceed available GPU and compositor capacity. - **Quality and latency:** Higher multipliers and lower real-frame rates can increase ghosting and latency. Smooth Cadence may trade responsiveness for steadier motion. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. Frame Generation and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation. The open MAKO Scaler does not use it. MAKO does not alter the user’s DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. > ⚠️ **Required MAKO Renderer update:** Installing the ZIP updates MAKO Decky, but does **not** replace the shared native Renderer. Open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer** afterwards. ## Installation New to Decky or installing MAKO Decky for the first time? See the [full install and use guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO#install-and-use) for Decky Loader setup and prerequisites. 1. Download `MAKO-Decky-v4.6.0.zip` below. 2. On SteamOS, open Decky Loader's settings and enable **Developer Mode**. 3. Choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the downloaded ZIP. 4. In MAKO Decky, select **Install MAKO Renderer**. For native Steam/Proton games, add `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command%` to the game’s Steam launch options. **Third-party launcher setup:** Follow the [quick guides for Heroic, Lutris, EmuDeck, and other Flatpak apps](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md). ## Updating an existing MAKO Decky installation 1. Quit any game currently using `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run`. 2. Uninstall **MAKO Decky**, then download the newer ZIP from [version 4.6.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/plugin-v4.6.0). 3. In Game Mode, open Decky Loader’s settings, choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the newer ZIP. 4. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 5. ⚠️ **Required:** Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer** to install the version bundled in the new ZIP. 6. In **Flatpak Setup**, select **Update** for every prepared application’s matching runtime extension. This replaces its Flatpak layer with the engine bundled in the new ZIP while preserving its preparation and per-game Wrapper commands. Existing profiles and Steam launch options are retained. The shared native Renderer and launcher are re-created in step 5; shared Flatpak extensions are retained, then refreshed in step 6. ## Before you play - Test MAKO per game. Start with Frame Generation and Scaling disabled, then enable one path at a time before combining them. - If you use Frame Generation or LS1 scaling, confirm the detected `Lossless.dll` path before launching. Leaving it blank permits normal discovery. The open MAKO Scaler does not need it. - Do not combine `mako-run` with another frame-generation or scaling Vulkan wrapper for the same game. ## Bundled MAKO Renderer `4.6.0` - Includes checksum-verified `MAKO-Renderer-v4.6.0-linux.tar.xz`. - Corresponding MAKO Decky source: [`plugin-v4.6.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/plugin-v4.6.0). - Corresponding MAKO Renderer source: [`render-v4.6.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/render-v4.6.0), pinned by commit and checksum in the ZIP metadata.

Model warnings explain unavailable native FP16. Restart the game after changing precision. - **Native Steam Remote Play:** Stream on the receiving native x86_64 Linux Steam client using your selected profile and optional AC/battery settings. Create a named copy during a stream; normal live/restart rules apply. Qt and Decky share client restoration and current shader selections. Requires system Python 3.11 or newer; standalone Steam Link, Flatpak Steam and browser streaming are unsupported. Stream quality and latency still need qualification. Thanks to [Hugo Uchôas Borges](https://github.com/hugouchoasborges) for the contribution. - **Disable Steam Overlay (Restart):** New per-profile Performance control, enabled by default. May reduce stutter; disables Steam's in-game overlay and FPS counter and may affect Steam Input. Gaming Mode menus and performance overlay remain available. - **Better profile capture:** Launcher and helper processes cannot stand in for the game or select another game's profile through old aliases. Failed Smooth Cadence reductions keep their retry delay across stalls and menu returns. Higher-multiplier pacing is rechecked against its real-frame cost. Brief native-only recovery samples restore the automatic base cap and generated workload before checking recovery. - **Frame pacing and recovery:** The matching Renderer improves capped Fractional spacing, completion pacing and recovery from retired Gamescope scaling swapchains, while keeping native fallback responsive. Scaling and HDR preserve games’ presentation-wait support while adapting output timing to compositor feedback. - **Shader overhead:** The bundled vkBasalt reduces per-frame CPU work and preserves ReShade effect settings. Effect GPU cost still increases with the Frame Generation multiplier. - **Clearer guides and reports:** Setup, configuration, Remote Play, Flatpak and troubleshooting guides are shorter. Diagnostic instructions now request 5,000 lines; reports retain startup, state and process/GPU health context. - **German interface:** MAKO Decky now follows Steam's German interface language with a complete translated catalog. Thanks to [Hu2ki3](https://github.com/Hu2ki3) for contributing German support to the Renderer configuration app in [PR #77](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/77). - **Russian interface:** MAKO Decky now follows Steam’s Russian language setting. Thanks to [rosakodu](https://github.com/rosakodu) and the Decky Loader Russia community for [PR #83](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/83). - **Japanese translations:** Clearer shader controls, installation messages, and explanations. eugeniosegala/mako.body: > Looking for the standalone Vulkan layer? See [MAKO Renderer v3.3.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/render-v3.3.0). ## What's new in MAKO Decky v3.3.0 ### Release codename: Neptune Fury > _“The realms of ocean and the fields of air are mine, not his.”_ > > **Virgil, _The Aeneid_, Book I, translated by John Dryden** --- - **Independent upscaling:** Scaling no longer enables Gamescope WSI automatically. Supported 64-bit and 32-bit Gamescope games can upscale with WSI off. - **Lower CPU and memory use:** The updated MAKO Renderer reduces CPU overhead and RAM/VRAM use, with improved memory handling during resolution changes. - **Smoother Frame Generation cadence:** Smooth Cadence is on by default and uses validated ordered Gamescope presentation to stabilize delivery. Fractional Adaptive retains real frames, while Fixed and Steady Base Cap can favor an even cadence at the cost of real-frame rate and responsiveness; turn it off per game if preferred. - **A cleaner panel:** Press R1 for a compact view that retains Live Status and warnings. Centered headings, solid deep-blue dividers and preserved controller focus make navigation clearer. - **Clearer model warnings:** See LS1 and LSFG compatibility problems together, with troubleshooting guidance and separate instructions when Lossless Scaling is missing. - **Improved Japanese translations:** Translated scaling and Live Status messages, with consistent control names and updated Adaptive guidance across MAKO Decky and MAKO Renderer. Thanks to [Tak-attack](https://github.com/Tak-attack) for [PR #64](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/pull/64). - **Clearer vkBasalt integration:** Updated controls and documentation cover 64-bit and 32-bit use, with a separate matching installation and links to official effect configuration guidance. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try the game’s V-Sync setting both on and off.** It can make frame delivery feel steadier, but may also add input lag or clash with the game’s FPS cap, VRR, or compositor. Every game is different: compare both options and keep the one that feels smoother and more responsive. Every game, renderer, and display setup behaves differently. Compare Fixed Frame Generation, Adaptive Frame Generation, and scaling-only operation one setting at a time. For most games, fullscreen is the best starting point for performance and frame pacing. Keep the configuration that feels best for that game. - **Adaptive target behaviour:** Adaptive varies the generated-frame count toward an average target. It cannot reduce a native frame rate already above that target, and the result still depends on the selected multiplier plus available GPU and compositor capacity. - **Quality and latency tuning:** Higher multipliers and lower real-frame rates can increase ghosting and input latency. Smooth Cadence may improve motion consistency while reducing responsiveness, so compare the available choices per game. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. Frame Generation and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation. The open MAKO Scaler does not use it. MAKO does not alter the user’s DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. > ⚠️ **Required MAKO Renderer update:** Installing the ZIP updates MAKO Decky, but does **not** replace the shared native Renderer. Open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer** afterwards. ## Installation New to Decky or installing MAKO Decky for the first time? See the [full install and use guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO#install-and-use) for Decky Loader setup and prerequisites. 1. Download `MAKO-Decky-v3.3.0.zip` below. 2. On SteamOS, open Decky Loader's settings and enable **Developer Mode**. 3. Choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the downloaded ZIP. 4. In MAKO Decky, select **Install MAKO Renderer**. For native Steam/Proton games, add `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command%` to the game’s Steam launch options. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Preferred clean update:** To prevent Decky retaining an older backend or bundled payload, uninstall **MAKO Decky**, install the newer ZIP, restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine, then open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer**. This also resolves cases where Decky does not show or reload the plugin after installation. **Third-party launcher setup:** Follow the [quick guides for Heroic, Lutris, EmuDeck, and other Flatpak apps](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md). ## Updating an existing MAKO Decky installation 1. Quit any game currently using `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run`. 2. Uninstall **MAKO Decky**, then download the newer ZIP from [version 3.3.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/plugin-v3.3.0). 3. In Game Mode, open Decky Loader’s settings, choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the newer ZIP. 4. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 5. ⚠️ **Required:** Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer** to install the version bundled in the new ZIP. 6. In **Flatpak Setup**, select **Update** for every prepared application’s matching runtime extension. This replaces its Flatpak layer with the engine bundled in the new ZIP while preserving its preparation and per-game Wrapper commands. Existing profiles and Steam launch options are retained. The shared native Renderer and launcher are re-created in step 5; shared Flatpak extensions are retained, then refreshed in step 6. ## Known limitation - **HDR frame generation and scaling are unavailable in this Decky release:** The engine foundation is included, but the plugin locks HDR exposure off and does not provide a per-game opt-in. In-game HDR controls may be unavailable by design. A later release can unlock the path after activation, presentation, colour, and performance are validated across games. ## Before you play - Test MAKO per game. Start with Frame Generation and Scaling disabled, then enable one path at a time before combining them. - If you use Frame Generation or LS1 scaling, confirm the detected `Lossless.dll` path before launching. Leaving it blank permits normal discovery. The open MAKO Scaler does not need it. - Do not combine `mako-run` with another frame-generation or scaling Vulkan wrapper for the same game. ## Bundled MAKO Renderer `3.3.0` - Includes checksum-verified `MAKO-Renderer-v3.3.0-linux.tar.xz`. - Corresponding MAKO Decky source: [`plugin-v3.3.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/plugin-v3.3.0). - Corresponding MAKO Renderer source: [`render-v3.3.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/render-v3.3.0), pinned by commit and checksum in the ZIP metadata.

xxjsonderuloxx/decky-lsfg-vk.name: v0.14.1 The LSFG-VK 2.0.0 Update
xxjsonderuloxx/decky-lsfg-vk.body: This release is a ground-up rewrite of Decky LSFG-VK, focused on better alignment and integration with [LSFG-VK 2.0.0](https://lsfg-vk.dev/). > This release changes how per-game profiles are created and managed. Existing v1 profiles are not compatible with this release and will need to be recreated. **New Layout and Automatic Organization** - Separate tabs for Steam Games, Non-Steam Games, Flatpaks, Settings, Config File (optional debug) - Collapsible lists that automatically organize by LSFG-VK enabled games and not-yet enabled - No more copy-pasting launch commands for each game! - Enabling a Steam or Non-Steam game will automatically configures its steam launch options while preserving existing launch arguments. - Streamlined flatpack integration and cleanup, does not require any manual launcher pastes in `target` section. - Enable All and Remove All actions for each category - Steam Deck "Game Mode" specific workarounds section better organized and managed in conjunction with LSFG-VK 2.0.0 config on a per application basis automatically. - LSFG-VK per-app config properly implemented by Steam AppIDs for automatic per-profile management. **Reworked Profiles** - Reworked Flatpak support with per-app profiles and improved application detection - Steam and Non-Steam games are automatically patched and unpatched as profiles are enabled or removed - Added detection and repair of broken/missing wrapper configuration **Now Playing Tab** - Added a Now Playing view that automatically follows the currently running game - When an enrolled game is detected to be running, automatically open a Now Playing tab, with only the applicable controls that apply in real time while game is running (FPS Multiplier, Performance Mode, Flow Scale etc) - When a non Steam shortcut such as an EmuDeck ROM or Heroic launcher game is running through an LSFG-VK-enabled Flatpak, the Now Playing tab automatically identifies the underlying Flatpak and exposes its real-time frame gen controls. **Misc** - Simplified LSFG-VK installation, configuration, and cleanup - Automatic conflict resolution with previously patched games - Higher multiplier options for Steam OS devices with higher HZ rates (ex 40 native FPS * 6x to saturate a 240hz monitor) - Moved FP16 acceleration to global option in settings tab, to more correctly follow lsfg-vk config conventions. - Better uninstallation cleanup discipline in-plugin and through Decky uninstall. > it is still recommended to first "Uninstall LSFG-VK" from plugin settings, then uninstall from Decky settings, in order to properly unpatch steam launch options before removing plugin overall **This is a major change from previous iterations of the plugin. Big reports and feedback on the new layout are greatly appreciated in Github Issues or the plugin Discord**

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.7.6
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body: # UNIFIDECK v0.7.6 **Added itch.io** as a new store, game de-dupe across stores, and a way to highlight games that you already own on other stores (happy autumn sale!) ## New Features - **Added itch.io.** Sign in through the usual login window to install linux and windows games. You can also play HTML5 games via browser. If you want add Free games to your library, add them to a collection and they will show up after sync. - **Added** an "owned elsewhere" banner to Steam Store pages in Gaming Mode. It lists the other stores where you already own the game, and you can turn it off in the Quick Access Menu. - **Changed** Xbox sign-in to Microsoft's code-based sign-in to allow for broader entitlements, so the Steam Store banner can also show the Xbox games you own. - **Added** a "Group duplicates" option that shows a single tile for a game you own on several stores. Thanks @kmturley - **Added** Battle.net free-to-play and subscription games, such as World of Warcraft, Hearthstone and Heroes of the Storm, to your library. - **UI Update** The Quick Access Menu now uses Decky UI elements, with scrolling labels for long names. Thanks @kmturley ## Major Issues Fixed - **Fixed** Steam crashing when a game's details page opened before Steam had finished loading it. - **Fixed** the Stop button not closing some games properly. - **Fixed** Warcraft III: Reforged sign-in failing with a "check your VPN" error. - **Fixed** other plugins and themes, such as Grey Uninstalled games (CSS Loader), TabMaster's Installed filter, etc seeing every Unifideck game as installed. Thanks @HoLuLuLu - **Fixed** library tabs still showing for stores you had signed out of. - **Fixed** games failing to launch when an incomplete GE-Proton was already on disk. Unifideck now downloads a fresh copy instead of reusing it. **Notes** - After this update, your Microsoft account will be logged out and you will need to login again with the new method. - For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue. Special thanks to @kmturley and @HoLuLuLu for their contributions to this release, and to everyone on Discord who helped with beta testing. Couldn't have done it without you! Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)!

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.7.5
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body: ### **UNIFIDECK v0.7.5** **Added GameVault** support, for installing and running DRM-Free games via Unifideck. ## New Features - **Added GameVault**, so you can browse and install from your own GameVault server or from local folder of game files (Thanks @stm85). See guide here - [Unifideck-GameVault-Setup.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32020645/Unifideck-GameVault-Setup.pdf) - **Added** support for GE-Proton installed outside Unifideck, such as through ProtonPlus. Unifideck can now use existing protons instead of downloading them again. Thanks @EricwanAR - **Added** a way to open logged in stores from the plugin UI. You can use the Cart icon to open the store's landing page/launcher. - **Improved** the plugin updater. UI is more compact now and update options open in a new popup. - **Added** a visible badge when Unifideck has stopped retrying a game that keeps failing to launch, with a button to reset it and try again. - **Added** better support for Steam Machine and its own tab and compatibility classifications. ## Major Issues Fixed - **Fixed** games launching behind Steam's loading screen instead of coming to the front. - **Fixed** games starting without keyboard or controller focus in Gaming Mode. Thanks @stm85 - **Fixed** being signed out of your stores after switching Proton version. - **Fixed** a Ubisoft game launching the wrong title when two games shared an ID. - **Fixed** Ubisoft sign-in being lost when you played a different Ubisoft game. - **Fixed** Ubisoft installs reporting themselves finished before the download was done. - **Fixed** wrong artwork appearing on sequels and other same-series titles. - **Fixed** Battle.net sign-in failing in certain scenarios. - **Fixed** GOG game setup inheriting CheatDeck settings and hanging. Thanks @matheussilva421 - **Fixed** a finished install being marked cancelled, so the game never appeared in your library. - **Fixed** the Play button still offering Install for a game that had just finished installing. - **Fixed** a download row that could not be cancelled and never cleared. - **Fixed** cancelling a download leaving work running in the background. - **Fixed** an interrupted GE-Proton download leaving a broken copy behind. - **Fixed** selected Proton version not taking effect in some cases. Thanks @stm85 - **Fixed** manually added non-Steam shortcuts being removed by a library sync. - **Fixed** launch options support. - **Fixed** the Update button on the Downloads page showing no highlight on controller focus. Thanks @FreudsCAT - **Improved** sync so it skips work it already did and repairs metadata left behind by an interrupted run. **Notes** - If the plugin update installation gets stuck, please uninstall the plugin and install the attached installation file manually. - Restart Steam after a sync or cleanup so the library refreshes fully. - The bundled GOG CLI was updated, which seems to have fixed stalling GOG downloads. - Capture Logs now includes a short history of Unifideck's own memory use, which helps us diagnose slowdowns. - For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue. Thanks @HSNEM for the Arabic translations. Special thanks to @moi952, @kevbenjam, @uglierwan, mmmtimmah and everyone on Discord who helped with beta testing, development and documentation. Couldn't have done it without you! Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)!

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.7.4
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body:
# UNIFIDECK v0.7.4


**Added Battle.net** as a fifth store. 


## Major Issues Fixed

- **Fixed** GE-Proton downloads failing.
- **Fixed** prefixes being wiped when your Proton did not actually change.
- **Fixed** game setup failing whenever you had forced a compatibility tool in Steam's own Properties menu.
- **Fixed** Cyberpunk 2077 and other titles that ship their own ICU library crashing during startup.
- **Fixed** external drives losing their identity when reconnected or renamed.
- **Fixed** Ubisoft showing as signed in before sign-in had actually succeeded.
- **Fixed** language options not reaching your games. Thanks @FreudsCAT
- **Added** Steam Machine and SteamOS categories to the library compatibility tab. German and English wording thanks to @kevbenjam
- **Improved** the Traditional Chinese translation. Thanks @frank460699

**Notes**

- For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue.

Thanks also to @matheussilva421 and @kmturley for build and tooling fixes. As always, thanks to our testers and contributors for their efforts <3

Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)!

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.7.3
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body:
## New Features

- **Added** Protontricks detection. Your Unifideck games now appear in Protontricks with the prefix the game runs in. If you use the Flatpak version, Unifideck grants it read access to the prefixes folder so it can see them. This does not mean we will support fixes via Protontricks perpetually. Tinker at your own risk.
- **Added** a language picker when installing Epic games that ship separate language packs.
- **Added** an **Installed** section to the Downloads tab listing every installed game with its size and storage location, each with Play and Uninstall.
- **Removed** finished and cancelled downloads from the Downloads tab history. Only failures are kept now, with a **Clear failed** button, since completed downloads show up in the Installed list instead.
- **Added** a manual **Save location** row to the cloud save window showing where your saves were detected, with **Change location** and **Reset to automatic** for all games instead of just the ones where the plugin couldn't find the save location.
- **Added** a prominent **Cloud saves** indicator on the game page showing Supported, Not supported or Unknown before you install the game.

## Major Issues Fixed

- **Fixed** launching a Ubisoft game re-installing the current prefix.
- **Fixed** the Update button never appearing for any store.
- **Fixed** some Epic games failing to install instantly on every attempt, including Fallout 3 GOTY, Fallout New Vegas, Hogwarts Legacy and Cyberpunk 2077 (language selector fixes this).
- **Fixed** uninstalling an Epic game removing it from your library without freeing any disk space.
- **Fixed** GOG games never receiving their Visual C++ and Unreal Engine runtimes, which made their launchers and games crash or refuse to start.
- **Fixed** Amazon showing as signed out and then failing to sign back in.
- **Fixed** saves being lost when a game's Proton version changed. 
- **Fixed** save locations, cloud save support and descriptions missing for many games, including titles starting with "The", "A" or a number, and titles with trademark symbols or edition names.
- **Fixed** Steam's Stop button and the X in the play row not actually stopping the game.
- **Fixed** the Proton version changing on every launch of an already set up game, which also wiped the Visual C++ registry entries some games need.
- **Fixed** "Space Required" sitting blank for several seconds on most game pages.
- **Fixed** the Quick Access panel jumping back to Settings instead of the tab you were on.
- **Improved** leftover Proton folders that Steam created for Unifideck games are now cleaned up automatically in the background, and only when they can be positively identified as ours. Your own non-Steam games are never touched.

Special thanks to @kevbenjam for the German localization improvements, and to all of our community testers on Discord for the feedback that shaped this release. Couldn't have done it without you!

Special shout out to u/MuglokDecrepitusFx on reddit for a bunch of QoL suggestions.

Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)!

redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is now supported

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is out of "under construction". It was tested on a Legion Go 2 with the 12 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections (QoL & Extras, Henry From Skalitz, and Kingdom Come 2: Refined Experience). Each one was installed through the plugin from a clean game, loaded with no mod errors, and played from a save in Trosky.

Some mods were checked in game, not just loaded: Unlimited Saving II saves with F5, More Carry Weight raises the carry limit, and the Letters From Theresa quest starts on its own.

What the plugin handles for you:

- Mods go into the folder the game loads them from, and mods that update another mod lay over it as they do on Windows.
- LuaDB, the script library some mods need, is installed with any collection that needs it, along with the launch option that loads it under Proton.
- Mods that change game settings are combined into one settings file instead of replacing each other.
- A mod's "required mods" can be installed from its page in one go.

Smaller fixes:

- A collection's installed count now includes its optional mods.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.37
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor is supported, and Shadow of War is on the way

**Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor** \* is now supported, contributed by zomars (#48). Mods that replace the game's own files, loader dlls and `.arch05` archives all install from Gaming Mode:

- Files a mod replaces are backed up first, and come back when the mod is uninstalled or switched off. Two mods replacing the same file never cost you the original.
- Archive mods are registered in the game's archive list on install and taken out again on uninstall or switch-off.
- Mods that load through a proxy dll get the Proton launch option they need set for you, added to whatever launch options you already have.

**Middle-earth: Shadow of War** (on the roadmap, not yet supported) has its groundwork in, also from zomars (#47): the DLL Loader and Packet Loader as Step 1, with the game file the loader overwrites backed up and restored on reset, and the loader's console hidden so the game shows in Gaming Mode.

**ReShade keeps your launch options.** Installing a ReShade preset no longer replaces the game's launch options, and installing ReShade itself now adds its setting to what is already there instead of overwriting it.

\* Community added game. Not tested by author.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.34
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## See more from a mod's author, and mods that come back on their own

**Tap a mod's author to see their other mods** (#46). On a mod page the author's name is now a button: "by Name · more from this author". It opens the store showing all of their mods for that game. To return to every mod, press B, pick "All mods" in the Filter, or use "Show all mods".

**Mods switched off for a missing file come back once it is there** (#36). If a mod was switched off because a file it needs, such as `_ResourcePack.esl`, was not installed, it used to stay off even after the file arrived. Opening My Mods now switches those mods back on as soon as everything they need is on disk. Mods you switched off yourself, or ones switched off for crashing the game, stay off.

**Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, early support (under construction).** The 10 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections install and load on a Legion Go 2, and LuaDB is set up as the game's mod loader. It stays marked "under construction" until mods have been checked in game.

Smaller fixes:

- A missing mod loader is always shown in a collection's to-do list, even if it had been skipped earlier.
- A mod made of a single loose XML patch now says which file you need to apply by hand.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.29
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Kingdom Come: Deliverance is now supported

Kingdom Come: Deliverance is out of "under construction". It was tested on a Legion Go 2 with the 10 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections (Fun And Working 2024, Fun & Working 2022, and Realistic & Immersive Overhaul 2023): each one installed, loaded in the game, and played from a save in town.

Some mods were checked in game, not just loaded: Unlimited Saving adds a working Save Game to the pause menu, Unlimited Weight raises the carry limit, and SimpleHUD hides the HUD.

What the plugin handles for you:

- Mods go into the folder the game loads them from, and the game is stopped from moving that folder aside on its first launch with mods.
- Mods with an installer, and engine mods such as Better Rain, install like any other.
- Mods that change game settings are combined into one settings file instead of replacing each other.
- An engine mod's list of game files is added to the game's own list, so an older mod cannot drop the game's newest patch.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.28
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Search finds every mod again

Reported in issue #43. The plugin remembers mods it has seen fail on your exact game version and keeps them off the store's front page. It was also hiding them from search, so a mod could vanish even when you searched for it by name. On the reporter's Cyberpunk 2077 that was Virtual Atelier and many other popular mods.

Search now finds every mod. The front page still leaves out mods that failed on your game version.

## Switching a mod back on clears its "broken" mark

If the plugin marked a mod as broken and you switched it back on, the mark stayed until the next game update, even through a reset, so a mod you were happily using stayed hidden from the store. Switching a mod back on now clears the mark. If the mod really is broken, the plugin will notice again the next time you play.

## Problem reports say what kind of trouble

"Report a problem" now says how many marked mods are broken and how many just need an update, rather than one number for both.

* Added several checks to help avoid future Decky errors, ensuring data is validated in case API servers change their data structure.

michpalm/game-glance.body:
Built on 3.5.0, with more control over artwork and Home content, a larger default layout, and smoother game-page transitions.

- **Hero art: Fill or Fit.** Fill covers the screen. Fit shows the whole art at the top over a blurred copy, on Home and both game-page layouts, including the opening transition. Steam's extra blurred placeholder is hidden after loading so it does not change the Fit backdrop on the game page.
- **Stable store and Family Sharing pills while browsing.** Known store labels, family-copy counts and store-version groups are available immediately on selection, with local metadata warmed ahead of browsing. Ownership still refreshes when Steam's library changes. Opening a game uses one moving pill pair with the native page's layout, avoiding overlapping fades and a family-pill position jump.
- **Optional gray treatment for uninstalled games.** Keep the current gray appearance, or turn it off to show uninstalled Home cards in color across Steam, Spotlight and Minimal rows.
- **Choose Home feed tabs.** Turn What's new, Friends and Recommended on or off individually. Disabled tabs load no content; turning all off removes the feed. Returning from a game selects an available tab, with focus restored after Quick Access closes.
- **Larger default layout.** Home, game pages, status bar, opening transition and screensaver use a fixed larger default, with adjustments for different screen shapes. This supersedes the earlier experiment that followed Steam's display scale.
- **Smoother Home-to-game transitions.** Clean and normal information cards share the settled page’s layout and styles. Moving text keeps its proportions, borders stay present during loading, and store/Family Sharing pills use one measured pair through the handoff.
- **Clearer settings.** Game logo and Hero art live together under Appearance because they affect both Home and game pages. The Home settings section is named Home page, and the Game Glance page toggle is shortened to Game Glance. With Spotlight Home off, only its main toggle remains visible in the Home page section.

Retains 3.5.0's version switching, settings preservation, Minimal row, controller battery, cloud badges and installation explanations. EmuAchievements remains deferred.

Validation covers the ROG Xbox Ally at its native 16:9 display, the shared Clean transition across eight emulated viewport shapes, normal-layout openings and Back navigation, store/Family Sharing pill stability, and all three games-row styles with gray treatment enabled and disabled. Viewport emulation is not physical testing on eight monitors or Steam Deck hardware. See the [release-readiness record](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/blob/b668e1902c47bacd1742f20633547e826b324b30/docs/validation/3.6.0-release-readiness.md) for current checks and remaining coverage limits.

## Install

Download `game-glance.zip` below. In Decky, enable Developer mode, then choose Settings → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP. Existing users can use Game Glance’s Updates section after this release is published.

# Game Glance 3.5.0

A stable return point for future updates, with version switching, a new games-row style and status-bar polish.

- **Choose a version.** Install any published stable release from 3.5.0 onward through Decky's confirmation flow, including returning to an older version. Settings preserve preferences introduced by newer versions when an older version saves them.
- **Minimal games row.** All game cards stay at the small portrait size, with Steam-style scrolling. Steam and Spotlight remain available.
- **Bluetooth controller battery.** Supported connected controllers show their reported battery percentage in the status bar, separately from the handheld battery.
- **Cloud status overhaul.** A white cloud with a small state badge matches between Home and the game page, including the opening transition (#64).
- **Installation explanations.** Steam's unavailable-game messages, such as "Available for Windows", remain visible. On the restyled page they appear next to Last played; the classic layout keeps Steam's message below the main button (#62). Installation and compatibility restrictions remain controlled by Steam.
- **Less unused artwork work.** Minimal skips the wide-card artwork warm-up, and failed artwork copies are released.

EmuAchievements integration remains deferred.

## Validation

Validated on the ROG Xbox Ally, including eight aspect-ratio simulations and a real upgrade/downgrade round trip using local test packages. Steam Deck hardware and the reporter's exact blocked-platform setup remain unverified.

Draft candidate: `3296c540295b1be807b9db21bef881e1d9391e2a`. The ZIP is the same build installed and verified on the Ally.

# Game Glance 3.4.2 (pre-release)

A test build for people who use **HLTB for Deck**. It's 3.4.1 plus the fix below. The built-in updater ignores it:
install it from the zip on this release page (Decky → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP). Once it's confirmed, the
updater offers it as usual.

- **The Play row no longer slides under the cards with HLTB for Deck.** A few seconds after a Steam game's page opened,
  HLTB for Deck added its own row of times above Steam's Play row and pushed it down behind Game Glance's cards. On the
  Game Glance page that row is now hidden: Game Glance's HowLongToBeat card already shows the same times. With the
  Game Glance page turned off, HLTB for Deck's row shows on Steam's page as before.

Tested on a ROG Xbox Ally with HLTB for Deck 2.0.12. Thanks to dadzios for the report and the video (#67).

# Game Glance 3.4.1

Choose which copy of a game to play, and fixes for the games row, the way into a game's page and play time on Home. Update from Quick Access → Game Glance → Updates.

- **Your recent games in the order Steam's Home shows them.** This is for the Games row set to recent games; a row showing a collection is unchanged. Games you played or installed on this device come first. Games you played only on another PC or handheld follow later in the row (from the 16th place), as on Steam's Home. A game you played here that Steam's servers have not seen yet shows its last played time instead of "Added".
- **Changed your mind? Press B.** Right after you pick a game, B now takes you straight back to Home with Steam's back sound and the same fade as coming back from a game page, and A works again at once. Once the game page is up, Steam handles B as always.
- **Play time you can trust on Home.** Home's play time now always matches the game page. It could show far more than you played (Red Dead Redemption 2: 223 hours on Home, 38 on the game page). Games you added to Steam from Lutris now show Lutris's own count, which includes play you started from Lutris.
- **No missed first press.** After coming back from a game page with B, the first Left or Right press always moves the selection.
- **No flicker at the top when opening a game.** With Game Glance's status bar turned off, or with the Game Glance page turned off (so games open on Steam's own page), Steam's top bar now stays on screen through the opening animation instead of disappearing and coming back.
- **A clearer setting.** The Games row style setting now says what Steam and Spotlight do. If your row started to move differently after 3.3.0: `Prefer the selected game wide at the left? Quick Access → Game Glance → Spotlight Home → Games row style → Spotlight.`
- **One sound for Play.** Starting a game with Home's Play button now plays only Steam's launch sound, not also the sound for opening the game's page.
- **News opens on its own.** A news card in What's new now opens just the article, which you can scroll, instead of the game's page with the article on top. B takes you back to Home.
- **Choose which copy to play.** When you and a family member both own a game, its family pill shows a **+**: press it on Home or the game page to open Steam's own choice of which copy to play. A game you own on more than one store through Unifideck gets a store pill that opens Unifideck's version choice. (Thanks to ZacharyQin for brining this up and the first draft.)
- **Steam's compatibility note no longer covers the cards.** The "Valve's testing shows…" row now sits below the Play row, with the same space on every side. (By ZacharyQin.)
- **Smoother controller moves in the Clean look.** Down from Play goes to the next thing you can see, the feedback row is centred on screen, the tabs sit below the header, and focus never lands on a hidden card.

Thanks to ZacharyQin for the copy choice and the compatibility note fix input, and to R3APER_PL and FMLkoifish for the
reports.

# Game Glance 3.4.0

Touch and mouse on Spotlight Home, and touch on the game page. Update from Quick Access → Game Glance → Updates.

- **Pick and open games by touch.** On a handheld's touchscreen, tap a game in the row to select it and tap it again to
  open its page, with the same transition as A. The Library card and the "back to start" preview take taps too.

- **Swipe the row.** The row follows your finger, one game per card width, and a flick glides on, slowing down smoothly. 
A flick that runs into either end bounces off it, and flicking on from the Library card takes you back to the first game. 
The art and colour catch up once you let go, as when you hold the d-pad. Past either end the row gives a little and 
springs back.
- **The tabs.** Swipe up anywhere on Home for What's new, Friends and Recommended, tap a tab to switch, swipe a row
  sideways, and swipe down to go back to your games.
- **The game page's cards** (Spotlight look): tap the info card for Steam's Game Info tab, or the HowLongToBeat card for
  the game's page on howlongtobeat.com. With the controller, press Down from the Play row to select the cards and A to
  open them (#24).
- **The controller is unchanged,** and it carries on from wherever your finger left off.

- **A mouse works too** (docked, or a mouse on a handheld): click a game to select it and again to open it, drag as
  with a finger, and scroll the wheel to move through the games, one card a notch (with the tabs up, the row under the
  cursor). Whatever you can click lights up with a faint ring under the cursor, on Home and on the game page: the
  games, the buttons, the tabs and the game page's cards. The wheel stops at the ends. A small arrow above the games
  (shown only while you use the mouse) opens What's new and the other tabs, and brings you back up.

- **HowLongToBeat "no match" shows at once.** A game without a match no longer searches again on every visit after a
  day: the result is kept and checked again in the background, and if HowLongToBeat has added the game since, its times
  show the next time you open the game's page.

- **A smoother way into a game's page.** The open transition's glass moves already blurred and lands exactly on the
  page's cards, with no last-moment shift of the card edges or their rings; the page's rings are now as fine as
  Home's. The moving text is drawn at the page's own size, so it no longer stretches or pops as the page takes over,
  and it settles exactly where the page puts it on any screen, docked to a TV and on ultrawide screens too. Games from
  Unifideck open as seamlessly as Steam games: the Play label, the cloud button's ring and the Uninstall button land as
  the page draws them. A game without a HowLongToBeat match opens with its card already filled. Coming back with B,
  Home's buttons and cards stay blurred as they fade in.

- **Play time for non-Steam games** (#52). Games you added to Steam yourself, such as emulators and launchers, show
  the play time Steam keeps for them, on Home, the game page and the screensaver, instead of 0 h.
- **Dates you can't misread** (#57). Last played and Added dates older than a week name the month ("Sep 18"), in your
  Steam language's own order, with the year when it isn't this one.
- **A lighter pre-load** (#48). The automatic pre-load covers only the Unifideck games you have installed, not your
  whole GOG, Epic and Battle.net libraries; a run where everything is already saved takes seconds instead of minutes;
  and it waits while a game is running.

Touch and mouse navigation closes #26; more mouse polish for the desktop comes later.

# Changelog

## 1.7.0
- The panel shows a preview of the selected popup template under the template picker, an animated loop of the whole popup, drawn by the popup renderer itself (the slide in from the screen edge is not part of it). *Preview as* picks common, uncommon, rare or ultra rare. The Test buttons stay.
- New template: PS3 Trophy (top right, glossy dark bar, trophy picture, grade-coloured cup).
- New option: screenshot on unlock (off by default), with *Include the popup* and a *Test screenshot* button. Saved to `Pictures/Finally Achievements/Screenshots`.
- The popup's environment settings now come from one function shared by the popup and the preview.
- The panel title is one line, so it no longer covers the *Show* dropdown.

otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.name: v1.6.3
otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.body:
## Near-instant popups and TV placement

Popups now appear about a second after an achievement is earned, instead of 10-15 seconds later.

### What changed since v1.6.2
- **Popups no longer wait on slow downloads.** The icon, unlock percentage, description and game art now load at the same time, and the popup waits for them at most 1 second. Anything slower is left out of that popup and saved for the next one. Before, each was waited for in turn with multi-second network timeouts, plus a gray-icon check and retries.
- **Unlocks are read the moment Steam writes them.** A change to Steam's `UserGameStats` file is read as soon as Linux reports it, instead of waiting for Steam's library data, which lags. The backup check now runs every 0.25 seconds instead of every second.
- **Downloads happen ahead of time.** When a game starts, its unlock percentages, game icon and art, and the icons of achievements still locked are downloaded and checked. An unlock's popup then reads them from disk.
- **Cheaper gray-icon check.** It runs in one helper that stays running instead of starting a new Python process per icon, and each icon's answer is saved.
- **Faster when a display fails.** A display setup the popup couldn't open on is skipped for 10 minutes instead of being tried first on every popup.
- **MangoApp is stopped earlier.** It now stops while the unlock sound's lead-in plays instead of after it.
- **TV placement fix.** With the popup screen size on "auto", popups use the screen size Steam's own interface reports, so they land in the right place on a TV.

otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.name: v1.6.2
otisabiburada/finally-decky-achievements.body:
A tester on a Steam Machine reported popups only appearing after pressing the Steam button, or 1–2 minutes late, and then with just a title.
The plugin now reads Steam’s own stats file directly, so an unlock should show up about a second after Steam writes it.
Names and descriptions now come from Steam’s local schema first. It has every language and includes secret achievements, so descriptions don’t go missing.
Nothing is shown twice if another detection path catches the unlock first.
Unlock history: a list of recent unlocks with the game, rarity and time. It starts from the day you install 1.6.0 and keeps the last 500. There are “Show more” and “Clear history” buttons.
Share card: select an unlock to make a 1200×630 image with the icon, name, description, rarity, game and date. It’s saved to Pictures/Finally Achievements and previewed in the panel. The plugin doesn’t post anywhere. You open or copy the file yourself.
Session summary: when you close a game, one popup such as “3 unlocked, 1 rare”. It only appears if you unlocked something.
Almost there alert: a popup such as “Only 2 achievements left”. You set the count from 1 to 5, and it fires once per count. It skips finished games and games with very few achievements.

Languages: English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Simplified Chinese and Polish.

kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard.name: PS5 Dashboard 1.10.0
kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard.body:
![PS5 Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/main/docs/screenshots/home.jpg)

## What's new in 1.10.0

### 🌍 The plugin speaks your language
PS5 Dashboard now follows the language you picked in Steam on each device, in **14 languages**:

English · Português · Español · Français · Deutsch · Italiano · Polski · Русский · Українська · Türkçe · 日本語 · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文

- Any other Steam language gets **English**, never the operating system's language.
- Plurals follow each language's rules ("2 дня" / "5 дней", "2 miesiące" / "5 miesięcy"…).
- Translations live in [`src/locales/`](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/tree/main/src/locales), one file per language. Spotted something off in your language? Issues and pull requests are welcome!

### 🟦 Rounded corners actually work now
Steam registers a CSS property called `--r` as an angle, and the plugin used that same name for its corner radius, so Steam threw the value away and every tile, card and button came out square. The **Tile corner radius** setting (0–24 px) now rounds the game covers on the home row, the lower rows, the Game Library, the info cards and the buttons.

### ✨ The glass aura follows the corners
The animated edge around the focused game curves with the tile, and its light now shades through grey and the accent blue as well as white and translucent black.

Also includes everything from **1.9.0** (Hide bottom bar setting, header spacing). See the [changelog](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install

1. Download **`ps5-dashboard.zip`** below.
2. In Game Mode: **Quick Access (`…`) → Decky → ⚙ Settings → General**, turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install plugin from ZIP**, pick `ps5-dashboard.zip`.

Updating? Install the new ZIP the same way; your settings are kept. The plugin panel should then show **v1.10.0** at the bottom. If it still shows an older version, restart Steam.

[![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20a%20Coffee-support-FFDD00?logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/kromossomoc)

- **Your time** card: non-Steam games show when you last played them instead of "Not played yet".

### Fixed
- **Tile corner radius really works now.** Steam registers its own CSS variable called `--r` as an angle, so the plugin's `--r: 25px` was thrown away and every corner came out at 0. The plugin's variables are now `--xbd-r`, `--xbd-a` and `--xbd-f`. Checked in Big Picture: 25 px in the settings gives 25 px tiles.

### Changed
- **Power menu looks like the Xbox power options**: one solid dark panel with an accent stripe on top, a bold title above it, roomy rows instead of separate pills, and the selected row filled with the accent color and a white ring.

## Install
1. Download **xbox-dashboard.zip** below.
2. On the Deck: Quick Access (`…`) → **Decky** → ⚙️ → **General** → turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP** and pick the file.

Requires [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader) 3.x.

cyruzin/loadout.name: Loadout v0.6.0
cyruzin/loadout.body:
- Remove Loadout's FPS cap: Steam's QAM frame limit works for every
  game. Profiles show the target they're made for ("Made for 40 FPS at
  1280x720"). A cap block from 0.5.0 or older is removed on the next
  apply. Launch options stay for per-game env and args.
- Remove the Uncapped profile (without the cap it was Performance again).
  Profiles: Quality, Balanced, Performance, plus Default.
- Profile list shows only the profiles the device's (or borrowed) block
  has; applying one it doesn't have is refused (games.profile_spec).
- ELDEN RING: Quality only (40 FPS costs too much image quality).
- Baldur's Gate 3 (native Linux): Quality only, FSR 2.2 Quality, mostly
  Low with Medium textures, VSync and the game's frame cap off.
- lsxcfg: Larian .lsx read/set by MapKey, byte-preserving. Absent key =
  the game's default: null removes the entry, a missing int32 is added,
  and Default undoes both.
- {xdg_data} path root (~/.local/share, Steam's folder refused) for
  native games' settings.
- Device detected at load, generic if unknown: no Setup screen. Reset
  Loadout clears settings and stays on the main screen.
- Recommended resolution per profile (shown, never written).
- Confirm modal leads with a plain summary; full diff under Show details.
- Games without an entry are no longer listed, except while a profile
  from an older version is applied ("(no settings)").
- Docs: README, GAMES, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cyruzin/loadout/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0
