# CE Decky 0.9.32

Lets more non-Steam games, and games on a Proton your Linux distribution installed, start Cheat Engine.

## Fixes

- Some non-Steam games running under Proton could not start Cheat Engine: **Advanced** said "Proton not observed" and **Load table & start CE** said the game was not running.
- A game running under a Proton your Linux distribution installed, such as `proton-cachyos` on CachyOS, can start Cheat Engine instead of failing with "no installed Proton tool matches".
- Cheat Engine stops by itself shortly after the game closes. It could stay attached, with the game still shown as running and **Change** unavailable, until you pressed **Stop CE**.

## Install

Close any running game, then update from the CE Decky panel. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 that needs 0.9.30 or later installed: an older version cannot reach the network there, so turn on **Developer mode** in Decky and install `CE-Decky-v0.9.32.zip` from the file. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.31...v0.9.32

gooorooox/ce-decky.name: v0.9.31
gooorooox/ce-decky.body:
# CE Decky 0.9.31

Fixes cases, in some tables, where a cheat stayed on or came back after you switched it off, or where **Load last table & cheats** failed; Auto-load also gives a game time to load before it starts.

## Fixes

- In tables that keep a script's own switches outside it, switching that script on no longer leaves them on without saying so, from the panel, in **Configure cheats** or at Auto-load.
- **Disable all** also puts back a cheat that showed off but was still active in the game, and a cheat it switched off no longer comes back at the next Auto-load.
- **Load last table & cheats** no longer fails because of a value set for a cheat that was off, or a setting inside a script that stays off.
- A script cheat with settings, such as jump or health, stays on while you switch other cheats; switching a script off switches off everything under it.
- A cheat inside a script that has not run yet can be switched on, in **Configure cheats** and from a pinned cheat.
- A table is no longer said to be written for a different build of the game when the game closed or every pattern it looks for is there, and a working table gets its green check.
- No more "Cheat Engine could not be launched" after a game exits or crashes with Cheat Engine attached.

## Changed

- **Load last table & cheats** waits until the game has been running for 10 seconds, and counts the wait down, so a table is not marked as not working because the game was still loading.
- **Configure cheats** opens with every cheat collapsed, and lists under **Scripts** only the scripts that hold other scripts.

## Install

Close any running game, then update from the CE Decky panel. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 that needs 0.9.30 installed: an older version cannot reach the network there, so turn on **Developer mode** in Decky and install `CE-Decky-v0.9.31.zip` from the file. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.30...v0.9.31

gooorooox/ce-decky.name: v0.9.30
gooorooox/ce-decky.body:
# CE Decky 0.9.30

Decky Loader 3.3.0 broke CE Decky's network access. It moved Decky's built-in Python from 3.11 to 3.14 and left out a standard module, `pathlib.types`, that CE Decky's networking library needs. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 Search finds 0 tables in every source, no table can be downloaded, and CE Decky cannot check for or install updates. This release supplies that module. If you are on Decky Loader 3.2.8, you were not affected.

## Fixes

- Search, downloads and CE Decky's own updates work again on Decky Loader 3.3.0.
- On Decky Loader 3.3.0, a table library, session or running Cheat Engine that CE Decky cannot read is reported as unreadable, instead of looking empty or stopped.

## Install

On Decky Loader 3.3.0 an installed 0.9.29 or older cannot reach the network, so it will not offer this update. Turn on **Developer mode** in Decky, install `CE-Decky-v0.9.30.zip` from the file, then open the Quick Access Menu. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept.

On Decky Loader 3.2.8 an installed 0.9.28 or newer can install this from the panel itself; close any running game first.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.29...v0.9.30

## New

- Review tells you when a table looks for code that is not in your copy of the game, and which pattern it is, so a table that would load and then do nothing is something you find out before you agree to it. It is checked only where CE Decky already knows which program the game runs, and a table that looks inside one of the game's other files is checked there too.
- Review also tells you when a pattern matches more than one place in your copy of the game. Cheat Engine picks any one of them, so a cheat built on that pattern can end up changing the wrong code - on a table that otherwise looks perfectly fine.
- Review tells you when a table is signed, and that Cheat Engine refuses those here, before you start a game to find out. One press makes a copy without the signature and opens it for review, so you agree to the bytes that actually get loaded; rows carrying a signature are marked, and a copy CE Decky made says which table it came from.
- That same press also takes out the code that needs a pattern your copy of the game does not have, and a table with both problems is fixed in one copy rather than two. The copy's review says what was removed and whether any cheat went with it. If a table you already agreed to turns out not to work, the question about it now offers to try a repaired copy before offering to stop using it, and says so plainly when no repaired copy can be made.

## Changes

- CE Decky updates itself only while no game is running. It still tells you about an update during a game, but pressing Update then asks you to close the game first. An update that finishes downloading after you started a game waits for it to close before installing.
- A cheat that is simply on or off is a switch now, with no value to choose and no field to fill: for one real table that is 24 switches in place of 48 controls. Switching one off writes its off value, so the cheat really stops. A cheat that does choose between things shows its list alone, with a box for a value the author did not list one press away.
- Panel messages start with what was found rather than with what CE Decky was doing, so the reason is the part you can read without opening the row.

## Fixes

- Stopping Cheat Engine leaves the game as it was found. Cheats are switched off first, so a game no longer keeps running with the changes a stopped Cheat Engine made and could no longer undo. If one will not switch off, CE Decky says which, and Home asks you to restart the game before a table is started in it again, with **Clear** for when you already have.
- Stopping Cheat Engine with Auto-load on no longer starts it straight back. Auto-load stays switched on and waits for the next run of the game; starting a table yourself, or switching Auto-load on again, starts it sooner.
- Switching Auto-load on while the game is running starts the table right away, rather than only after the panel was closed and opened again.
- Switching on one cheat no longer brings the rest of the table with it. A table's script can declare most of its own flags as on, so one cheat could quietly mean damage multipliers and movement speed as well; now those are switched back off, and Review says up front how much the table turns on by itself. A flag whose code could not be proven to survive being switched off is left on rather than risk the game, and the panel names it so you can switch it off yourself.
- A game whose executable is very large declares its version again, so its tables can reach the green compatibility mark instead of staying on the grey one. A table already proven here keeps its current mark until a cheat from it works once more.

## Install

Turn on **Developer mode** in Decky, install `CE-Decky-v0.9.29.zip` from the file, then open the Quick Access Menu. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept.

An installed 0.9.28 or newer can install this from the panel itself; close any running game first.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.28...v0.9.29

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.5.1
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
## GabeCubeAura 1.5.1

A corrective update for coexistence with Eli Hodapp's Pixel Faceplate plugin. The Faceplate features introduced in 1.5.0 remain unchanged.

### Fixed

- Keep the cooperative Faceplate claim synchronized after setup, configuration imports, resets and support changes, including saved changes whose command is cancelled or reports a later error.
- Publish the claim before engine startup, clean up after partial startup failures, and prevent late callbacks from claiming the display after unload.
- Make the nonsecret claim readable by Pixel Faceplate's unprivileged backend under restrictive file-creation permissions, without broadening private configuration or credential permissions.
- Use atomic claim replacement and serialize updates between cooperating GCA backend processes so an old backend cannot remove its replacement's claim during restart.
- Retain the claim while the display is powered off or suspended. Disabling Faceplate support releases the reservation; access to the serial port remains protected by its exclusive kernel lock.
- Refresh the bundled integration integrity receipts to match the corrected source.

These changes build on Eli Hodapp's cooperative handoff contribution in [PR #5](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/pull/5), integrated through [PR #11](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/pull/11). His original commit, tests and BSD notices are preserved.

### Installation

Install `GabeCubeAura-v1.5.1.zip` through Decky Loader's **Install Plugin from ZIP File**, or use GabeCubeAura's update screen. Keep the ZIP compressed. Existing settings, saved artwork and access keys are preserved. Export your settings before upgrading.

`SHA256SUMS` covers the installable ZIP and the complete corresponding source ZIP.

### Validation and limits

All 37 mandatory coexistence tests passed in a Linux virtual machine, including root/unprivileged-user access, live process checks, exclusive serial locking, crash recovery and 20 consecutive ownership transfers.

Automated coexistence checks use separate Linux processes, virtual serial ports and simulated firmware acknowledgements. Update checks also exercise the updater distributed with 1.5.0 against the new package, with Decky service control and startup health responses simulated. These checks do not constitute validation on a physical JSAUX Faceplate, CH340 USB adapter or installed SteamOS/Decky session.

Pixel Faceplate's polling cadence is unchanged. Clock mode can delay handoff until its next scheduled wake-up; a 30-second handoff is not guaranteed.

### Licensing and source

GCA code is GPL-3.0-only. The separately identified original Faceplate graphical assets retain CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms. Third-party contributions keep their existing credits and licenses. Complete corresponding source accompanies this release.

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.5.0
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
## GabeCubeAura 1.5.0

GabeCubeAura 1.5.0 adds the optional JSAUX Faceplate, prepared artwork, Dashboards and Steam Players City, with updated setup, local backups and display controls. See [what's new](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/wiki/Release-1.5.0).

### Added

- A yellow Artwork / Dashboard Artwork guide in the Decky panel when no current creation is ready, with a direct Create artwork button. Older transfer receipts and removed creations no longer hide the guide.

- Logo size in Adjust image, from 50% to 100% in 5% steps, for separately composed logos. Prepare a new preview and apply it; embedded source logos remain part of the image.
- Preparation, USB transfer and settled-result messages in Decky’s JSAUX panel, using the existing status stream.
- Redacted local diagnostic export and optional five-minute capture details, with no automatic report delivery.
- Local creation ZIP export for active saved artwork, including prepared media and portable metadata.
- Initial calibration with no preloaded Home artwork, mandatory setup and final confirmation. Existing libraries and saved settings are preserved on upgrade.

- Local configuration exports include a complete saved-settings reference, with independent Faceplate, ambience and artwork choices and an explicit coverage list.
- Player Count Only shows the exact number to the unit. Every count layout retains the City smile, including timers, with margins where the content fits.

- Configurable Steam Players City bottom rows: Players + controller in the supplied initial calibration, with Player Count Only available as a separate choice; players with P1 and battery percentage/bar, session time, achievements or total playtime; or Without player count with all eight in-game Dashboard rows. Saved choices are preserved. Battery display appears directly under Players + controller and for Dashboard rows containing controllers. Count Only keeps unit precision; combined rows use k from 1,000. Personal and Steam Families timers temporarily take the right-hand information slot, or the full row without players, before the saved choice returns. Row updates keep the last confirmed City scene and do not change the hourly player-count schedule.

- Low planters and a planted bed in Steam Players City, with garden hedges in smaller settlements. Vegetation follows day/night and weather, with snow on upper surfaces. Architecture, traffic, the player count and the 24-second loop retain their existing behaviour.

- Steam Players City support for Whole image and Bottom edge Faceplate extension, excluding the count rail. A disconnected or powered-off Faceplate falls back to current-game Artwork without changing saved routes; Home yields to Steam. Saved extension choices remain visible in Settings and Decky.

- Daytime snow and thunderstorm Faceplate artwork, retaining original night images and animation timing. Snow day removes the implausible yellow night reflection from the path and limits warmth to window cores. The light bar retains the original white snow and lightning, for both day and night. Weather animation and the Faceplate catalogue provide independent Snow and Thunderstorm day/night choices; old settings/imports preserve the existing selection for both periods.
- Live light-bar previews in Settings and the Decky panel, targeting about 20 frames per second through one shared colour stream that pauses when hidden. Weather keeps a single selected-animation preview and displays its Faceplate image only when the device is connected.
- Independent Rain · day and Rain · night choices in Weather settings and the Faceplate catalogue, retaining the existing rain selection for both on upgrade. Previews use the selected period.
- Automatic day/night colours for both Bluewater and Pearl Rain, with matching saturated light-bar rain palettes. The brighter daytime Bluewater rain uses a petrol head and cyan tail for contrast. Global day/night brightness stays independent.

- Support for the optional JSAUX Pixel Matrix Faceplate, with independent
  display routes for Home and games, a power control and automatic power-off
  on sleep or shutdown.
- Faceplate artwork preparation for static and animated images. Browse
  SteamGridDB with a personal API key, crop and adjust a source, preview the
  prepared result, then explicitly assign it to a game for reuse.
- Artwork Dashboard and weather scenes for the Faceplate. Choose separate
  information rows at Home and in game, including controller batteries,
  session duration, available Steam playtime and achievement progress.
- Steam Players City: an animated city based on the running game's concurrent
  Steam player count, local weather and time of day. The displayed count stays
  fixed throughout each loop; scene updates normally run hourly after the
  initial display, with an additional refresh after screensaver activation. Rain falls in diagonal
  trails, with brief impacts on roads, paths, paved areas and visible roofs.
- Optional presentation integrations with Decky Vocal Assistant (DVA) and
  Decky Animated Screensaver (DAS). DVA owns voice activation, recognition and
  speech; DAS owns its screensaver Studio and collections. GCA retains control
  of its light bar and Faceplate.
- Faceplate playback of prepared DAS collections, including autonomous
  multi-GIF collections installed through the companion plugin.
- A settings-only reset alongside the complete local reset, with distinct
  confirmation text for what each action removes.

### Changed

- Enable automatic update checks by default on fresh installation and settings reset, initially every 24 hours; keep a saved opt-out. Downloading and installation remain manual.
- Settings-only reset forgets Faceplate setup and routes while preserving artwork, access keys and local support evidence. Reconnecting an unconfigured panel offers setup again; saved media does not suppress it.
- Remove the former Hi-Fi Crest tuning panel while retaining the audio pattern and existing rendering choices.
- Initial Faceplate brightness is 70%; the panel retains the USB-power notice above 70%. No Home artwork is preloaded. Users can prepare and assign their own static or animated creations.

- Merge Faceplate troubleshooting details into one Faceplate diagnostics panel, with Connection, Display and Transfers sections. Keep useful data, show repeated errors once and use plain wording.

- Use Economy refresh as the single control for five-point battery steps and five-minute Dashboard clocks; off restores exact percentages and one-minute clock updates. Keep transfer statistics concise. Native clock and animation speed are unchanged.

- Remove Previous screensaver collections from Data and the obsolete Compatibility tab. Existing files stay on disk.
- Keep public update installation manual. Remove the automatic-install choice and drop any inherited consent when this build starts.
- Default public update checks to 24 hours. Remove the five- and fifteen-minute choices and move inherited values at those intervals to 24 hours.
- Keep setup actions visible above Steam’s bottom bar while the content scrolls.
- When upgrading an existing GCA installation, offer Faceplate setup in Decky with a yellow message if an unconfigured Faceplate is detected. Keep the light-bar setup unchanged, recognise existing Faceplate choices and remember an explicit Not now choice after confirmation.

- Show progress, confirmation with the exact local file path, and errors when exporting configuration JSON. Remove the Dashboard-tab reminder and high-brightness advisory from the quick Decky panel; retain them in Settings.

- Bluewater restores its original light-bar rain loop in day and night, removing the later violet contacts. Faceplate day/night images and Pearl Rain palettes are retained.

- Lower the scalloped precipitation umbrella by one native pixel, keeping its shape and colour.

- Next-hour forecast rows use a scalloped umbrella for precipitation probability, separately from the weather-condition icon.
- Steam Players City: Player Count Only uses US thousands separators, for example 48,213. Combined rows keep their compact k notation.

- Faceplate Home and in-game menus share the same background order. Choose Artwork or Weather with or without Dashboard in Display; configure the common information in Dashboard.

- Add six lightning events per 24-second Storm loop in Steam Players City,
  with changing positions behind the skyline and an unchanged count row.

- Reorganise the quick panel and full settings around native Decky controls.
  Keep common light-bar, ambience, game-display and connected-Faceplate
  actions within reach, with detailed controls in their relevant sections.
- Show Faceplate controls while the device is connected and preserve saved
  choices when it is disconnected. Quick selectors and Settings share the
  same supported Home and in-game display choices.
- Keep Faceplate brightness manual and independent from light-bar brightness.
  Changes apply to the current picture without uploading its GIF again.
  A USB-power notice appears above 70%.
- Make Faceplate Off a power action that preserves both saved display routes.
- Start a fresh guided setup from the supplied calibration at 15/255 light-bar brightness, with evening dimming off and an optional 75% night
  level. Preserve resumed setup choices and completed-user preferences.
- Keep setup previews temporary until confirmation, and show a green
  SteamGridDB connection check only after validation succeeds.
- Keep guided setup first and the quick controls unavailable until setup is
  confirmed. Recover unreadable setup progress without trapping the user.

### Fixed

- Restore source exposure for the two daytime cloud-break weather animations and invalidate their prepared caches. Other weather scenes and saved brightness remain unchanged.

- Fix direct Dashboard Weather ↔ Dashboard Artwork switching across provider-local and zoned time representations, including Apply from the weather Dashboard.
- Protect Home/game artwork promotion against concurrent Apply requests. A later status-read failure no longer turns a completed application into a false failure.
- Do not reuse an old transfer receipt to confirm a failed new display choice; describe the failure as an application failure when the choice may already be saved.

- Restore a stable neutral Faceplate scene when the weather city or solar data is unavailable. Defer automatic power-on after host/USB restart until the current scene is confirmed. Preserve saved routes and unknown readings.

- Keep Steam Players City cars rigid as they move, with perspective-based
  changes in size and motion.

- Prevent overlapping settings panes after rapid L1/R1 navigation.
- Use current Dashboard visibility and information choices for preview and
  playback, while preserving independent Home and game preferences.
- Preserve readable controller, session and achievement information at full
  battery and when some Steam statistics are unavailable.
- Improve Screen Sync startup and recovery after an interrupted capture.
- Keep the screensaver visible through a brief interruption in Steam status.
- Keep the previous collection if preparing or installing its replacement fails.
- Distinguish content still being sent from content confirmed by the Faceplate.

### Licensing

- Retain GPL-3.0-only for GCA code, including the Faceplate engine and UI. Identify separately owned original Faceplate images and animations under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; exclude code, technical metadata, third-party media and user imports from that graphical scope. Preserve third-party terms and valid previous grants. See [Licensing and reuse](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/wiki/Licensing).

### Documentation

- Shorten the README and move detailed setup, display, integration and
  troubleshooting instructions into a user guide.
- Add separate device illustrations for light-bar-only and Faceplate examples.
- Clarify that GabeCubeAura is an independent project by Alyenax and is not
  affiliated with Valve or JSAUX.

## Installation

Install `GabeCubeAura-v1.5.0.zip` through Decky’s Install Plugin from ZIP File, or use GabeCubeAura’s update screen. Export your settings before upgrading. Existing libraries and saved settings are preserved. Complete guided setup on a fresh installation; an unconfigured Faceplate has its own setup. No Home artwork is preloaded.

## Licensing and source

GCA code, including the Faceplate engine and UI, is GPL-3.0-only. The 197 positively identified original Faceplate graphical assets use CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Third-party components retain their own notices and terms. Game artwork, user imports and composite documentation GIFs are outside that artwork grant. See [Licensing](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.5.0/LICENSING.md) and the supplied artwork inventory. Complete corresponding source accompanies this release.

The device preview GIFs are software illustrations, not hardware recordings. Software verification does not establish optical playback or controller focus on every SteamOS/device combination.

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.4.0
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
GabeCubeAura 1.4.0 makes the first configuration easier, gives brightness one
clear place in the interface and replaces the fixed-red restriction with real
CPU and GPU thermal protection.

## New features

### Guided first-time setup

- Choose Moderate, Atmosphere, Signals or Immersive in a full-screen Decky
  setup.
- Preview each choice on the physical 17-LED bar before applying it.
- Set Day brightness, optional sunset dimming and the exact city used for
  sunrise and sunset times.
- Review the complete setup before saving it. Existing users keep their saved
  routing and visual settings without seeing onboarding again.

### One global Day/Night brightness control

- Day brightness now applies to every Home and in-game display. Presets and
  routes never overwrite it.
- Optional Night brightness is calculated as a percentage of Day brightness
  and changes automatically at local sunset and sunrise.
- Weather does not need to be selected for automatic night dimming to work.
- Values below 8/255 show a clear warning because they can strongly affect the
  lighting experience.

### Real thermal protection

- At 94°C or higher on either the CPU or GPU, GabeCubeAura stops every
  animation and hardware write, then returns complete light-bar control to
  Valve immediately.
- GabeCubeAura stays disabled until both coherent readings remain below 90°C
  for 30 continuous seconds.
- Missing or incoherent sensor data during an active thermal alert keeps the
  plugin disabled.
- Fixed red is available again for ordinary effects. The protection is based
  on temperature, not colour.

### Weather-first Atmosphere

- Atmosphere now uses Weather as its Home display.
- If no current weather frame is available, it falls back to Slow Prism with
  Screen Sync colours and returns to Weather automatically when data recovers.

## Major fixes

- Remove Follow Steam Brightness, which could not follow Steam's slider while
  GabeCubeAura owned the bar. GabeCubeAura now controls its own brightness and
  restores Steam's exact saved value during a Valve handoff.
- Make brightness transitions and interrupted-write recovery safe without
  overwriting a newer Steam value.
- Keep thermal protection above every preview, permanent display and temporary
  layer.
- Make Signals and Immersive onboarding previews visible without requiring a
  paired controller, live audio, artwork or Gamescope capture.
- Restore Stable updates every 24 hours after first setup and remove any saved
  Private Lab authorization.

## Minor fixes

- Reorder presets so Lights out, Essential and Focus appear first.
- Clarify that Lights out excludes even Valve's download animation while
  Essential still allows confirmed downloads.
- Move Light bar brightness to the end of Display Routing.
- Hide TW3-SteamRGB and StripMine ownership controls behind one optional
  compatibility toggle.
- Report RGB attenuation clearly when the driver does not expose
  `brightness_scale`.

## Installation

Download `GabeCubeAura-v1.4.0.zip` and install it through Decky Loader without
extracting it. `GabeCubeAura.zip` is the identical fixed-name archive used by
the updater and recovery flow. SHA256 values are provided in `SHA256SUMS`.

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.3.2
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
GabeCubeAura 1.3.2 turns Audio Sync into a complete permanent display, adds
one-step lighting presets and gives SteamOS integration clearer, safer control.

## Highlights

- Audio Sync reacts to game and system audio with ten patterns, including
  Hi-Fi Crest, Slow Prism, Spectrum and Stereo Field.
- Home and in-game Audio Sync can use different patterns, palettes and custom
  colours. Artwork and live Screen Sync colours work with every pattern.
- Nine lighting presets switch the complete setup in one action: Lights out,
  Focus, Essential, Moderate, Atmosphere, Signals, Immersive, Immersive+ and
  Festive.
- Artwork colour intensity ranges from greyscale to vivid colour without
  changing brightness or reloading the image.
- The optional SteamOS top-bar indicator shows current weather beside the clock
  with three locally bundled icon styles.
- Consistent output calibration, Blackout and three Steam ownership policies
  provide predictable brightness and safer handoff to native effects.
- Fresh installations use Stable updates, check every 24 hours and contain no
  Private Lab authorization or token.

## Major fixes

- Audio Sync now preserves partial PipeWire reads, processes every complete
  analysis block in order and never renders stale samples.
- Audio and live colour state survive Home/game changes, launch animations and
  capture restarts without blue or fallback-colour flashes.
- Steam download detection no longer treats queued or deferred work as an
  active transfer, and LED manager ownership recovers correctly after Decky
  restarts or rejected requests.
- Screen Sync releases stale capture clients and recovers cleanly across plugin
  replacement, AppID changes and Desktop/Gaming Mode transitions.
- Artwork colour intensity now passes through the real Decky RPC allowlist and
  remains stored instead of returning to 100%.

## Minor fixes

- Improve Hi-Fi Crest timing and optional diagnostics.
- Add Sapphire and Coastline palettes and smoother live-source transitions.
- Make every lighting preset explicit about Audio Sync, controller and Steam
  event routing.
- Reduce only the Clear sky night moon whites while preserving every other
  Weather scene.
- Simplify colour controls, quick-panel copy and advanced diagnostics.

## Installation

Download `GabeCubeAura-v1.3.2.zip` and install it through Decky Loader without
extracting it. `GabeCubeAura.zip` is the identical fixed-name archive used by
the updater and recovery flow. SHA256 values are provided in `SHA256SUMS`.

Software tests cover rendering, routing, capture recovery, updates, ownership
and packaging. Physical diffuser appearance and response latency still depend
on the SteamOS build and target Steam Machine hardware.

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.2.1
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
GabeCubeAura 1.2.1 brings real-time Screen Sync, fixed layouts for up to four
controllers, richer night Weather scenes and safer recovery across Steam,
Gamescope and Decky session changes.

## Highlights

- Screen Sync maps the running game's Gamescope picture across the 17 LEDs in
  Panorama mode, or uses one calmer colour in Ambient mode.
- Steam's screensaver can temporarily use Screen Sync, then the selected Home
  or in-game display returns automatically.
- Failed or PAUSED capture sessions are closed before retry. Gamescope and
  PipeWire rediscovery is rate-limited after Desktop Mode, Gaming Mode,
  suspend and screensaver transitions.
- Controller status supports one to four fixed seats. The Automatic colour
  preset uses battery colours for one controller and distinct player colours
  from two controllers onward.
- Weather adds eight night scenes and Customization+ exposes the four new
  night-cloud patterns.
- Steam activity, downloads, native hardware effects and thermal warnings keep
  priority over plugin output.
- The standalone [TW3 SteamRGB](https://github.com/Alyenax/TW3-SteamRGB)
  companion can replace only the permanent display while its live Witcher HUD
  claim is active. Alerts, Game launches and playtime countdowns stay above it.

The experimental Witcher telemetry Lab is not bundled with GabeCubeAura. It is
distributed separately through TW3 SteamRGB.

## Installation

Download `GabeCubeAura-v1.2.1.zip` and install the archive through Decky Loader
without extracting it. `GabeCubeAura.zip` is the identical fixed-name recovery
archive. SHA256 values are included in `SHA256SUMS`.

Software tests cover rendering, routing, capture recovery, ownership and
packaging. Physical direction, diffuser appearance and reaction latency still
depend on the SteamOS build and target Steam Machine hardware.

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.3.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
## More handhelds, more RGB

Ambideck 1.3.0 adds screen-following RGB implementations for Lenovo Legion Go/Go S/Go 2, MSI Claw, compatible AYANEO/AYN Loki/Zotac Zone kernel LEDs, and selected OneXPlayer/OneXFly/AOKZOE models.

- Colours adapt to the available lighting zones: four corners, left/right colours or one shared colour.
- Devices without a native rainbow use one static colour averaged from the last screen colours, with soft white before the first frame.
- Device detection, reconnect recovery and output rate limits keep lighting writes away from screen capture.
- Quick Access shows the detected device and its lighting capability. HueSync handback remains specific to Ally.

**Hardware validation is still outstanding for the new backends and output worker.** Support depends on the exact model, controller firmware/mode and available kernel interfaces. See [RGB compatibility and exclusions](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck/blob/release/1.3.0/docs/rgb-protocols.md).

Validation: 146 Python tests passed (1 Linux-only test skipped on macOS), 66 frontend tests passed, TypeScript passed and the production bundle was verified.

### Install

In Game Mode, enable Decky Developer mode, then use **Install plugin from ZIP** with `ambideck.zip`. Existing settings are preserved.

Changes: [PR #3](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck/pull/3).

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.2.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
## What's new

- **Makes way for screen recorders.** While a recorder such as [Showreel](https://github.com/michpalm/showreel) holds the capture lock (`/run/decky-screen-capture.lock`), Ambideck lets go of gamescope's screen stream and hands the lights back (to HueSync's setting, or the rainbow). When the recording ends it follows again within about a second. The panel shows **Paused while Showreel records** meanwhile.

  gamescope has one screen stream whose size the first reader sets, so without this a recorder would get Ambideck's tiny frames, or both would share a full-size stream, which can crash gamescope. The README's **Screen recorders** section describes the lock for other recorder authors.

## Fixes

- The lock is checked again right before every connection to the stream, not only every half second, so Ambideck never joins a recorder's stream.
- A recorder that crashed and was never cleaned up (a zombie process) doesn't keep Ambideck paused.

## Install

Press **Update** in Ambideck's Quick Access panel, or download `ambideck.zip` below and use Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**.

Runs on a ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) with Bazzite or SteamOS 3.8.

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.1.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
## What's new

- **Follow outside games.** "Outside games" is now **Off / Normal colour / Follow**. With Follow, the rings follow the Steam interface just like they follow a game, and keep following without a gap when you quit. If you had **Artwork** selected, it becomes Follow. Following outside games keeps the capture running whenever Game Mode is up (about 7 % of one CPU core, roughly 0.2 W).
- **Dark scenes.** Dim scenes are lifted, so dark games show their colour more clearly. A new **Dark scenes** setting chooses what near-black does: **Glow** (a faint glow, as before) or **Off** (that half of the ring switches off and fades back in).
- **Updates from Quick Access.** Ambideck checks GitHub once a day. When a newer release is out, the panel shows **Update to X.Y.Z**; press **Update** and confirm in Decky's dialog. Decky checks the download against the release's SHA-256 and keeps your settings. **Check for updates** asks right away.

## Fixes

- The light controller is found again if it disappears (for example after the driver reloads), with one log line instead of one per frame.
- Steadier screen capture: buffer checks, evenly spaced retries, and a timeout when the stream never starts.
- HueSync is asked to step aside again when a game starts or quits while Ambideck keeps following.
- Turning the lights off outside games now holds against HueSync, like following does.
- Backend calls no longer block Decky while Ambideck connects to the screen stream.

## Install

Download `ambideck.zip` below, then Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**. From 1.1.0 on, future versions can be installed from Ambideck's own Update button.

Runs on a ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) with Bazzite or SteamOS 3.8.

michpalm/ambideck.name: Ambideck 1.0.0
michpalm/ambideck.body:
First release of Ambideck: an Ambilight for the ROG Xbox Ally's stick lights.

While a game runs, each half of each stick ring takes the colour of its corner of the screen. When you stop
playing, the lights go back to your normal setting.

## Features

- **Follows the screen** in any game: four corners (top and bottom half of each ring), or one colour per side.
- **Keeps colours alive:** colourful pixels count more than grey ones, so pastel scenes keep their tint, and
  dark scenes still glow faintly.
- **Hands the lights back** to your [HueSync](https://github.com/honjow/HueSync) setting, or to the
  controller's rainbow if you don't use HueSync.
- **Per game:** switch it off for games where it distracts.
- **Outside games:** off, your normal lights, or the colours of a game page's artwork.
- **Docked:** off by default, with one switch to keep it on.
- **Settings:** brightness, colour boost and speed (Smooth, Balanced, Fast), in Quick Access.

## Install

Ambideck is not in the Decky store.

1. Decky → Settings → General → turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Download `ambideck.zip` below.
3. Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**.

## Tested on

ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) on Bazzite, handheld and docked to a TV. Measured while playing ULTRAKILL: about
+0.18 W on battery and about 7 % of one CPU core.

## Known limitations

- The original ROG Ally and Ally X use the same driver and should work, but their light-zone order is untested.
- HDR games are not tested yet.
- Steam in Bazzite's Game Mode sends no sleep event, so after waking, the colours return within about 2 seconds.

## About

Written with [Claude](https://claude.ai), directed, reviewed and tested on device by the author. Not
affiliated with ASUS, Microsoft, Valve, Philips or any game shown.

jedirhymetrix/decky-bluetooth-order.name: Bluetooth Order v0.1.0
jedirhymetrix/decky-bluetooth-order.body:
## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-11

Initial public release of **Bluetooth Order**.

### Features

- Reorders Steam's existing paired Bluetooth rows in Quick Access and Settings.
- Native order, most recently connected, name A–Z, and name Z–A modes.
- Optional connected-first priority and independently enabled menu overrides.
- Passive, persisted successful-connection history; disconnects retain recency.
- Redacted diagnostics, history reset, and one-button restoration of native order.

### Reliability and distribution

- Scoped mounted-QAM attachment with owned-reference restoration; no root reset
  or automatic service restart.
- Settings adapter recognizes verified shared Decky renderer-patch chains.
- Stale panels disable their controls and explain how to reopen after updating.
- Bounded backend waits, render-loop regressions, isolated QAM session tracking,
  and a hash-checked XML fallback for Decky's frozen Python runtime.
- Immediate observer shutdown skips subscription/retry work when cancellation
  races a completed connection on Python 3.11.
- Complete ESM release ZIP, pinned dependencies, checksums, and CI/release checks.

### Verification and known limits

- User confirmed QAM and Settings working on the tested Deck with Decky 3.2.10.
- Automated frontend, backend, and packaging tests cover sorting, lifecycle,
  observer behavior, archive safety, and release metadata.
- Connection history starts with observed transitions; it cannot reconstruct
  earlier use. Fresh installs default both overrides off.
- Steam UI changes and other plugins' route patches can affect attachment.
  Every TabMaster registration order is not verified.
- Interaction can hold visible ordering. Exact QAM unload restoration can remount
  native rows on a later render. Full boot/resume acceptance remains incomplete.

For installation, privacy, and rollback instructions, see the repository README.

rayekkk/legiongo2companion.body:
### ✨ Added
- **Controller sleep:** under Gyro & touchpad, choose when detached controllers turn themselves off when unused:
  Never, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes, for both controllers, as in Legion Space.
- **Controller sleep:** until you pick one, Companion changes nothing and shows **Controller default**; the choice
  survives updates, and turning the module off leaves the controllers at their current time.
- **Controller sleep:** Companion checks your choice every two minutes and after a wake or reconnect and sets it
  only on a controller that reports another value, so a controller asleep when you chose gets it once it wakes.
- **Controller sleep:** available on the Legion Go 2 and on the Legion Go with the 2025 controller firmware (beta).

### 🔧 Changed

**Display**
- Needs SteamOS 3.9 or newer, which supports the Legion Go 2 screen natively; the page now holds only
  **Fix HDR brightness in games**.
- The HDR fix stays because without it games on SteamOS 3.9 still read a 1499-nit HDR peak instead of
  the panel's real values; on older SteamOS the page asks you to update SteamOS, and the fix works there too.
- After the update, Companion removes its old display script by itself (only the exact script it
  installed); a Gaming Mode that is already running keeps it until it restarts.
- If Setup had kept your own script as a `.backup`, it is put back on SteamOS 3.8 and left alone on
  3.9, where it would override SteamOS.
- The original EDID copy that the HDR fix restores is now kept root-only in
  `/var/lib/legiongo2companion/` instead of Decky's settings folder; the old copy moves there by itself.

### 🐛 Fixed

**TDP**
- With **Allow up to 50 W** the boost limits hold again; since 2.3.0 the firmware's custom mode put its own
  limits (37/45 W on the Legion Go 2) back within half a second while the page showed 50 W.
- Companion now leaves the firmware a moment to settle before it sets the boost limits.

**Vibration**
- While a controller sleeps or stops answering, Companion no longer keeps resending your settings to
  it, which could make it buzz now and then.
- After a wake it retries only the settings that did not take, and its periodic check slows from
  every 30 seconds to every 5 minutes until the controller answers or is reconnected.
- Controllers no longer buzz when Companion starts, is updated or uninstalled, or when a controller
  is attached or detached, unless their vibration mode really has to change.
- Companion reads each setting first and writes only one that differs, never one it cannot read
  reliably.
- A setting is confirmed only when the controller reports it twice in a row, so a delayed reply no
  longer counts as a failed write (many "did not confirm" log entries) or as a confirmed one.

**Controller sleep**
- A setting is confirmed only when the controller reports it twice in a row, so a delayed
  reply no longer counts as a failed or confirmed write.

**Controller firmware**
- Check, Download and Install need both controllers attached and say so: "Attach both
  controllers to check or install firmware updates."
- Install still refuses a controller below 30% battery.

**Battery**
- When the firmware turns on fast charging and battery protection at once, the page now says the
  charging mode cannot be read instead of showing "Invalid argument".
- The page offers **Reset charging mode to Standard**, and your saved protection choice is applied
  again afterwards.

**Lighting**
- The stick lights are set again once when Companion starts and once shortly after a wake, so they no
  longer stay wrong when the controller wakes with stale values.
- The stick lights now work while one controller is detached (they failed with "The joystick-ring
  interface does not belong to the expected controller.").
- The stick lights are set again after a controller is attached or detached.

**Fan**
- Fan Control no longer turns itself off for good when the fan briefly returns to firmware control on its
  own (seen once while a controller was reattached).
- Companion takes the fan back after its usual safety checks, up to 3 times in 10 minutes.
- Fan Control still turns off when anything else writes the fan speed, and a single misread of the fan
  setting no longer counts as such a write.

### 🗑️ Removed
- **Display:** display modes (PQ, Gamma 2.2, Hybrid), Setup, Reset display fix, Brightness slider in HDR and the
  Restart Gaming Mode buttons are gone from the panel, Desktop app and Manage Modules (SteamOS 3.9 does it).
- **Display:** turning Display off no longer asks for a Gaming Mode restart.

### ✨ Added

**Consoles**
- Companion runs as an early beta on the Legion Go and Legion Go S; each console shows only the
  modules and options that apply to it, in the panel, the Desktop app and Manage Modules.
- Battery, the stick lights and Wi-Fi work on all of them (the stick lights on the Legion Go S need
  its `hid-lenovo-go-s` driver in SteamOS).
- Vibration and Gyro & touchpad work on a Legion Go whose controllers have the 2025 firmware.
- Button mapping, Display, Fan Control and controller firmware stay Legion Go 2 only.
- None of this has been tested on these consoles yet; the README Compatibility table shows what is
  supported, beta or not needed.
- On the Legion Go 2 Z2 (83N1), the power-button light, controller firmware updates and Fan Control
  (beta) now work; Fan Control runs its one-time fan check first. Not tested on an 83N1 yet.

**TDP**
- Uses each console's own firmware limits; **Allow up to 50 W** is offered on the Legion Go (higher risk,
  untested there) but not on the Legion Go S, whose firmware already allows more.
- **Separate battery presets** (under **More**, off by default): Silent, Balanced and Performance use the
  lower limits each console's firmware sets on battery and their usual values on the charger, also in game profiles.
- The Legion Go 2 battery limits are Silent 8/8/20 W, Balanced 16/16/30 W, Performance 20/20/35 W; presets
  switch when you plug in or unplug, and Maximum and Custom are unchanged.

**Lighting**
- The power-button switch now appears on the Legion Go and Legion Go S with a Beta note; it stays
  hidden when the BIOS does not describe the light exactly as expected.

**Vibration**
- On the Legion Go S (beta), **Vibration strength** (Off, Low, Medium, High) and **Touchpad
  vibration**, also per game; the page shows what Companion set because the controller cannot report these.
- On the Legion Go S, Companion sends only the settings you change, so Legion Space's values for
  the others are not overwritten.

**Device report**
- **About → Save device report** (the **Logs** page in the Desktop app) writes a read-only text
  file to your Desktop with hardware and firmware details, firmware tables (DSDT) and EC readings.
- It contains no serial numbers, network names or user names; attach it to a
  [Beta report](README.md#reporting-a-problem-on-legion-go--go-s-beta) from a Legion Go, Legion Go S or new model.

### 🔧 Changed

**Updates**
- Updating from 2.2.x resets the gyro source, battery protection, lighting control and Wi-Fi band
  policy once (Decky runs the old uninstall first); set them again, later updates keep them.
- The gyro source, battery protection, lighting control and Wi-Fi band policy now survive an update
  (the band policy is applied once Wi-Fi has reconnected).

**Display**
- An update reinstalls the script for the panel mode you set up and asks for a Gaming Mode restart only
  when the running Gaming Mode does not already use that exact script (always after updating from 2.1.0 or 2.2.x).
- After updating from 2.1.0, whose script sat in /root where Gaming Mode never read it, the script is
  installed in the right place and the old copy removed; no Setup is needed.

**TDP**
- Presets now come from each console's BIOS table, so every console in the family gets its own firmware
  limits.

**Controller firmware**
- The updater, in the panel and the Desktop app, shows a red **Risk notice** above its
  buttons: it is the only Companion feature that could damage the hardware.
- It has been tested only by reinstalling the firmware already installed, not by updating
  to a newer version; the notice goes away once the next real update has been verified.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Controllers**
- The controller no longer stays dead until a restart, usually after sleep (Legion Go 2, and a
  Legion Go with the 2025 controller firmware), when SteamOS's InputPlumber loses it on a reset or reconnect.
- Companion checks about 17 seconds after a reconnect, a sleep and its own start, and restarts
  InputPlumber once if the controller is still lost; button mapping and gyro source come back on their own.
- That restart happens at most once per 10 minutes and three times per start, and never while
  InputPlumber is stopped or disabled or a firmware update is running.

**TDP**
- **Allow up to 50 W** keeps working after an update without **Retry helper download**; the verified
  `ryzenadj` helper is now kept outside Decky's plugin folder, which every update deletes.
- After updating from 2.2.x the helper is downloaded once in the background at the next start (turning
  **Allow up to 50 W** off cancels it); the firmware limits run until then.
- **Allow up to 50 W** always runs the firmware's custom mode under the higher limits; before, an earlier
  mode (for example Performance) could stay active and replace them.

**Controller firmware**
- Install no longer stops fwupd after a fixed 10 minutes while it is still writing; it
  stops it only after 10 minutes without progress, or 30 in total, asking it to exit cleanly first.

**Install**
- When Decky stops Companion while it is still starting (right after installing a ZIP), Companion now
  stops within Decky's time limit instead of being killed after 5 seconds.

**Startup**
- The panel and the Desktop app wait for the console to be detected instead of briefly showing every
  module.

### 🔧 Changed

**TDP**
- With **Allow up to 50 W**, the Legion Go 2 keeps sustained power at its firmware limit (35 W) even when a
  higher value is requested; only the boost limits go to 50 W.
- The panel shows the sustained power that actually runs, and Custom offers sustained power up to 35 W
  with boosts up to 50 W.
- In the Desktop app, choosing **This game** creates the game's profile at once, as in the panel.
- In the Desktop app, the power summary names the game and its preset from the limits that run now and warns
  "above Lenovo's limit" only while 50 W is not allowed.
- In the Desktop app, **Retry helper download** appears only while the helper is missing, and **CPU Boost**
  cannot be switched while its state is unknown.
- The Desktop app shows the "50 W paused", "TDP control unavailable" and "Could not load profile" (with
  **Retry profile**) notices.
- The Desktop app's CPU energy preference uses the panel's names (System default, Prefer CPU, Balanced ·
  Prefer CPU, Balanced · Prefer GPU, Prefer GPU) and stays shown at 50% when the system sets it.
- The Desktop app's readouts are **Limits now** (SPL · SPPT · FPPT) and **Set by**, also on the Overview.

**Fan**
- The 100°C point of a curve now runs at least 2000 RPM (before: 1500 RPM) and stays editable up to full
  speed; at 100°C and above the fan still runs at full speed.
- A saved curve whose 100°C point was lower is raised to 2000 RPM, with the rest of the curve unchanged.
- Dragging a curve point below the minimum running speed stops the fan only when dragged below half of that
  minimum; above it, the point snaps to the minimum. Stepping with the D-pad or keys is unchanged.
- "Assign curves to TDP presets" waits for unsaved curve changes and for a pending curve review.
- The Desktop app uses the panel's names and formats ("Maximum", "50.0%", "Save global curve", "Assign
  curve to …", "Starting curve", "Speed unit", "Speed edit step", "Full screen curve editor").
- The Desktop app can save an unchanged curve to confirm a review or to give a preset its own copy.
- The Desktop app offers "Use global curve" only for a preset that has its own curve, and always lets you
  turn Fan Control off while connected.

**Wi-Fi**
- **Automatic** always means the original Wi-Fi behaviour; if the band setting Companion applied was
  changed outside Companion, choosing Automatic puts the recorded original back (and says so) instead of refusing.
- A saved policy that is not recognized and changed nothing is simply cleared, and a profile that cannot
  be read still refuses.
- Automatic can be chosen whenever there is a saved setting to clear, also on another Wi-Fi card, during
  a recovery or while the link state is unknown.
- In the Desktop app, band choices and the reconnect buttons need a live connection and a supported Wi-Fi
  card, as in the panel.
- The Desktop app shows the panel's notes (settings locked, unsupported card, link state) and reports a
  change it could not verify.

**Display**
- In the Desktop app, all display controls pause while display settings cannot be read, and during an
  unfinished reset only "Retry display reset" can be used (without a second question).
- In the Desktop app, "Brightness slider in HDR" appears only when the screen supports it and no
  restart is pending.
- In the Desktop app, the first mode choice waits for the restart that finishes a reset, and "Reset
  display fix" appears once a mode is chosen.

**Battery**
- In the Desktop app, battery protection shows the saved choice while Companion manages charging and
  waits for a known battery state; controller levels outside 0–100% show "—" (a detached controller is marked).

**Lighting**
- In the Desktop app, effect, colour, brightness and speed wait for the stick lights, and the lights
  show "Restoring saved state…".
- In the Desktop app, "Restore original lighting" stays available while the lights recover.

**Vibration**
- In the Desktop app, Touchpad strength waits for Touchpad vibration, and vibration names match the
  panel (which keeps "Med", "Race" and "Std" on its narrow sliders).

**Button mapping**
- In the Desktop app, the button choices wait for button mapping and are hidden with Restore
  defaults when the controller does not support it.

**Gyro & touchpad**
- In the Desktop app, the gyro source waits for the controller test to end and reads "Not
  confirmed yet…" until Companion has confirmed it; test rates show one decimal.

**Controller firmware**
- In the Desktop app, the install asks "Install controller firmware?".

**Modules**
- In the Desktop app, Manage Modules shows each module's description, error or note as the panel does.

**Settings**
- Settings from the old standalone plugins (LeGoTDP, LeGo Vibe Control, LeGo2 Brightness Fix) and from
  versions before 2.1.0 are no longer imported.
- Companion still pauses while those old plugins are installed.

### 🐛 Fixed

**TDP**
- A first CPU Boost or EPP change that was interrupted part-way (Companion stopped, or the system could not
  confirm the old value afterwards) is now still put back when TDP is turned off or Companion is removed.
- A sustained power (SPL) above 35 W saved by 2.2.0 or earlier, globally or in a game profile, now reads
  as the 35 W that actually runs, in the panel and the Desktop app.
- TDP and battery share one firmware lock, so their firmware calls never overlap.

**Wi-Fi**
- With the iwd backend, when NetworkManager refuses to reconnect a network (seen with a WPA3 profile on a
  mixed WPA2/WPA3 network), Companion asks iwd to rejoin it.
- A 5/6 GHz switch, "Reconnect to 5/6 GHz" or a rollback no longer leaves Wi-Fi disconnected with the
  band policy stuck in recovery.
- Changing the band policy while `/etc/iwd/main.conf` has duplicate `[Rank]` sections or keys is refused
  up front, instead of leaving the band policy stuck in recovery.
- Wi-Fi never writes a line break or other saved text into `/etc/iwd/main.conf` from saved settings.

**Display**
- When another program keeps switching the panel's HDR mode back a moment after Companion sets it,
  Companion now stands off for a minute as intended instead of switching back and forth indefinitely.

**Controller firmware**
- Install refuses a controller that is detached from the console or below 30% battery, and
  checks it again with a fresh reading right before it is written.
- If Install stops there, the message says which controllers were already updated; Check
  refuses to start while another firmware updater is running.

**Modules**
- A module that failed to start can now be turned off from the Decky panel too; its switch reads On
  with the error and **Retry … start**.
- A module that is turned off no longer shows its old startup error.

**Desktop app**
- The Overview TDP badge reads "Off · Lenovo defaults" while TDP control is off and otherwise names
  the preset with its sustained power, as in the panel.
- The TDP page shows "Loading power limits…" instead of placeholder 15/20/25 W values until the
  first reading.
- A change that gets no answer in time now says to check the current value before trying again,
  since it may already have been applied.
- The connection to Companion refuses NaN and Infinity values, which the panels never send.

**Updates**
- About in the Desktop app shows the result of the update check ("Up to date", "No public release yet",
  …) instead of "Not checked".

**Vibration**
- The Desktop app shows "Controller driver not found" when the panel does.
- If the controller does not accept a change, the setting goes back to the value the controller really
  has, instead of showing the new one.
- A change made while no controller is connected now says "Controller not connected. The change is
  saved and applies when it connects." in the panel and the Desktop app, and both show the saved value.

**Startup**
- Modules now start one at a time, which avoids firmware errors when several of them touch the
  hardware right after boot.
- A module whose start takes longer than 15 s no longer holds back the others.
- Until it has finished, the panel and the Desktop app show it as **Starting** ("Still starting. Its
  controls appear when it has finished.") instead of hiding it or reporting an error.
- A module that is still starting can be turned off ("Turns off when it has finished starting."); the
  choice is saved at once and applied right after the start, never in the middle of a hardware change.
- Stopping or removing Companion during such a start no longer lets that start apply changes
  afterwards.

**Fan**
- The BIOS/EC versions Companion has already tested are saved in a way that survives a power cut, so the
  fan self-test is not repeated after one.

**Logs**
- Removing old plugin logs never follows a link out of the log folder, and Companion logs a warning when a
  Decky update stops its unload workaround from applying.

### ✨ Added

**Desktop app**
- A native C++/Qt app in the application menu with the same modules, settings and wording as the
  Decky panel, laid out for a mouse and a wide window.
- It uses SteamOS's own Qt 6.9 or newer, so nothing extra is installed, and talks to the running
  Decky plugin so both always show the same state.
- When Desktop Mode starts, Companion starts in the system tray; click the icon to open the window.
  Turning off **Show tray icon** in the app's settings also stops this.
- Uninstalling the plugin closes the app, and updating the plugin restarts it in the new version
  (it asks first if you have unsaved TDP or fan changes).
- Decky's **Install from ZIP** works while the app is open.

**Game profiles**
- The TDP page lists every game that has its own settings, by its Steam name, with what it uses
  (This game, This game + charger, or Global with its settings kept) and its power limits.
- **Edit** opens a game's settings in the same controls, also when the game isn't running, and
  saves them without touching the settings running now; **Delete** removes a profile after a confirmation.

**TDP**
- Custom sliders in the Desktop app follow the same rules as in Decky: boosts never drop below sustained
  power.

**Logs**
- About → View logs shows recent events from Companion's event log with a **Problems** filter.
- The log is `/var/log/legiongo2companion/events.jsonl`, readable by root only, at most 3 MiB.
- The events can be exported for a bug report.
- Warnings now mean something needs attention; expected events such as a Gaming Mode restart are no longer
  reported as problems.

**Controller firmware**
- Check, download and install Lenovo's newest left controller, right controller and
  receiver firmware from Gaming Mode (experimental), asking Lenovo's Legion Space update service.
- Every image is verified with Lenovo's signing key, and everything newer is installed in
  one step with SteamOS's fwupd tool.
- Companion's own controller features pause during the update and the new versions are
  checked afterwards; tested on the Legion Go 2 only by reinstalling the current versions of all three components.
- Installing needs the charger or at least 30% battery; when Lenovo's service answers
  slowly or with errors, a check retries instead of failing.

**Wi-Fi**
- With the WPA backend, the Decky panel can now turn on Only 6 GHz (the Desktop app already could), after
  a confirmation that Wi-Fi is lost outside 6 GHz coverage.
- Only 6 GHz needs NetworkManager 1.58 or newer and is hidden otherwise.

### 🔧 Changed

**Compatibility**
- Tested on SteamOS 3.8 Stable; also checked on SteamOS 3.9.3 Beta, where Display uses SteamOS's
  own Legion Go 2 display profile and Only 6 GHz is available.

**Panel**
- Pages are shorter and easier with the D-pad: explanations moved into the controls' descriptions,
  technical facts into **Show details** at the end of each page, and results into short notifications.
- A failure stays under the control that failed, and every page ends with a row you can always reach.
- Confirmation is asked only for restarting Gaming Mode, Only 5/6 GHz, Only 6 GHz, installing or
  resetting the display fix, deleting a TDP game profile, allowing 50 W and discarding unsaved Custom limits.
- One Fan Control status (for example **Starting your curve…**, **Paused, resuming automatically**,
  **Turned off after an error**) on the page and in the main menu.
- One battery line with both controllers, and a single Wi-Fi **Band** choice.
- Module names are TDP, Fan Control, Vibration, Lighting, Button mapping, Gyro & touchpad, Battery,
  Display and Wi-Fi, with "Gaming Mode" throughout; the Full Power preset is now **Maximum**.

**TDP**
- One **Settings for <game>** choice (Global, This game, This game + charger) replaces the per-game and
  AC toggles.
- **Global keeps the game's settings** for later instead of deleting them; **Delete profile for
  <game>** removes them.
- Presets are buttons that apply at once, Custom limits are a draft with **Apply**, and the power line
  shows what runs now and the live draw.
- Only the Legion Go 2 is supported; TDP, CPU Boost and EPP write nothing on other models and the page says
  the device is unsupported.
- A game's profile applies as soon as the game starts, instead of at the next five-second check.
- The RyzenAdj helper is no longer downloaded at startup; turning on **Allow up to 50 W** downloads and
  verifies it first.
- Inside the normal firmware range a firmware refusal is reported instead of switching to RyzenAdj.
- Disabling the module or uninstalling restores your system's own platform profile, CPU Boost and EPP
  (turning TDP off restores the platform profile), captured before Companion first changes them.
- That capture happens on a fresh install, or after the first reboot following this update; until then the
  previous defaults apply: Balanced, Boost on, balance_performance.

**Fan**
- Custom control now persists: switching between Gaming and Desktop Mode no longer turns Fan Control off.
- After sleep, shutdown, a plugin reload or an update the fan briefly returns to firmware automatic and
  then resumes your saved curve (**Starting your curve…** or **Paused, resuming automatically** meanwhile).
- This includes the first start after updating from 2.1.0 when Fan Control was on.
- The 100°C point's speed is editable; it stays at 100°C, can go down to 1500 RPM and never below the point
  before it, and at 100°C and above the fan still runs at full speed.
- A transient internal error restarts the controller up to three times in ten minutes before Fan Control
  turns itself off with the reason.
- Hardware evidence (fan stall, foreign override, failed readback, invalid sensor value) still turns Fan
  Control off immediately, and a fault in the current boot prevents automatic resume.
- BIOS and EC updates no longer turn Fan Control off; it used to require BIOS RRCN16WW and EC 1.16 exactly
  and now checks the EC fan interface's behaviour at every start.
- After a firmware update, a one-time check raises the fan speed briefly and watches the fan follow; if it
  does not, Fan Control turns off and says the BIOS/EC version changed how the fan is controlled.
- Turning Fan Control on again repeats that check, and a passed check is remembered for that BIOS/EC pair;
  the 83N0 model requirement is unchanged.
- An unstable EC read or selector interference now counts as a transient error, retried up to three times
  in ten minutes, instead of turning Fan Control off at once.
- The fan controller and its backup now release the EC on SIGTERM and are protected from the
  out-of-memory killer.
- A leftover override without a live owner is released to firmware automatic instead of blocking Fan
  Control until power-off.

**Lighting**
- The power-button light survives BIOS updates; it no longer requires BIOS RRCN16WW with an exact ACPI
  table, and instead checks that the live table still places the light at the same register bit (83N0 only).

**Vibration**
- Disabling the module or uninstalling restores the controller's own vibration settings captured
  before the first change on a fresh install; existing installs keep restoring the default profile.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Display**
- Your 2.1.0 panel mode now actually loads; the display script moves automatically to the Gaming Mode
  user's folder when the plugin starts, and one Gaming Mode restart applies it.
- Hybrid no longer fights another HDR tool; when something keeps switching the screen back, it stops
  after four undone switches in either direction instead of blanking the screen every few seconds.
- Disabling Display in Hybrid no longer switches through PQ on the way out.
- After a failed screen read or a resume, Hybrid keeps forwarding brightness for the rest of the Gaming
  Mode session.
- After an interrupted EDID write, the fix continues once gamescope publishes its EDID at a new path
  and the old file is gone.
- Turning the EDID fix off restores the original only into the file Companion trimmed, never into a new
  file gamescope published in its place.
- Uninstalling clears the HDR setting only when you had chosen an HDR mode, and in Desktop Mode Display
  no longer polls the Gaming Mode screen.

**Fan**
- Starting Fan Control no longer occasionally waits 20 seconds and counts as a failed attempt.
- Saving an unsaved curve right after turning Fan Control on or off is no longer refused as "changed
  elsewhere".
- With the TDP module turned off, power-preset curve assignments use the global curve.
- A full runtime directory can no longer keep the custom fan speed after Fan Control stops; the fan returns
  to firmware automatic first and the stop reason is recorded only if it can be.
- The independent backup also retries a release that failed once when the main fan process is already gone.

**TDP**
- A charger change that fails part-way is retried, instead of the battery limits being written back over
  the charger limits; a game switch right after plugging in applies the charger settings.
- A limit the firmware keeps clamping is retried three times, not again every 30 seconds.
- Extras taps and helper retries apply in the order you made them.

**Game profiles**
- Saving a game profile no longer drops profiles beyond the 512th, for example ones imported from
  LeGoTDP; the limit only applies to new profiles.

**Wi-Fi**
- A disconnected device shows Disconnected, so Only 5/6 GHz and Only 6 GHz can be turned off while they
  leave you without Wi-Fi.
- Turning a band policy off also works after a failed reconnect, and with iwd it is never blocked by the
  saved-network check.
- Reconnect works again after an automatic rollback; an open saved network no longer blocks the iwd
  features, and `/etc/iwd/main.conf` stays intact when its last section has no final newline.
- The backend is read from NetworkManager's effective configuration, so a configuration override is no
  longer misread; without a link, Wi-Fi no longer runs `nmcli` in the background.

**Lighting**
- The first time Companion takes over the lights it keeps their brightness, and it writes settings
  even when the controller's current value can't be read.

**Button mapping**
- It can be disabled while InputPlumber is unavailable or stalled, the restored system actions
  are verified, and it accepts an InputPlumber profile with no mappings.

**Vibration**
- One failed controller event no longer stops Vibration from reapplying your settings when a
  controller reconnects.

**Install**
- Stopping, reloading or updating the plugin no longer takes five seconds and a forced kill on Decky
  3.2.10.

**Panel**
- Pages stop reading hardware while the Companion tab is hidden, and the check for conflicting plugins no
  longer rereads every plugin's manifest every five seconds.
- A momentary error in that check no longer blocks the panel until Decky restarts.

**Logs**
- Fewer warnings in the system log for expected events; events from the plugin's first seconds are kept.

### ✨ Added

**Fan**
- New Fan Control: build your own cooling curve in the Steam overlay with direct control through the
  console's embedded controller (EC), with live temperature and measured fan speed beside the editor.
- An eight-point curve from 0 to 100°C; adjust the first seven points, the last stays fixed at 100°C and
  full speed. Points stay in temperature order and the curve cannot decrease in speed as temperature rises.
- Edit by touch (drag points) or with the controller: press **A** on the graph, select a point with
  **LB / RB**, and use the **D-pad** to change temperature and speed; **B** leaves point editing.
- Choose a speed edit step, or open the **full-screen curve editor** for more room.
- Choose RPM or percentage and see the actual measured fan speed separately from your requested curve;
  live readings also work with firmware automatic control, and 100% is the tested 4800 RPM ceiling.
- Built-in hysteresis avoids chasing small temperature fluctuations; speed rises quickly when needed, then
  falls more gradually as the device cools.
- Three starting curves (Silent, Balanced and Aggressive) are editable; new settings use Balanced with one
  global curve, choosing a template changes the draft, and saving keeps it for later.
- Optionally assign curves to Companion's TDP presets, including game and battery/AC profile changes;
  assignments start off and do not follow the separate SteamOS QAM power profiles.
- You choose when custom cooling runs: saving a curve while control is off does not activate it, and
  turning Fan Control off returns control to firmware automatic.
- After startup, plugin reload, sleep or a fault, custom control needs explicit re-enabling; saved curves
  remain, and the page reports blocked operation or incomplete recovery.
- A separate watchdog helps release custom control back to firmware automatic if the controller stops
  responding; stale or inconsistent readings and detected faults also trigger recovery.
- This recovery depends on a working kernel and EC connection.
- Fan Control is limited to the validated Legion Go 2 8ASP2 / 83N0, BIOS RRCN16WW and EC 1.16; other
  hardware or firmware variants are not enabled.
- Supported targets are **0 RPM (stop)** or **1500–4800 RPM**, and measured speed can vary from the
  target.
- Use only one fan controller at a time, and return any other controller to firmware automatic before
  enabling Fan Control.

### 🔧 Changed
- **Vibration:** rapid edits now keep the latest queued value for each control and profile instead of replaying
  superseded values behind a slow hardware write; closing the page still saves the final accepted change.
- **Wi-Fi:** power-save changes and recovery verify the active network profile, reducing the chance of restoring a
  previous connection's policy after switching networks; unverified recovery remains pending.
- **Display:** invalid OLED mode requests are rejected before changing settings or installing the legacy display
  script, instead of silently selecting PQ.
- **Docs:** the README now explains controls, recovery and hardware limits, with screenshots of all nine modules,
  module management and the full-screen fan editor.

koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.name: Elemental DeckKeys 1.1.0
koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.body:
**New**
- Send whole folders: drag a folder onto the Files tab or use "Choose folder". The folder structure is kept; if a folder with that name already exists, a new one ("Name (1)") is made.
- A folder that does not fit on the Deck is refused before anything is sent.
- Upload speed and time left, and the progress in the browser tab title (for example "42% · Elemental DeckKeys"), so you can follow it from another tab.
- The Deck and the PC stay awake while files are transferred.
- Faster with many small files (4 files at a time); a dropped file is retried automatically.
- "Resume" continues a stopped folder in the same folder on the Deck, skipping the files that already arrived (a file that was cut off starts again).

**Fixed**
- Ending the session or switching DeckKeys off now stops a file that is being sent or downloaded.

**Update** – run the install command again in Konsole on the Deck (pairing is kept, open pages reload by themselves):
```
curl -L https://github.com/Koutasora/Elemental-DeckKeys/releases/latest/download/Elemental-DeckKeys.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp && sudo bash /tmp/Elemental-DeckKeys/files/install.sh
```
Or unpack `Elemental-DeckKeys.zip` on the Deck and double-click `Install Elemental DeckKeys.desktop`.

koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.name: Elemental DeckKeys 1.0.1
koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.body:
**Fixed**
- Letters could repeat by themselves (for example "Enjoy" arriving as "Enjoyyy") when typing in Live or Touchpad over a laggy Wi-Fi. Holding a key, such as Backspace, still repeats as before.

**Update** – run the install command again in Konsole on the Deck (pairing is kept, open pages reload by themselves):
```
curl -L https://github.com/Koutasora/Elemental-DeckKeys/releases/latest/download/Elemental-DeckKeys.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp && sudo bash /tmp/Elemental-DeckKeys/files/install.sh
```
Or unpack `Elemental-DeckKeys.zip` on the Deck and double-click `Install Elemental DeckKeys.desktop`.

koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.name: Elemental DeckKeys 1.0.0
koutasora/elemental-deckkeys.body:
Control your Steam Deck from the browser on your PC or phone, over the local network. Works in Game Mode and Desktop Mode.

**What's in 1.0.0**
- **Text** – send typed or pasted text, optionally with Enter; saved snippets.
- **Live** – your keyboard types on the Deck as you press keys; Ctrl+V types the PC clipboard; macros (Alt+F4, Alt+Tab, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+A, F11, Super).
- **Media** – play/pause, previous, next, stop, volume, mute.
- **Touchpad** – the PC mouse (and optionally keyboard) controls the Deck until Esc; a touchpad on phones.
- **Files** – send files to `Downloads/DeckKeysTransfers/Received`, download from `Downloads/DeckKeysTransfers/Send to PC`.
- Pairing with a 6-digit code and a QR code, HTTPS with the Deck's own certificate, sessions, on/off switch.
- Optional Decky panel for Game Mode.

**Install** – in Konsole on the Deck:
```
curl -L https://github.com/Koutasora/Elemental-DeckKeys/releases/latest/download/Elemental-DeckKeys.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp && sudo bash /tmp/Elemental-DeckKeys/files/install.sh
```
Or unpack `Elemental-DeckKeys.zip` on the Deck and double-click `Install Elemental DeckKeys.desktop`. Then open `https://steamdeck.local:8443` on your PC.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.6
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Improve text, background and button contrast when using custom CSS Loader themes.
- Stop showing ordinary folders as unknown plugins while keeping plugins with damaged manifests visible.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.5
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Read release notes before downloading an update or choosing another version.
- Expand or collapse longer notes with a compact arrow that works with a controller.
- Review downgrade warnings alongside the selected version’s notes.
- Fix security warnings opening halfway down the page and improve panel sizing.
- Translate the new interface into all ten supported languages.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.4
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Add a compact, expandable capability overview based on the validated plugin ZIP and installed files, with detected folders, commands, devices, domains and GitHub projects. Analysis is informational and does not restrict access.
- Require review for executable downloads moving to another GitHub project, newly insecure HTTP code downloads, and newly identified administrator-command execution without a root declaration. Preserve existing root acknowledgment and Decky’s native confirmation; unchanged routine updates do not repeat warnings.
- Simplify security details and installation review, remove duplicate summaries, and localize the new interface in all ten supported languages.
- Improve domain detection for HTTP sessions, Request objects, Decky fetch calls and larger JavaScript bundles. Exclude shell help text, syntax and pseudo-devices such as /dev/null from misleading capability lists.

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.3
nukeador/deckyup.body:
- Recognize release ZIPs with packaging suffixes such as `ResonaDeck-1.2.0-Stable.zip` while preserving validated plugin identity and version checks.
- Exclude clearly marked prerelease ZIPs from automatic stable updates.
