featherwolf/enhancedgv.name: EnhancedGV v0.19.2 — hotfix
featherwolf/enhancedgv.body:
> **Hotfix.** Store content stopped loading for many Steam games, showing
> "no store data (success=false)". Update and it comes back within a couple of
> minutes. Nothing on your end was wrong, and no settings are lost.

- **Store content loads again.** Steam's store has been labelling many of its
  replies with a different app's number, often one of the game's DLC, while the
  details inside still describe the right game. The plugin looked the reply up
  under the game's own number, found nothing, and called the game unavailable.
  It now checks which game the details describe instead of trusting the label.
  It has nothing to do with which DLC you own.
- **Clearer error when Steam sends nothing back.** An empty reply now says so
  instead of reporting `success=false`.

---
Install via Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP. The plugin's Updates section checks for and links to new releases.

featherwolf/enhancedgv.name: EnhancedGV v0.19.1 — hotfix
featherwolf/enhancedgv.body:
> **Hotfix.** If you set up IGDB credentials on 0.19.0, changing any other
> setting afterwards silently forgot your Client ID. Update, then paste the
> Client ID in once more — leave the Secret field empty, the saved one is kept.

- **Saving another setting no longer forgets your IGDB Client ID.** The panel
  was writing back the empty id it had loaded with, which dropped IGDB to the
  keyless baseline and hid the **Remove credentials** button. An empty id now
  means "leave it alone", exactly as an empty secret already did.
- **Remove credentials now erases rather than blanks.** Both fields are deleted
  outright, the old settings contents and the cached access token are
  overwritten before removal, and store data cached while IGDB was in use is
  dropped. The overwrite is best effort — on an SSD doing wear levelling the old
  blocks can survive it — so regenerating the secret at dev.twitch.tv is still
  the only complete revocation. The button now also appears whenever *either*
  half is stored, so a device left holding a secret with no id can clear it.
- **Credentials survive updates, reinstalls and uninstalling the plugin.** They
  live in Decky's settings folder, which a plugin update never touches, so
  updating doesn't log you out of IGDB. Uninstalling doesn't erase them either:
  press **Remove credentials** first if you want the secret off the device.

---
Install via Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP. The plugin's Updates section checks for and links to new releases.

featherwolf/enhancedgv.name: EnhancedGV v0.19.0
featherwolf/enhancedgv.body:
- **Metadata for emulated / non-Steam games (experimental, off by default).** When
  a non-Steam game has no Steam store page, EnhancedGV can now pull a description,
  details and artwork from **Hasheous** — a free, keyless community game database.
  Turn it on in Quick Access → EnhancedGV → *Non-Steam games (experimental)*.
  - It only kicks in for games that have their own entry in your Steam library
    (e.g. ROMs added as individual shortcuts via Steam ROM Manager). A single
    emulator/frontend shortcut (one ES-DE/RetroDeck entry for your whole library)
    has no per-game page to attach to.
  - Steam always wins when a game genuinely exists on Steam (you get the full store
    page); Hasheous is only used as a fallback for titles Steam doesn't have.
  - Reviews, Steam Deck compatibility and update history are Steam-only, so those
    sections simply don't appear for a non-Steam game.
  - This is the keyless baseline (title, description, genres, developer/publisher,
    platform, logo). No account, no key, nothing to sign up for.
- **Optional artwork upgrade for those games (free IGDB credentials).** Add IGDB
  credentials in the same panel and those games also get proper **cover art,
  screenshots, genres and developers** — so the media gallery works for a SNES ROM
  the same way it does for a Steam game. Setup is below; it takes a few minutes and
  costs nothing.
  - Entirely optional; with no credentials you get the keyless baseline unchanged.
  - **IGDB is queried directly** rather than through Hasheous' metadata proxy. That
    proxy needs a client API key issued per registered application, and only
    Hasheous admins can create one — three exist service-wide. IGDB's own API is
    free and self-serve, so anyone can turn this on.
  - One expanded request per game returns the cover, screenshots, genres and
    companies together.
  - The access token is minted from your credentials, cached for its ~60-day life
    and refreshed automatically. The secret travels in a form body, never a URL,
    is stored on the device only, and is never logged or shown by the diagnostic.
  - Images load in display sizes rather than originals (a cover is ~21 KB instead
    of ~2.7 MB), so the gallery doesn't stall on a handheld connection.
  - The panel header notes where non-Steam content came from ("via Hasheous + IGDB").
- **Better matching, and a manual override for when it still gets it wrong.**
  Hasheous indexes ROM *dumps* rather than releases, which works well for retro
  ROMs and badly for modern console games — Breath of the Wild appears only as a
  Wii U entry with no ROM attached, and a search for Metroid Dread returned Game
  Boy Color and amiibo entries that outranked the real game. Three changes:
  - Wrong-platform entries no longer win. Candidates with no ROM are skipped (they
    could never resolve anyway), rom hacks, bootlegs, soundtracks and amiibo
    entries rank last, and the game's own platform is preferred when known.
  - **With IGDB credentials set, IGDB is asked first** (after Steam), and Hasheous
    only as a backstop. IGDB indexes games, so it answers with the actual release.
    Without credentials IGDB cannot answer at all, so Hasheous is used alone.
  - **You can point any game at any listing yourself**, using the field that was
    already there: Quick Access → EnhancedGV → *Store data source*. A bare number
    or Steam URL still means Steam, exactly as before; type `igdb:1103` or
    `hasheous:6292` to use another source and press **Save ID**. IGDB ids are on
    the game's igdb.com page, and an `igdb.com/games/…` link works too. The choice
    sticks and is never re-detected. **Clear (leave blank)** still hides the panel
    for a game, and **Re-detect automatically** still starts over.
- **Beta channel is back.** Quick Access → EnhancedGV → Updates → *Beta channel
  (test builds)*. Betas are published as GitHub pre-releases instead of private
  drafts, so the toggle can actually see them; stable users are never offered one.
  Each beta cut is numbered (`0.19.0-beta.1`, `.2`, …) and installs under that
  version, so you're offered the next cut and, when it ships, the finished release
  — previously the updater treated a beta and its release as the same version and
  left beta testers stranded.
- **Store content survives a flaky connection.** If a background refresh of cached
  store data fails (offline, rate-limited), the last good copy is kept instead of
  being replaced by the error.
- **The panel appears far sooner on a game page.** It used to wait for a
  once-every-2-seconds re-sync to notice the page had finished laying out, so on
  most page loads it arrived a beat or two after everything else. It now retries
  in a tight burst as soon as Steam renders the page and stops the moment it has
  landed.
- **Store content is fetched the instant the page opens**, in parallel with the
  page transition and the panel's own setup, instead of only after the panel has
  mounted. Plugin settings are read once at startup so they are never on that
  path either.
- **Content appears in two stages instead of all at once.** The description,
  trailers, screenshots and details now paint as soon as they arrive rather than
  waiting for reviews, update history and the Deck report; those sections show a
  small shimmer and fill in a moment later.
- **Revisiting a game is instant.** Cached store data past its refresh window is
  now shown immediately and refreshed in the background, so a game you've opened
  before never sends you back to the loading placeholder.
- **Pressing down before the panel appears no longer skips it.** The placeholder
  is a real selection stop, so the D-pad/stick scrolls into the section instead
  of jumping straight to the tab strip — and if the press lands in the split
  second before the panel is in place, it is replayed into the panel once it is,
  so you end up where the press would have taken you.
- **Focus is no longer lost when content replaces the placeholder** you were
  sitting on — the selection moves to the panel's first item instead of dropping
  out of the panel and scrolling the page back to the top.

### Setting up IGDB artwork (optional, free)

IGDB is owned by Twitch and uses Twitch developer accounts, so setup happens there:

1. Create a **Twitch account** at <https://twitch.tv> if you don't have one.
2. **Enable two-factor authentication** on it. The developer console refuses to
   register an application without it, and this is the step people miss.
3. Go to <https://dev.twitch.tv/console/apps> and press **Register Your
   Application**. Name it anything.
4. Set **OAuth Redirect URL** to `http://localhost`. IGDB never uses it, but the
   form demands a value.
5. Set **Client Type** to **Confidential**. This is the setting that allows a
   secret to exist. Get it wrong and step 7 fails with "Twitch rejected the
   client id/secret pair".
6. Copy the **Client ID**.
7. Press **New Secret** and copy the **Client Secret**. It is shown once.
8. On the Deck, paste both into the EnhancedGV panel and press **Save credentials**.

Free for non-commercial use, limited to 4 requests per second — far above anything
this plugin does. Saving clears cached data so games you already opened refetch
with artwork. **Remove credentials** goes back to the keyless baseline at any time.

If artwork doesn't appear, open a game's page and press **Test artwork lookup**. It
reports each stage separately, so a failure names itself rather than showing an
empty gallery:

| Stage | A ✖ here means |
| --- | --- |
| Non-Steam sources enabled | The toggle is off. |
| Credentials present | One of the two fields is empty. |
| Access token from Twitch | Twitch rejected the pair — usually Client Type was not **Confidential**, or the secret was regenerated after you saved it. |
| This game maps to IGDB | No IGDB link was found for *this* title. Not fatal: the credentials are then tested against a known game, so the rows below still tell you if they work. Set the id by hand with `igdb:…` in *Store data source*. |
| IGDB game fetched | `401`/`403` = token or client id rejected. `429` = over the rate limit. |
| Screenshots listed | Credentials work; IGDB simply has no screenshots for that title. |
| Image address resolved | Screenshots exist but carried no image id. Please report this one. |

**Known limits.** Steam games are untouched by all of the above. No trailers for
non-Steam games, because IGDB supplies YouTube ids rather than playable URLs. A
single emulator or frontend shortcut covering your whole library has no per-game
page to attach to.

### Security

A multi-lens audit ran over the plugin once it started collecting credentials:
65 candidate issues, each reviewed by three independent verifiers. Seventeen were
confirmed and all are fixed in this release.

Three of them were **not** new — they were also present in v0.18.0 and earlier:
the news injection, the URL filter blind spot, and the freeze.

- **The IGDB client secret is no longer readable by other plugins.** `get_settings`
  is an unauthenticated RPC that any code in the Steam UI can call, and it was
  returning the secret in cleartext. It now reports only whether one is stored.
- **The file holding it is no longer world-readable.** It was written `0644` in a
  `0755` directory, next to a token file that was correctly `0600`.
- **Credentials no longer follow redirects.** A redirect from IGDB would have
  re-sent the bearer token and client id to any host, over plain HTTP.
- **Certificate verification is no longer dropped automatically.** On a
  certificate error the plugin used to silently retry unverified, which handed an
  on-path attacker control of every Steam, Hasheous and GitHub response.
- **Update links are pinned to GitHub over https.** A forged release response
  could otherwise choose where the "download the update" link sent you.
- **The trailer diagnostic only speaks https**, so an upstream response cannot
  point it at local files or the local network.
- **Steam news can no longer inject script into the panel.** A link or image URL
  in an announcement could break out of the HTML attribute it was placed in. News
  content now also goes through the same allowlist filter everything else uses.
- **The URL filter no longer has an encoding blind spot.** A single HTML entity
  could hide a `javascript:` scheme from it.
- **A game description can no longer freeze the plugin.** A pathological run of
  whitespace made the on-device HTML parser take tens of seconds; it is now
  linear, and oversized fields are truncated.
- **Plain-text descriptions are rendered as text**, not as HTML.
- **Links open only if they are ordinary web links.** `steam://` and `file://`
  targets from a store or news response are ignored rather than handed to the
  Steam client.
- **Trailer URLs must be Steam's own CDN**, so a tampered store response cannot
  point the player at another host, and a malformed manifest can no longer
  exhaust memory.
- **Matching a non-Steam game is bounded**, so one page open cannot turn into
  thousands of lookups.

---
Install via Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP. The plugin's Updates section checks for and links to new releases.

featherwolf/enhancedgv.name: EnhancedGV v0.18.0
featherwolf/enhancedgv.body:
- **Fixes the remaining crash in co-installed plugins (SDH-PlayTime).** Even after
  EnhancedGV stopped patching Steam's render function, it still re-synced its panel
  from inside Steam's render — inserting/removing its host element and updating state
  while React was mid-render of the shared app-page. That threw DOM errors that
  surfaced through **PlayTime** (which renders on the same page), making its crash
  look like PlayTime's fault. All of that work is now deferred until after Steam
  finishes rendering, so nothing touches the shared page mid-render.
- **Smoother scrolling through long sections.** Holding the D-pad through a long
  section (e.g. "About this game") no longer freezes the view and then jumps to the
  next section — the page now follows the cursor as it moves.
- **Fixes the selection highlight disappearing** on the Play button (and other
  native controls) after scrolling down into the store panel and back up. The
  injected panel was re-syncing itself every 2 seconds and re-registering its
  controls on Steam's shared gamepad-focus tree even when nothing had changed —
  disturbing Steam's focus bookkeeping. It now only re-syncs when something
  actually changed.
- **Fullscreen media navigation is visible now.** While a trailer or screenshot
  is fullscreen, a hint bar shows the controls (◀ ▶ browse, A play/pause,
  X mute, B exit) and the title/position overlay is larger — no more navigating
  blind.
- **Fullscreen locks the selection to the media.** The D-pad can no longer move
  the (invisible) selection onto page elements hidden behind the fullscreen
  view; left/right browse the carousel, B exits.

---
Install via Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP. The plugin's Updates section checks for and links to new releases.

featherwolf/enhancedgv.name: EnhancedGV v0.17.0
featherwolf/enhancedgv.body:
- **Plays nicely with other plugins.** EnhancedGV no longer patches Steam's app-page
  render function or touches its render output. Earlier builds turned the page's
  child element into an array, which crashed **SDH-PlayTime** (it reads that same
  render output) and destabilised **TabMaster** with extra re-render pressure. The
  panel is now injected entirely from EnhancedGV's own component in Decky's tree:
  it finds the visible app page in the DOM, reads that page's app ID from its React
  fiber, and portals the panel in — re-providing the page's gamepad-focus node so
  it stays controller-navigable. No shared Steam React internals are patched.
- **Sharper scaling across displays.** Trailers, screenshots, thumbnails and
  description images now size relative to the screen (Steam Deck 800p, 1080p
  handhelds, 4K TV) instead of a fixed pixel size tuned for a single display.
- **The "What's this game about?" summary is now selectable.** It's a D-pad focus
  stop, so it scrolls into view and can be read on a gamepad — previously the
  cursor skipped over it between the media and the sections.
- **Update panel** now clearly shows the new version, a download/install call to
  action, and an **Open the release page** button.
- **View patch notes (this version)** button in QAM → Updates opens the current
  version's changelog in a popup (CHANGELOG is now bundled with the plugin).

---
Install via Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP. The plugin's Updates section checks for and links to new releases.

starkka15/gamevault.name: v1.3.2 — fixes the plugin failing to open
starkka15/gamevault.body:
## Fixes "Error parsing json result" on opening GameVault

v1.3.0 and v1.3.1 could fail as soon as you opened the plugin:

```
GAMEVAULT ERROR
ActionSet: init
ActionName: InitActions
Message: Error parsing json result Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

The release zips were packaged with Windows line endings in most of the
scripts, so they could not start on SteamOS. This was a packaging mistake in
those two releases, not a Decky Loader incompatibility — it happens on any
Decky version. Thanks to @theSt33v for the report (#13).

v1.3.2 has no feature changes. It is v1.3.1 packaged correctly, and the release
is now built by a script that refuses to produce a zip with this problem.

### If you are on v1.3.0 or v1.3.1, update by hand

The in-app updater lives inside the plugin, which you cannot open, so it cannot
fix this for you. Download `GameVault.zip` below and install it over the top:
Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install Plugin from ZIP file**. (Developer mode
is switched on under Decky → Settings → General.)

Your logins, libraries and installed games are stored separately and are not
affected.

starkka15/gamevault.name: v1.3.1 — ZOOM Platform support
starkka15/gamevault.body:
## ZOOM Platform support

Adds **ZOOM Platform** as a store: log in (including two-factor), browse your
library, install and play. Both build types are handled — a native Linux build
is installed directly, and a Windows build is installed through umu/Proton.

Unlike the other stores, ZOOM ships no command-line tool and no documented API,
so this talks to the website's own endpoints with a logged-in session.

### Thanks

Windows installs are handled by **[zoom-platform.sh](https://github.com/DarthSidiousPT/zoom-platform.sh)**,
the actively-maintained fork by **DarthSidiousPT**. The official script has not
been updated since December 2024 and cannot read installers packaged with a
recent Inno Setup — the fork can, and it handles multi-part installers better
besides. Thank you for keeping it alive.

### This one is new — expect rough edges

The extension has been tested on one account with one game, on a single device.
Please report anything that misbehaves.

**Known issue: the game list does not refresh on its own after you log in.**
The workaround is to press **Toggle Installed** (show installed games) and then
press it again to turn it back off — the list will populate. This is being
looked into.

Other things worth knowing:

- Windows installs run silently, so a game offering optional components gets its
  defaults rather than asking.
- Where a game offers both, the native Linux build is preferred. It is faster and
  needs no Proton.
- A Windows install needs roughly the download size plus the installed size free
  at its peak, so a 7 GB game wants about 15 GB of space.

### Also in this release

Everything from v1.3.0 — the **About → Store Tabs** page for hiding stores you
don't use — is included.

starkka15/gamevault.name: v1.3.0 — Hide unused store tabs
starkka15/gamevault.body:
## Hide the store tabs you don't use

Adds **About → Store Tabs**, with a toggle for each store. Turn off the ones you
don't use and they leave the tab bar — handy on a TV, where every extra tab is
another R1 press.

Hiding is presentation only. A hidden store keeps its login, its installed games
and its Steam shortcuts, and comes back unchanged when you turn it on again.

- Defaults to everything visible, so existing installs are unaffected.
- A newly installed store appears on its own rather than arriving hidden.
- Turning every tab off falls back to showing them all, so you can't strand
  yourself with an empty bar.

Closes part of #12. The ZOOM Platform half of that issue is still in progress and
is not included in this release.

### Under the hood

Tab visibility is keyed on each tab's `ActionId`, not its title or position. The
tab bar previously remembered the active tab by array index, so filtering the
list would silently move you to a different store; tabs are now keyed by
`ActionId`, with a fallback for the old numeric value and for the case where the
remembered tab is the one you just hid.

starkka15/gamevault.name: v1.2.5 - GE-Proton architecture fix
starkka15/gamevault.body:
Backend-only maintenance release.

## GE-Proton install now picks the correct architecture
GameVault's "Install GE-Proton" downloaded the first `.tar.gz` asset in the release, which GloriousEggroll now lists as the **aarch64 (ARM)** build — so on an x86_64 Steam Deck / ROG Ally it installed the wrong architecture. It now selects the **x86_64** build, handling both the new `GE-Proton<ver>-x86_64.tar.gz` naming and the older plain `GE-Proton<ver>.tar.gz`, and refuses to install an aarch64 build on x86_64.

## Note on EA / Need for Speed launches
The EA "couldn't find suitable wine release" launch failure was fixed in the **maxima-cli** dependency (updated to resolve the renamed GE-Proton assets). No GameVault change was needed for it — the EA extension pulls the updated maxima-cli automatically.

starkka15/gamevault.name: v1.2.4 - GOG install-loss + Amazon login fixes
starkka15/gamevault.body:
Maintenance release with two store fixes. All changes are backend-only — no UI changes.

Thanks to **Gameplayhard** for reporting the bug.

## GOG — installed games no longer lost on logout
Previously, logging out of GOG wiped your library database, so your installed games disappeared and appeared to need re-downloading. That no longer happens: your installed games are left in place on logout, and logging back in now **self-heals** by re-detecting the games already installed on your system.

**If GOG is currently showing your installed games as missing:** just **log out of GOG and log back in** — GameVault will re-detect them automatically. No re-downloading required.

## Amazon — login and status fixed
- Logging back in after an Amazon logout no longer fails.
- The Amazon login status now correctly reflects whether you're signed in.

Amazon installs were never affected by the GOG issue above — nothing to recover there.

---
Please report any issues on the tracker.

failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.name: CheevoDeck 1.0.0
failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.body:
Welcome to 1.0, everyone! I consider this my love letter to RetroAchievements. Everything in this update is what I've envisioned since the beginning for what a truly feature-rich RA tracking app should have. It's not just a tracker, it's a suite with all the tools you will ever need to hunt achievements, while also adding a welcoming social experience. Everything is covered below, including all of the new flagship features, quality of life improvements, fixes, and much more. The first thing you will notice when using CheevoDeck 1.0 is that when you enter a page and then go back, you are exactly where you came from. When you are looking at an achievement or anything and you close the Quick Access Menu side window, when you open it again, you are exactly on that achievement still. It was restructured from the ground up, so now no more starting at the top of the page all of the time because full state is now persisted. Alright, on to the features first!

## Features

### Memories

- Turn your SteamOS screenshots and video clips you take into memories. Every screenshot and video clip you take with Steam gets filed under the game you are currently playing into a special memories album. For screenshots, if you take them within 60 seconds of unlocking an achievement before or during it, the achievement and info are added to that memory. Any achievements unlocked during a video clip will also be added to that memory.
- Your screenshot and clip memories are completely independent, so even if you delete the SteamOS source media, it safely exists within CheevoDeck.
- Organize your memories any time, giving them captions to describe how you felt in that moment. Give them tags and color coding as well, allowing you to filter them by category, such as "Funny" or "Personal Best" or whatever you choose.
- Viewing a memory will show the achievements unlocked during or around the time it was captured. It goes a step further for video clip memories where you can use **Timeline Playback**, which highlights your achievements unlocked in real time as it happens in the video.
- Share memories with ease by pressing **R2** on one, where you will be asked to enter a caption and select tags. If you already gave it one, it will be filled out for you as a recommendation. Pressing **Post** opens up CheevoDeck's custom web browser straight to the Discord server's #shared-memories section, filling everything out and attaching your memory for you. You only have to press **Post**. There is also a **Shared Memories** button in the Memories page that brings you straight to #shared-memories to view others' posts in the gallery.
- To start using this feature, select the **Memories** button under your current game's info on the main page. It's the third button from the left.
- Under **Utilities**, you are also able to export / import memories between devices over the network or through sharing file bundles.

### Event Tracking

- **News & Events** has a new **Events** tab listing every RetroAchievements event, allowing the organizing, tracking, and management of events.
- Add events to your tracked list to keep an eye on certain ones or the ones you are working on.
- **Achievement of the Week** now has its own button in there.
- Checklist events let you mark games as beaten or mastered or check off other criteria.
- Because there are different types of events, each is handled uniquely for your tracking.
- Customization for your tracked events, such as adding notes to them, color coding them, or organizing them into collapsible / expandable categories.

### Milestones

- Milestones turns your hunting into a game of its own, with daily quests, combos, XP and ranks earned from the achievements you unlock as well as exploring CheevoDeck.
- Earn XP from learning how CheevoDeck works! Much less boring than a tutorial! The milestone achievements show you features you might never have found, and each one explains how to unlock it. There are Daily and Weekly Quests, combos for unlocking achievements several days in a row, and a rare Bonus Daily Quest with special requirements and rewards that shows up more often the longer your combo runs. Select the rank card to see the full rank table.

### Activity (Calendar)

- The Activity calendar shows activity for a user for each day of each month. Light green indicates light activity, while dark green indicates a lot of activity. It takes the spot where the Mastery Goals button used to be on the Profile page; Mastery Goals is still in the **Quick Menu**.
- View activity for you, your friend, or even a stranger! Selecting a day opens up a list of all of the achievements unlocked that day.
- Easily traverse months or even years back to see how you did or what games you tackled in the past.
- Integrates with Milestones where if you have multiple days in a row with unlocks, you start a Combo where you earn XP each day, contributing to your Milestones rank.

### Web Browser (Utility)

- CheevoDeck's in-house custom web browser offers tons of features and has great performance as well due to blocking intrusive ads, which can be cumbersome on some devices.
- Tab Support: You are able to store up to 100 tabbed pages.
- Bookmarks: Easily bookmark your favorite sites and manage different categories.
- Ad Block: Blocks various ads, which helps speed up page load times, lower CPU usage, and keep memory usage lower. It's quite useful for the Steam Deck, as some very large ads tend to block the very small window on the Deck. Also, you are able to define exemptions.
- YouTube Video Ad Block: Blocks YouTube video ads, allowing you to listen or watch anything uninterrupted.
- YouTube Video Ad Auto-Speedup & Skip: When not using YouTube Ad Blocking, whenever a video ad shows in the middle of a YouTube video, it is automatically sped up to 16x and skipped for you. Ads before a video play normally and are skipped as soon as YouTube allows, unless you turn on **Fast-forward Pre-roll Ads**. Auto-Speedup can be toggled off as well. This is a fallback if video ad block stops working, and I have to update things.
- Video and Audio Background Play: Play a podcast, YouTube video, music, etc. while your browser is minimized and hidden in the background while you play your games for a cozy, chill time.
- More Supported Video Formats: On the built-in SteamOS browser, certain YouTube videos would throw an error. That no longer happens, as more video formats are supported.
- Download Management: Download and manage files in the **Downloads** tab, keeping track of the progress.
- Extremely Memory Efficient: It's designed to be lightweight and not take up many resources. If you want it to clean up everything, simply close it. But if you want it to remain in memory, use the Minimize option. Even then, it does not use many resources.
- High Compatibility: Handles music, videos, documents, and spreadsheets with ease, so whether you want to view a spreadsheet guide or watch a tutorial video, it will work fine!

### Global Buttons

- Your mapped shortcuts that open useful things used to only work within CheevoDeck with the Quick Access Menu side window opened. Now, with Global Buttons, once enabled, you can summon a variety of tools or pages without even opening CheevoDeck. Imagine being able to view your current GameFAQs guide or summoning CheevoDeck's browser while you are playing your game without even having to open the side window. It's now possible!
- Global Buttons can be toggled on/off in your **Quick Menu** on the main page. Only back buttons or button combos are supported for Global Buttons.
- Customize your back buttons and button combos in **Quick Menu** > **Options** > **System** Tab > **Mapped Shortcuts**. Actions that support this feature will have an * after the name.
- Works with the Steam Deck's built-in controls, the ROG Ally and Ally X (**M1** and **M2**), the Steam Controller, the DualSense, the Switch Pro Controller, the Xbox Series X|S Wireless Controller, and the DualShock 4 over Bluetooth.
- After you update, CheevoDeck asks you once whether to turn Global Buttons on. After that point, you can toggle it on/off from the **Quick Menu**.

### Stormbreaker (Utility)

- Protects you from a rare SteamOS glitch where the Quick Access Menu gets stuck and your controls stop responding. Stormbreaker watches for the focus race that causes it and breaks it up the moment it starts.
- While incredibly rare, when the freeze does happen, it sucks because you lose game progress in the process because resetting the system is what most people end up doing due to controls not being responsive. Well, not anymore and not under Stormbreaker's watch!
- Just by having CheevoDeck installed with Stormbreaker on, you are protected from any situation in any game in any plugin. It runs in the background, barely using any resources, as the freeze guard only reacts when focus moves and Automatic Recovery only checks in on Steam's interface every couple of seconds.
- If a freeze ever gets past it, Automatic Recovery restarts Steam's interface while your game keeps running. You can also turn on **Recovery Button Combo** and hold **L4**, **L5**, **R4** and **R5** (**M1** and **M2** on the ROG Ally) for three seconds to do it yourself.
- It has its own page in **Utilities** with Status and Logs tabs, and it's on by default and only runs in Game Mode.

### Calculator (Utility)

- The ultimate achievement hunter utility. It's in **Utilities** and you can map it to a button or access it from the **Quick Menu**. YES!

### Help on Every Page

- Every page now has a **?** button in the top strip that opens that page's tutorial online in CheevoDeck's custom browser. Need help or have a question about how something works for a certain page? Try that button and it might answer your question.

## Quality of Life Improvements

- Every page now returns you to where you were. Close the Quick Access Menu, back out of a dialog, or press **Back**, and you land on the exact row you left, even deep in a long list. SUPER WIN! No more having the page start at the top each time upon QAM opening.
- Long lists are much smoother. A sliding window system has been implemented and built from the ground up, allowing traversal of super-duper long lists. Before, the lists would dynamically expand and expand and expand without collapsing offscreen content. Now they do!
- No more [brackets] for tags. Tracked (Achievements), Game Notes and the Dolphin Mapper have a proper tag field now. So if you want to put an achievement under the "Side-Quests" category, all you do is type in (via the on-screen keyboard) "Side-Quests" into its own field. Your existing tags will work and show up in the new tag field, so no worries.
- Note reminders are now incredibly accurate. They fire when they should, stop as soon as a note is turned off, completed, edited or deleted, and keep the exact interval you typed.
- Mastery Goals no longer reloads your whole library as often, which was slow on big libraries.

## Changes

- The **Quick Menu** now supports eight customizable shortcuts, with new ones for Memories, Web Browser, Calculator, Stormbreaker and Map Shortcuts.
- Added a **Global Buttons** toggle to the **Quick Menu**.
- Picking a mapped shortcut's action is now a list grouped by category, and **X** clears a mapping. No more cycling through dozens of actions.
- Battery Saver is now called Standby. It didn't really save battery, as the services didn't use much power to begin with. It's useful if you are done achievement hunting and want to play Steam games but don't want the services running.
- Standby can be mapped to a button now.
- Snapshot is now a developer tool, and only shows up in the mapping list with **Developer Options** on. Don't get this confused with screenshots for memories. This is just a tool to take a picture of the CheevoDeck interface.
- New Sets & Revisions is now called Set Feed.
- Back and Exit prompts show in the Quick Access Menu footer.
- Shorter page titles: About, Mapper, History and Compare. This was in response to adding the **?** help button at the top of each page, which reduced the amount of room for the title itself.
- **B** when viewing tracked achievements for other games now goes back to the main page, just as going back when viewing the current game's tracked achievements.
- Cheevo Check now ships ARM64 versions of its tools, in preparation for ARM SteamOS support.

## Just a Heads-Up

- Your **Quick Menu** shortcuts have been reset just this one time with the new defaults. You can change them back to whatever you want.
- Your mapped button shortcuts are also reset once to the new defaults.
- Links open in CheevoDeck's browser now, with the exception of the credentials entry links.
- New snapshots (debug) save to **Pictures/CheevoDeck/Snapshots**. The ones you already have will not be touched.

## Fixes

### Cheevo Check

- A CHD inside a zip, 7z or rar now gets the same result as the loose disc.
- Fixed re-scanning a 7z or rar game saying it couldn't be read.
- Games in zips using Deflate64 compression can now be scanned.
- A password-protected archive no longer stalls a scan.

### Mastery Goals

- A bad response from RetroAchievements can no longer reset every goal card to zero.
- Switching accounts during a check no longer writes counts into the other account's goals.
- The goal-complete sound is no longer drowned out by the button press sound, remedied by simply adding a slight delay to the toast.
- Fixed game icons missing from an open goal after a plugin reload.
- Fixed the "No games match this filter" message getting cut off at the bottom of the screen.

### Tracked & Game Notes

- Achievements unlocked just before switching games are no longer missed. Their tracked rows clear, the unlock notification fires, and Mastery Goals updates.
- Note editors no longer act like everything is okay if a save ever fails.
- Fixed an achievement untracked or unlocked right after a reorder coming back in Tracked.
- Long game titles in Tracked Sets are no longer cut off.

### Leaderboards

- Fixed a leaderboard being forgotten if you closed the menu right after reopening it.
- With the Friends filter on, Top Players now counts your friends on the board instead of the whole board.
- New leaderboards show up within a day instead of three.

### Dolphin Mapper

- **B** on the controller step no longer closes the whole mapping and loses your edits.
- Changing a slot's controller type no longer keeps the old face button layout.
- Proper atomic saving to avoid any corruption scenarios.
- Settings toggles no longer say they saved when Dolphin's files weren't written, and no longer replace a linked config with a plain file.
- Dolphin config folders that an older version left locked are handed back to you automatically.

### Main Page & Profiles

- The main page no longer jumps down and back up when a new game loads.
- Tab buttons no longer stay dimmed while the cursor is on them.
- Button captions under the top strip are no longer cut off at the edge of the panel. Text is now centered to avoid this.

### Social

- A friend's avatar you fixed with **Resolve** no longer goes back to the wrong picture a couple of days later, making it a truly long-lasting solution.
- **X** and **Y** on the Friends list now work while the cursor is on a friend's star.

### Guides

- The glyphs and prompt text in the footer for the Guides page no longer wrap and have been simplified.

### File Watcher

- The time left estimate now shows up quickly on large files instead of taking minutes.

### Miscellaneous

- Fixed a situation where a game would show the previous game's icon.
- Fixed the emulator login toggle in the Switch User dialog showing its old setting.
- With Snapshot (Debug) mapped to the **Menu** button, invoking it inside a dialog no longer saves the dialog. It takes priority.
- Fixed the focus highlight going missing when opening the panel during a game.
- Selected buttons on a few pages showed a blue ring instead of the usual white one.
- Pages no longer open with the cursor on a dialog's button when that dialog had taken you out of the plugin.
- Game pickers no longer flash their **Cancel** button while the console list loads.

Alright, that's everything! I really hope you enjoy CheevoDeck as it has grown to not only just be a RetroAchievements tracker, but a RetroAchievements suite with all the tools achievement hunters will ever need to achieve their goals!

failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.name: CheevoDeck 0.9.1
failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.body:
This one is a follow-up to the quality of life improvements in 0.9.0 and aims to iron out those pesky bugs! Both Tracked and Notes pages had some strange behavior going on, but no worries, the infrastructure has improved drastically. I also added some very minor quality of life improvements as well, such as changing the formatting of Tracked and Game Notes categories. Now, by default, it no longer is in all caps and now matches whatever case you type. If you liked the old style, you are able to change it back in options. See below for more!

## Tracked Page

- Fixed the cursor vanishing after editing a note.
- Changing an item's tag now leaves the cursor in the category you were already in, instead of following the item over to its new one. If you're tagging a lot of items in one go, this saves you walking back to your place every time.
- Fixed the page shifting under you while you scroll up through categories.
- Notes are no longer cut off at 300 characters. The editor always let you type 500, so now it reflects that.
- The Completed tag no longer shows up in your tag suggestions.

## Game Notes Page

- The same cursor and page-shifting fixes as Tracked above.
- Changing a note's tag also leaves the cursor where you were instead of following the note.

## Options

- Added Formatting settings for header case. **Tracked Header Style** and **Notes Header Style** control your tag categories on those two pages, where Typed shows the tag exactly as you typed it. Capitalized shows the Steam default capitalized headers. Also, **General Header Style** covers every other header. View them in **Quick Menu** > **Options** > **Display & Notifications** tab under **Formatting**.

## Miscellaneous Fixes

- Fixed categories coming back collapsed when they should have been open. It only sorted itself out if you closed and reopened the panel, and it could happen on Tracked, Other Games, Game Notes and Dolphin Mapper.

Alright, I hope this helps improve your achievement hunting journey even more! I'm working on a very special new feature that will most likely be included in the next update. See you around!

failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.name: CheevoDeck 0.9.0
failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.body:
This is the biggest one yet! And it's all quality of life improvements across the board. Phew, where do I even begin? The most notable improvements are traversal. Now when you edit something, such as tracked notes, when you come back from the edit, you now land right back on the thing you edited; no more starting at the top of the page regardless.

## Tracked Page
- Custom tagged categories now sort alphabetically.
- Added the ability to expand and collapse tagged categories.
- Editing notes now lands you right back on the note you were editing in the list instead of moving you to the top of the page.
- Fixed an issue where reordering caused strange behaviors with the cursor.

## Game Notes Page
- Custom tagged categories now sort alphabetically.
- Added the ability to expand and collapse tagged categories.
- Category headers now show how many notes there are.
- Editing notes now lands you right back on the note you were editing in the list instead of moving you to the top of the page.
- Adding a new note will now select it once added to the list.
- Fixed an issue where reordering caused strange behaviors with the cursor.
- Added a button shortcut in the note editor to instantly mark the note as complete.
- Added a button shortcut in the note editor to delete the note; requires double-press.

## Dolphin Mapper
- Modified the expand/collapse buttons to be consistent with that of Tracked and Notes pages to declutter the UI.
- Editing mappings now puts you exactly where you left off before editing it; not at the top of the page.
- Adding a new mapping will now select the new mapping once added to the list. No more warping to the top of the page.
- Selecting the help button now lands you back on the help button when coming back from the help dialog.
- Fixed an issue where reordering caused strange behaviors with the cursor.

## File Watcher, SMB Shares, and Cheevo Check
- Improvements to traversal by remembering the last button when going from the page to a modal dialog.

## Guide Page
- Moved the exit button prompt and glyph to last, above the viewer. Since it wraps to the second row, this ensures people can see it.

## Main Menu
- Improved the aesthetics of the tabbed pane.
- Modified the collapsible control for Players Near You to be consistent with the changes above.

## Profile Page
- A green dot now shows next to your friend's status if they are online, based on if they were active within 15 minutes.

## Game Info Page
- Achievement Sort and Filter toggles now persist and remember your last settings.

## Miscellaneous Fixes
- Fixed lists that could stop growing while you scrolled.
- Fixed a small window where if A was pressed quickly after exiting a modal to a page, it would trigger odd behavior.
- Fixed issues where deleting a category's last mapping had undesired behavior.
- Fixed UTC dating anomalies.
- Fixed overly large button glyphs, specifically in notifications and comments.

This should really enhance your achievement hunting experience. Have at it, fellow cheevo hunters!

failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.name: CheevoDeck 0.8.8
failinator5000/decky-cheevodeck.body:
The folder chooser is the headline this time with a huge QOL update. CheevoDeck had been using Decky's chooser for **Cheevo Check**, **File Watcher**, patch downloads and update downloads for quite some time. I've written my own to replace it everywhere, which includes many user-friendly additions, such as better focus, prompt text support, and easily accessible buttons.

## What's New
- A more user-friendly folder chooser has been swapped in.
- The button prompts for comments, notifications, and a few other utilities that were hardcoded are now dynamic based on which controller you are using, and now show the proper glyph based on this. This now makes it consistent with the rest of CheevoDeck.
- The update notification now includes a select prompt for download/install options.
- Further made **Cheevo Check** more user-friendly.

- Added info text that shows in the intermediary loading window if connection to RA is weak.

lozazamastro/playhub-metadata.name: Version 1.8.0
lozazamastro/playhub-metadata.body:
This update adds flexible RPCS3 trophy detection for EmuDeck, custom emulator layouts, and serious background performance improvements.

## What's new
- A new **RPCS3 data folder** setting lets you point Playhub Metadata to an RPCS3 installation, `dev_hdd0`, `home`, user, `trophy`, or individual trophy-set folder.
- A controller-friendly folder picker is available directly in the existing RPCS3 card in the QAM.
- **Improved performance and reduced resource usage**. The plugin now performs less background work, uses fewer system resources, and feels smoother throughout Steam Gaming Mode.

## Improvements
- The first QAM opening now reuses the metadata cache created during plugin startup instead of downloading and applying the entire cache again.
- Library, achievement, RPCS3, and scraper settings are loaded in one bootstrap pass.
- The backend now reparses the large settings file only when its timestamp or size changes.
- Custom paths follow RPCS3 `config/vfs.yml` redirections, including EmuDeck layouts where `dev_hdd0` lives on another drive.
- The settings page reports whether the selected location is valid and how many trophy sets were found.
- Existing game-to-trophy associations are preserved when the RPCS3 data location changes.

## Fixes
- Fixed sluggish gamepad navigation during the first QAM opening on installations with large metadata and achievement caches.
- Invalid folders are rejected without replacing the last working configuration.

Existing metadata, credentials, imported achievements, trophy associations, and per-game settings are preserved.

lozazamastro/playhub-metadata.name: Version 1.6.0
lozazamastro/playhub-metadata.body:
## What’s Changed

* The plugin has been totally redesigned to better match the new design of the Playhub plugins.
* Added **local RPCS3 trophy support** for PlayStation 3 games, including trophy names, descriptions, grades, icons, unlock status and unlock dates.
* Added a new complete **RPCS3 trophy management workflow**:
  * Scan RPCS3 trophies
  * Sync all PS3 trophies
  * Clear RPCS3 associations
  * Automatically update PS3 trophies
  * Manually select the correct installed trophy set when automatic detection fails
* Added automatic **RPCS3 trophy detection after closing a PS3 game**, even when the game had no previous trophy association. This allows ISO-based games to be detected automatically after they have been launched at least once.
* Added a per-game **achievement source selector**:
  * Auto (default and suggested)
  * RetroAchievements
  * Xbox
  * PS3 (RPCS3)
  * Disabled
* Added **IGN metadata scanning** with global and per-game description language selection.
* Added automatic description translation into all the 194 Google Translate supported languages.
* Added **Steam Activity news and announcements** per-game enable/disable controls and manual Steam title matching.
* Added **Delete metadata** actions globally and for individual games, with a confirmation dialog before deletion.

## Improvements

* Improved RetroAchievements scanning by skipping unsupported platforms before hashing or contacting RetroAchievements:
  * Xbox
  * Xbox 360
  * PlayStation 3
  * GameCube
  * Wii
  * Wii U

IMPORTANT:
PS3 games stored as **ISO files must be launched at least once in RPCS3** before Playhub Metadata can detect and display their trophies. After the first launch, RPCS3 generates the local trophy data and Playhub Metadata can automatically detect it when the game is closed. If you're importing the games via Steam Rom Manager be sure to open at least one time RPCS3 and that all the games are visible in the emulator list.

danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.name: v0.0.7
danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.body:
FSR 4 on the Steam Deck, and the compatibility list is whole again.

### Added

- **FSR 4.1.1b — Steam Deck**, in the Basic upscaler dropdown. One choice
  downloads the community RDNA 2 build of the FidelityFX upscaler, checks it
  against a hash pinned in the plugin, puts it next to the game and switches on
  the INT8 override that reaches FSR 4 on RDNA 2. Close the game first; it
  applies on the next launch. Frame generation is left exactly as it was.
  Thanks to [@drewboardman](https://github.com/drewboardman), who built this and
  tested it on a Deck.
- Setup names which upscaler build is in the game folder, identified by its bytes
  rather than its version — the community build reports the same 4.1.1 the
  released SDK does — and will put the bundled one back.

### Fixed

- **297 of the 695 games on the compatibility list were answering "no wiki entry
  matched".** One row on the wiki was saved without its leading `|`, which the
  parser read as the end of the table, so everything after Metro Exodus was
  invisible: Monster Hunter Wilds, the Resident Evil entries, Stalker 2, The
  Witcher 3 and 293 others. A row that lost its first character is now read as
  the row it is. Bundled list regenerated — 698 entries.
- Games listed under *Upscaler mods support* and *Luma Unreal Engine* no longer
  claim OptiPatcher support they do not have, and their notes are their notes
  rather than the images column. Those two tables have one column fewer than the
  main one, and were being read as though they did not.
- The refreshed list adds Onimusha: Way of the Sword to the games that need
  REFramework in place before OptiScaler can do anything.
- All six FSR 4 quality presets are offered. The reference INI writes them as one
  comma-separated line, of which two were being read, so Quality, Performance,
  DRS and Ultra Performance were rejected by the settings writer and never
  reached the file.
- Choosing an FSR version on RDNA 2 no longer turns on the FSR 4 upgrade path.
  That path forces the FP8 model, which such a GPU does not have, and OptiScaler
  answers with a silent FSR 3 fallback.
- Verification recognises a community upscaler by hash, and reinstalling keeps it
  instead of overwriting it with the bundled build.
- Replacing the upscaler is atomic and rolls back the DLL, the INI and the
  manifest together if any part of it fails. It refuses while the game is
  running, and on an install this plugin did not make.

[0.0.7]: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler/releases/tag/v0.0.7

---

### Install

Decky Loader → gear icon → **Developer mode** → **Install Plugin from URL**, and paste:

```
https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler/releases/download/v0.0.7/Decky-OptiScaler-v0.0.7.zip
```

Or download the zip below and unpack it into `~/homebrew/plugins/`.

Everything from the `0.0.5.x-testing` prereleases, as one release.

### Added

- Non-Steam games can be set up. Their folder is taken from the shortcut's
  target, since Steam reports no install folder for them.

danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.name: v0.0.5.2-testing
danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.body:
A prerelease on the `testing` branch, fixing two games that 0.0.5.1-testing broke.
Bundled OptiScaler release is unchanged at 0.9.4.

### Fixed

- **Monster Hunter Wilds would not boot.** Its wiki page lays out three
  *mutually exclusive* install methods, and the settings miner read all of them.
  `LoadReshade=true` belongs to METHOD 3 — the arrangement where REFramework's
  dll is renamed to `ReShade64.dll` so OptiScaler loads it — and it was applied
  on top of METHOD 1's files, which is what this plugin installs. OptiScaler was
  told to load a `ReShade64.dll` that was not there while REFramework was already
  loaded through `dinput8.dll`. Settings are now read only from the part of a
  page describing the method actually performed; everything from the first
  "METHOD 2" or "Alternate Method" heading onward is ignored.
- **Resident Evil 2 was given 2× output scaling it never asked for.** The entry
  says "*If* applying Output Scaling is crashing the game, then ... set
  `Enabled=true` and the desired multiplier (*e.g.* `Multiplier=2.0`)" — advice
  for a problem you may not have, with an example number — and both keys were
  written unconditionally. A setting hedged by an "if", a "try", an "e.g." or a
  "desired" is no longer applied; it is reported instead, naming the word that
  made it a maybe. "Requires X, otherwise it crashes" is still an instruction,
  because a refusal is not free either.
- **The overlay moving to another key is said out loud.** Several REFramework
  entries ask for `ShortcutKey=0x24` because REF's own overlay is on Insert too.
  Applying it is right — doing it in silence meant Insert stopped opening the
  OptiScaler overlay and looked broken, when it had simply moved to **Home**. The
  plan now names the key to press, before it is written.
- **REFramework only installs `dinput8.dll`.** Its release notes ask for nothing
  else to go into the game folder, so the build stamp stays in the download cache
  and is recorded in the manifest instead.

### Changed

- **REFramework can be removed without removing OptiScaler.** It is required for
  these games to work, so it is still a compulsory step before the install — but
  it is also a 23 MB third-party DLL that hooks the engine and can stop a game
  booting, and an all-or-nothing install left no way to find out which of the two
  mods was at fault. It is a toggle once installed, and turning it off restores
  whatever `dinput8.dll` the game shipped with.
- **A missing `PDPerfPlugin.dll` is now a warning, not a quiet row.** Without it
  the Resident Evil entries do not upscale at all — while OptiScaler loads, live
  control connects and the frame rate reads out normally, which is exactly how
  this was reported. The setup now says in as many words that the panel will
  connect and report normally while nothing on screen changes.

---

### Install

Decky Loader → gear icon → **Developer mode** → **Install Plugin from URL**, and paste:

```
https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler/releases/download/v0.0.5.2-testing/Decky-OptiScaler-v0.0.5.2-testing.zip
```

Or download the zip below and unpack it into `~/homebrew/plugins/`.

danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.name: v0.0.5.1-testing
danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.body:
A prerelease on the `testing` branch. Bundled OptiScaler release is unchanged at
0.9.4.

### Added

- **Games that need REFramework are set up with it, automatically.** Nine
  entries on the compatibility list — the Resident Evil titles, Devil May Cry 5,
  Monster Hunter Wilds, PRAGMATA — say in prose that OptiScaler does nothing in
  that game unless [REFramework](https://github.com/praydog/REFramework) is
  already next to the executable, because REF is what exposes the upscaler the
  game will not expose itself. The plugin read straight past that: those games
  got an install that reported success, set the launch options, and changed
  nothing on screen, with no error anywhere to go looking for. The requirement
  is now read out of the entry, stated on the checklist before anything is
  written, and the right build is downloaded and installed with OptiScaler as
  one step.
- **The two REFramework builds are told apart, because they are not
  interchangeable.** praydog's nightly is one unified build for every game it
  supports; the pd-upscaler branch is built per game and is what the entries
  pairing REF with PureDark's UpscalerBasePlugin need, since that plugin does
  not support the unified build. Which one an entry wants is read from the entry
  itself — the pd entries name the branch and the plugin, the nightly ones do
  not — and only the per-game asset name is curated, because "RE2.zip" is not
  reachable from "Resident Evil 2 (2019)" by any matching rule and the wrong
  game's build is a crash on launch. A game with no known asset says so and
  links the release page rather than falling back to a near-enough one.
- **REFramework gets a `WINEDLLOVERRIDES` entry of its own.** For the same
  reason OptiScaler's proxy needs one: Proton ships its own `dinput8` and loads
  that in preference to the game folder. The wiki never mentions it — those
  pages are written for Windows, where the folder wins — which makes it the one
  instruction in the whole set-up that cannot come from the entry, and without
  it a set-up that followed the wiki to the letter would put REF in place and
  never load it.
- **`PDPerfPlugin.dll` is named rather than pretended about.** PureDark's
  UpscalerBasePlugin is on Nexus Mods behind a login, so nothing here can fetch
  it, and the pd-upscaler games do not work without it. It gets a row of its own
  on the checklist with the link, marked as the user's job, and ticks when the
  file turns up next to the executable — an install that reports success and
  leaves the game rendering exactly as before is the failure this whole feature
  exists to stop, and it would be absurd to reintroduce it one file further
  down.
- **REFramework can be added on its own,** to a game already set up or after a
  download that failed. A 13 MB download over a handheld's connection is the
  part that fails, and making somebody reinstall OptiScaler to retry it is a
  poor answer to a flaky network.

### Fixed

- **Wiki pages whose name contains brackets are downloaded again.** The
  compatibility list writes `[Resident Evil 2 (2019)](Resident-Evil-2-(2019))`,
  and the link parser stopped at the inner bracket: the page came out as
  `Resident-Evil-2-(2019`, which the wiki does not serve, so the detail page for
  every parenthesised title silently never downloaded. Those are exactly the
  Resident Evil entries whose settings — `Dxgi=false`, `OverlayMenu=false` — and
  REFramework instructions live on the page rather than in the notes column, so
  automatic set-up had been working from half an entry for them. Dead Space
  (2023) and Elden Ring were affected too.
- **The bundled compatibility list has been regenerated,** so an offline Deck
  gets the corrected page names rather than the truncated ones.

### Changed

- Anything REFramework installs goes through the same contract as every other
  file this plugin places: a `dinput8.dll` the game already had is set aside and
  put back on removal, and both REF files are in the manifest, so removing
  OptiScaler removes them too.

---

### Install

Decky Loader → gear icon → **Developer mode** → **Install Plugin from URL**, and paste:

```
https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler/releases/download/v0.0.5.1-testing/Decky-OptiScaler-v0.0.5.1-testing.zip
```

Or download the zip below and unpack it into `~/homebrew/plugins/`.

arcadalabs-jason/wifioptimizer.name: v0.24.7-beta
arcadalabs-jason/wifioptimizer.body:
Faster reconnect after sleep when the access point lock is on.

## Fixed

- Access point lock: waking up somewhere the pinned access point is weak or out of range no longer means a slow reconnect. The lock now moves to the clearly stronger access point before WiFi reconnects, instead of WiFi first joining the weak one and the lock moving a minute later, which dropped the connection a second time. On a Steam Deck OLED this took a reconnect after sleep from about 30 seconds down to about 12, with no second drop. Qualcomm ath11k cards only for now, as before.

## Improved

- Force reapply writes a line to the log saying which settings it found had stopped holding, plus the state of the WiFi link (power save, signal, speeds, retries, lost beacons), before it changes anything. If a stream goes bad and Force reapply fixes it, Copy diagnostics now shows what the link looked like just before.

VirusTotal scan of wifi-optimizer.zip: https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/b2ef3265d164dc160750d07a45821b0d53818b1c4ab3ea8e656e04ceefce4062

arcadalabs-jason/wifioptimizer.name: v0.24.6-beta
arcadalabs-jason/wifioptimizer.body:
Fixes from a second full review of the plugin, most of them for things that happen at the same moment as something else (a game launching, a wake from sleep, the auto-fix script running). If WiFi on a Steam Deck LCD stays dead after sleep, Copy diagnostics now shows more. Please keep sending them.

## New

- After a wake, if the access point lock holds you on a weak access point and a clearly stronger one of the same network is in range, the lock moves to it. Never during a game or stream, and for now only on Qualcomm ath11k cards such as the Steam Deck OLED's. The panel shows the move while it runs. Afterwards the lock's row says whether it moved, also when the WiFi card stops responding during the move. An access point that refused is skipped at later wakes until you change the lock.
- The top of the panel shows the connection: band and signal.
- The beta channel's "Go back to" no longer offers a release older than the last security fix, which is this one. Older releases still install from their zip.

## Fixed

- Reset, or turning a fix off, is no longer undone when a game launches or a stream starts at the same moment, or while the plugin is still starting up.
- Turning off network buffer tuning or CAKE, and uninstalling, can no longer be undone by the auto-fix script running at the same moment.
- Another account on the device can no longer hold up updates or the fixes by locking the plugin's lock files.
- Updates from this version on: when the updater can't tell whether a game is running, it waits instead of restarting Decky, and other Decky plugins or this plugin are never mistaken for a game or stream.
- Streaming auto mode: a custom app name that matches another Decky plugin, or the plugin itself, is no longer taken for a stream. Custom app names must be plain ASCII.
- The weaker access point and WPA2 notices work again with streaming auto mode off. They were broken since 0.24.4-beta.
- Force 6 GHz on NetworkManager 1.58.0 (SteamOS 3.9.5): the row only says a network needs WPA3 when a 6 GHz access point of that network is in range. It then says how to switch just that network: in Desktop Mode's network settings, set its security to WPA3 Personal. Until then the row shows the reason and stays off. Once you change it, the row updates within a minute. With no 6 GHz access point in range, turning it on says so.
- Allow WPA2, Force 5 GHz and Force 6 GHz on another network no longer move the access point lock off the network it was turned on for.
- A stuck WiFi command is no longer blamed on the access point or on the 6 GHz band.
- A process that can't be read, as happens with a stuck WiFi driver, no longer holds up the panel, streaming auto mode or updates.
- Ending a stream at the same moment as a game launch no longer leaves the fixes on.
- Streaming auto mode no longer turns the fixes off for a few seconds when the plugin restarts in the middle of a stream.
- Turning streaming auto mode on no longer turns the fixes on for a moment for an app you unticked.
- A lock, band, DNS, IPv6 or Allow WPA2 change made just before uninstalling is no longer left on your network, and uninstalling removes the settings folder even after an interrupted save.
- Bazzite and CachyOS: a WiFi backend switch cut short by a restart or power loss is finished or undone the next time the plugin starts.
- Bazzite and CachyOS: after a backend switch, uninstalling no longer leaves /var/lib/wifi-optimizer behind.
- With a USB WiFi adapter in use as well as the built-in card, power save is read and set on the card you're connected with, so Fix now, auto mode and Reset act on the right card.
- The panel stays responsive while the WiFi driver is stuck.
- Right after waking from sleep, the panel no longer says the WiFi card isn't responding while WiFi reconnects. A card that really is stuck is now shown even while WiFi still reads as connected, and with no WiFi card found the panel says so instead of asking for a restart.
- Steam Deck LCD: the plugin only turns off the WiFi card's PCIe power saving once WiFi power save is confirmed off. The two together are what can leave the card stuck.
- The auto-fix script can no longer be held up by a stuck WiFi command, or made to skip its fixes by another account's process.
- The auto-fix script no longer waits on a stuck process search, and no longer takes a WiFi command started a moment earlier for a stuck one and skips its fixes.
- While the WiFi card isn't responding, CAKE is no longer reported as changed, and turning it off no longer says it was removed.
- Turning Prevent lag spikes off puts the card's PCIe power saving back the way it was, also when the auto-fix script ran at the same moment.
- The plugin log no longer contains your network's name when NetworkManager reports an error.
- Copy diagnostics no longer mixes up its sections when a network has a name like "info" or "device".
- Copy diagnostics and the plugin log also hide hardware addresses inside device names (USB adapters, docks) and the names of VPN devices.
- Copy diagnostics ignores log lines other programs write under the plugin's name.
- Save diagnostics no longer collects everything a second time, and no longer says it saved a file that only holds an error.
- Dismissing a failed Move or Allow WPA2 message no longer hides the next notice.
- Move the lock says so when it finds no clearly stronger access point, instead of showing an error.
- Move the lock and Allow WPA2 also say when they worked.
- Force reapply all shows its result under the button, refusals included.
- When an update can't start, for example while Decky restarts, the panel says so at once instead of waiting 15 minutes.

## Improved

- Copy diagnostics: the kernel's warning lines from a failed wake are kept, the log window is the wake that failed rather than the last one, and the driver settings in force at startup are recorded every time.
- Copy diagnostics also records the BIOS version and date.
- When WiFi doesn't come back after a wake, the plugin log records the WiFi card's power and PCIe state at that moment, so Copy diagnostics after the restart still shows it.
- When the WiFi card stops responding, the panel says to restart first; Copy diagnostics afterwards still shows the failure.
- Streaming auto mode says on every card what it does to the driver settings between streams. On the Steam Deck LCD that includes the ones that help WiFi come back after sleep.
- Before the plugin reconnects WiFi or scans on its own, every built-in streaming app counts as a stream, ticked or not. Otherwise, with streaming auto mode on only the ticked apps count, and with it off every built-in app does. Custom app names count only while auto mode is on.
- The panel no longer says fixes are paused when none are on, shows the WiFi region by name instead of a code, names controls the way the panel labels them, and points to Copy diagnostics when nothing else helps.
- Show details is now at the bottom of the panel, next to Copy diagnostics, so the panel starts with status and Optimize Safe.
- The Reset confirmation is shorter and says what Reset turns on and off, the WiFi region included.
- The Allow WPA2 notice is shorter and shows the end of the access point's address, so you can check it is yours. The README has the details.
- Notices and descriptions are shorter, and the lock and band say a reconnect takes up to half a minute.
- Under iwd, the access point lock and Force 5 GHz can't be turned on and say why.
- If the plugin's settings folder is behind a link, the panel says so instead of asking you to free storage. The notice goes away once the folder is fixed.
- If the plugin's settings file can't be read, the panel says to tap Reset settings instead of restarting.
- The WiFi region message no longer calls a region chosen earlier the card's own.
- CAKE's description says its effect on built-in WiFi cards is small.
- The README explains what stays in force when you disable the plugin in Decky: power save, the driver settings, and the lock, band, DNS and IPv6 on your networks. To test without the plugin: Reset, disable, restart.
- The README says to tap Reset before uninstalling, since Decky can stop the plugin before its uninstall finishes.
- Security problems can be reported privately with Report a vulnerability on the repository's Security tab.

## Allow WPA2: what Reset and uninstall can undo

- Since 0.24.5-beta the plugin keeps a record of every network you use Allow WPA2 on, so Reset and uninstalling put those networks back to WPA3 only.
- Allow WPA2 turned on with an earlier version was never recorded, so Reset and uninstall can't tell those networks apart from ones SteamOS saved as WPA2 itself, and leave them as they are.
- Installing 0.24.4-beta or older (the install command installs 0.24.3 until the next stable release) and then updating again also loses the record. The networks keep working either way. To put one back to WPA3 only by hand:

  ```
  sudo nmcli connection modify "NAME" 802-11-wireless-security.key-mgmt sae
  ```

  where NAME is the network's name as `nmcli connection show` lists it. Only do this for a network that was WPA3 only before you used Allow WPA2.

VirusTotal scan of wifi-optimizer.zip: https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/d98e6173fb6e9b0114c04baf744814f636fa6720ac1da2b598e4f8dee01c2d92

arcadalabs-jason/wifioptimizer.name: v0.24.5-beta
arcadalabs-jason/wifioptimizer.body:
A big round of fixes from a full review of the plugin. If WiFi on your Steam Deck LCD doesn't come back after sleep, this is the build to try: Copy diagnostics now shows what the driver was set to during the boot that failed, which is what's needed to track it down.

## Fixed

- Bazzite and CachyOS: switching the WiFi backend back to wpa_supplicant could leave no WiFi until a reboot on most non-Realtek cards (Legion Go, ROG Ally and others). The plugin now brings the WiFi interface back. Reset and uninstall after an iwd switch also turn wpa_supplicant back on, so WiFi still works after the next boot.
- Updates: an update that has to restart Decky now waits for a game or stream to end before it does, and a stuck update no longer holds the panel for minutes.
- The plugin no longer hangs when the WiFi card stops responding (for example after a bad wake). Commands that get stuck are not started again.
- Reset turns everything off first and keeps track of any network it couldn't reach, and retries it. Uninstall does its most important steps first, inside the time Decky allows.
- Custom DNS now covers IPv6 too, so the router's DNS is no longer used alongside yours.
- Allow WPA2: the banner no longer claims something NetworkManager on SteamOS 3.8 doesn't do, it is only offered when it's safe, and Reset and uninstall now put WPA3 back (see below).
- Disabling the plugin in Decky now stops the auto-fix script from applying changes at every connect. Its power save setting stays in force until you tap Reset, so tap Reset before disabling.
- Copy diagnostics no longer includes a Bluetooth device's address, the device name or part of an IP address.
- A USB WiFi adapter is no longer mistaken for the built-in card.

## Improved

- Copy diagnostics shows the boot where WiFi failed: the driver settings in force at that boot, the WiFi card's PCIe power state, and the kernel and NetworkManager lines around the last sleep, kept even when the log is flooded with errors.
- The panel says why WiFi isn't connected (radio off, card not responding, NetworkManager asleep) and what to do next, shows which WiFi region the card is really using, and its messages and explanations match what the plugin does.
- Every setting's explanation can be opened with a controller.
- The WiFi region list has more countries and a "Not managed" option.

## Allow WPA2: what Reset and uninstall can undo

- From this version the plugin keeps a record of every network you use Allow WPA2 on, so Reset and uninstalling put those networks back to WPA3 only.
- Allow WPA2 turned on with an earlier version was never recorded, so Reset and uninstall can't tell those networks apart from ones SteamOS saved as WPA2 itself, and leave them as they are. The README has the command to put one back to WPA3 only by hand.
- Going back to an older version loses the record too. If you go back to 0.24.4-beta or older (that includes running the install command, which installs 0.24.3 until 0.24.5 is out) and then return to this version, Reset and uninstall no longer know which networks you allowed WPA2 on, and leave them as they are. The networks keep working either way. To put one back to WPA3 only by hand:

  sudo nmcli connection modify "NAME" 802-11-wireless-security.key-mgmt sae

  where NAME is the network's name as `nmcli connection show` lists it. Only do this for a network that was WPA3 only before you used Allow WPA2.

## Known issues in this beta

- If a game launches or a stream starts at the same moment you tap Reset, some fixes can come back on. Tap Reset again.
- Right after waking from sleep, "The WiFi card isn't responding" can show for a moment while WiFi reconnects. If WiFi comes back, ignore it.
- In streaming auto mode, the driver settings that only apply when the WiFi driver loads are left out between streams. The panel says so for the Steam Deck LCD, but it applies to other cards too (ROG Ally, Legion Go, Intel).

VirusTotal scan of wifi-optimizer.zip: https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/d962ea176fec4c6e006b13545d9d351488ff1a3da7ebb78ba1e386727818ad8f

xxjsonderuloxx/decky-optiscaler.body:
Decky OptiScaler v0.3.0 Release Notes

Major Refactoring & UI Improvements

This release represents a complete overhaul of the Decky OptiScaler plugin, focusing on maintainability, user experience, and advanced configuration options.

New Features

INI Preservation System
- Added INI preservation toggle - Prevent OptiScaler from overwriting your custom game configurations
- Smart conditional UI - Advanced settings (Frame Generation Type & OptiScaler Settings) are now hidden by default and only appear when INI preservation is disabled
- Cleaner default experience - New users see a simplified interface, power users can access advanced options

Enhanced Non-Steam Games Support  
- Dedicated Non-Steam Games section with comprehensive setup instructions
- Multiple DLL options with detailed descriptions (dxgi.dll, winmm.dll, dbghelp.dll, etc.)
- SteamOS-optimized instructions - Removed clipboard references for better handheld compatibility

Improved Status Display
- Consolidated status messages - No more redundant "Mod Not Installed" + "OptiScaler Not Installed" 
- Clear single message when not installed: "OptiScaler Mod Not Installed"
- Detailed info when installed - Shows both installation status and current version
- Conditional Update button - Only appears when OptiScaler is actually installed

Complete Code Refactoring

Modular Component Architecture
- Broke down massive 2000+ line index.tsx into manageable components:
  - FGModInstallerSection.tsx - Installation and updates
  - InstalledGamesSection.tsx - Game selection and patching  
  - NonSteamGamesSection.tsx - Non-Steam game instructions
  - PreserveIniSection.tsx - INI preservation settings
  - OptiScalerFGTypeSection.tsx - Frame generation type settings
  - OptiScalerSettingsTabs.tsx - Advanced OptiScaler configuration
  - PluginUpdateChecker.tsx - Plugin update management
  - SettingsSections.tsx - Shared settings components

Code Cleanup
- Removed unused scripts and legacy assets
