nico8324/couchlink.name: v0.4.0 — StreamLink is now CouchLink
nico8324/couchlink.body:
**StreamLink is now CouchLink.** The old name clashed with the unrelated
[streamlink](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink) project, and the plugin's Python package
(`py_modules/streamlink`) shadowed that project's import name.

### Upgrading — read this

Decky treats this as a **new plugin**, not an update:

1. Remove **StreamLink** on *both* devices (Decky → gear → StreamLink → uninstall).
2. Install [`CouchLink.zip`](https://github.com/Nico8324/CouchLink/releases/latest/download/CouchLink.zip) on both.
3. **Pair again** from the Deck. An old host and a new client can't discover each other — the `/ping`
   identity string changed with the name.

### Also in this release

* The update check finally works. Every release up to 0.3.0 shipped with the feed URL pointing at a
  placeholder repo, so the plugin never saw a new version.
* Store listing image is the project's own rather than the plugin template's banner.
* `LICENSE` keeps the plugin template's original copyright, as the Decky store requires.

Nothing else changed: same wake/sleep/auto-sleep behaviour, same host API, same
[known limitations](https://github.com/Nico8324/CouchLink#known-limitations-read-this) (S5 wake still
doesn't work on the Steam Machine — use Sleep).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Nico8324/CouchLink/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

nico8324/couchlink.name: v0.3.0 — approve-on-host pairing, away mode, stream stats
nico8324/couchlink.body:
Install on **both** devices: Decky → gear → General → Developer mode → Developer → **Install Plugin from Zip** → `StreamLink.zip`.
Then pair once from the Deck (*Pair host…* → *Find hosts on this network* → **Allow** on the host's screen).

### New

* **Approve-on-host pairing** — discover the host, tap it, press **Allow** on the host's own screen. No typing a token (manual entry kept as a fallback).
* **"Leaving home" mode** — keep the host awake for streaming over the internet, and restore your sleep settings when you're back.
* **Stream session stats** — fps, bitrate, ping and slow stages parsed from Steam's `SessionStats`, shown on both panels.
* **Update check** against a configurable JSON feed; the Deck warns when host and Deck versions differ.

### Changed / fixed

* The host is matched in Steam's device list by its hostname (learned at pairing) instead of a fixed name.
* The client tolerates non-JSON replies from the host API.

### Known limitations

Wake from a full power-off (S5) does **not** work on the Steam Machine — a firmware limitation
([SteamOS#2735](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/SteamOS/issues/2735)). Use **Sleep**. Wake also only works on your
own LAN; use *Leaving home* before you go out. Details in the [README](https://github.com/Nico8324/StreamLink#known-limitations-read-this).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Nico8324/StreamLink/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0

koua29/savewaypoint.name: v0.2.0 — Sync your non-Steam saves to your own GitHub
koua29/savewaypoint.body:
First stable release. SaveWaypoint finds the game saves nothing else is backing up — emulators, GOG/itch titles, anything you added to Steam as a non-Steam shortcut — and syncs them to a **private repo on your own GitHub account**. No server of ours, no subscription, and because every backup is a commit, your version history comes free.

### What it does

- **Finds saves on its own.** Known emulator locations, plus a scan of Proton prefixes. Each entry is rated by what is actually in the folder: 🟢 detected (a `SaveGames` folder or `.sav` files are there), 🟡 probable, 🔴 nothing saved yet.
- **Leaves Steam games alone.** Steam Cloud already syncs them and a second writer racing it helps nobody, so they are filtered out — switchable, for the games Cloud does not cover.
- **Signs in from your phone.** GitHub device flow: the Deck shows a short code, you approve it on your phone. No keyboard, no browser on the handheld.
- **Test before you trust it.** Checks a save can be archived *and* written back, without uploading anything.
- **Restore any earlier backup** from the commit history.
- **Updates itself**, on a stable or beta channel.

### Getting started

1. Create a GitHub OAuth App and tick **Enable Device Flow** (see the README).
2. Paste its Client ID, press **Connect GitHub**, approve on your phone.
3. **Manage saves…**, switch on what you want, then **Back up now**.

### Known limitation

Backing up is proven on a Steam Deck and the archives were verified to hold real save data. **Restoring has not yet been exercised on a device.** The code path is tested, but before you rely on it, do a dry run: back up a save, then restore the copy you just made.

### Install

Download `SaveWaypoint.zip` below, then on the Deck in Desktop mode:

```bash
unzip -o SaveWaypoint.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```

drewboardman/decky-wifi-guard.name: Wi-Fi Guard v0.1.0
drewboardman/decky-wifi-guard.body:
Wi-Fi Guard pauses Steam downloads while connected to a chosen Wi-Fi network and restores downloads when leaving, while preserving pre-existing pauses.

- Event-driven Steam network and download subscriptions: no periodic polling, pings, or active Wi-Fi scans.
- Native Decky panel with current-network selection, an editable SSID, and a master switch.
- Pure decision algebra, small effect interfaces, and separate Steam/Decky/storage/NetworkManager adapters.
- Fault containment for callbacks, async operations, React rendering, startup, and cleanup. Bounded event processing and operation deadlines stop automatic protection on unexpected faults; recovery requires an explicit retry.
- Atomic settings and pause-ownership persistence for reload recovery.

Validation: 53 automated tests, TypeScript checking, production build, and archive validation. Live Steam Deck acceptance (including sleep/wake and native API compatibility) still requires on-device testing. The frontend shares Steam's process; plugin-level fault containment cannot guarantee against native Steam or OS crashes.

Install by extracting the ZIP's `Wi-Fi Guard` directory into `~/homebrew/plugins/` on the Deck and restarting Decky, or use the ZIP asset URL with Decky's developer “Install Plugin from URL” option. Remove the unpublished `Wi-Fi Download Guard` prototype first if previously sideloaded, and configure the SSID again.

`SHA256SUMS` contains the checksum for the installable ZIP. See the repository README and architecture document for recovery behavior and scope.

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
### Added

- **The builder on the AYN Thor's bottom screen, under Armada OS.** A new *Bottom screen* section in the Quick Access panel puts the builder on the Thor's second screen, by touch, while you play on the top one. It shows the team, the selected line, and the details of whichever Digimon you tap, with the same edits as the builder: *I'm here*, change branch, evolve, devolve, remove, lock, reorder, and start a new line from a stage-by-stage grid.
- **Both screens stay in step.** An edit on either one shows up on the other at once: the bottom screen waits on the plugin for changes rather than polling, and the plugin tells the Steam UI when the bottom screen saves.
- **Kind to the OLED.** With no touch for two minutes the bottom screen dims, and after ten it goes black. The touch that wakes it doesn't press anything.

### Notes

- The bottom screen is drawn natively: the plugin borrows the panel from gamescope as a DRM lease and draws it with the system's Python and cairo, the way Panel de Control's bottom screen does. Armada's own bottom-screen desktop is paused while it's on, and comes back when it's switched off.

- **And on the branch picker.** Each option in *Change* / *Evolve* lists the personality it arrives with next to its requirements, which is the moment you're actually choosing between branches.

### Notes

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.name: v1.2.0 — track where each line is, and what's next
danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
### Added

- **Mark where you are in a line.** Each evolution line can now carry the stage you've actually reached: press **Y** on a Digimon in the builder (or use *I'm here* in its details modal) and it's badged **NOW**. Pressing Y on the marked stage again clears it, as does *Clear the current-stage mark* in the line's ⋮ menu. The mark works on locked lines too — the lock protects a line's members, and where you've got to isn't one of them.
- **A *Next up* view in the Quick Access panel.** The panel now switches between two views: *Lines*, the team overview it has always shown, and *Next up*, which gives each line the evolution it's working towards and the Agent Rank, stat, item or Jogress requirements to get there — the thing you actually want mid-battle. Pressing **Y** on a line there marks that evolution as reached without opening the builder.

### Notes

- Lines with no mark are read as sitting on their first stage, and say so, so *Next up* is useful before anything has been marked.
- Share codes are unchanged, and stay byte-for-byte compatible with the website: the mark is a note about your save, not part of a team plan, so it doesn't travel in a share code.

### Install

Download the zip below and install it from **Decky → gear icon → Developer → Install Plugin from File**, or unzip it into `~/homebrew/plugins/` and restart `plugin_loader`.

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.name: v1.1.0 — team overview in the Quick Access panel
danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
### Added

- **The Quick Access panel is now a team overview.** Opening the plugin from the Decky menu lists every evolution line with its name, how many stages it has, whether it's locked, and its sprites — so the team is readable without leaving the game.

### Changed

- **Opening a line from the overview lands on the line.** Pressing A on a line in the panel still jumps to the builder, but focus now starts on that line's first Digimon in the detail panel on the right instead of on the team list, so the d-pad carries on from where you were pointing. Opening the builder with *Open Team Builder* still starts in the team list.

### Install

Download the zip below and install it from **Decky → gear icon → Developer → Install Plugin from File**, or unzip it into `~/homebrew/plugins/` and restart `plugin_loader`.

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.name: v1.0.1 — gamepad navigation fixes
danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
Fixes for d-pad navigation, so focus moves the way things are actually laid out on screen.

### Fixed
- **Sidebar buttons move by position** — left from *Clear* now lands on *Share* beside it, instead of jumping to *Add line* at the top of the other column.
- **Moving between the two panels** — d-pad right off a line's ⋮ enters the evolution line, and left off the first Digimon goes back to the team list.
- **Focus highlight no longer clipped** at the top edge of the evolution line panel.
- **Digimon details modal opens at the top**, instead of already scrolled down to the remove button.

Full notes in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-builder/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install
Download the zip below, copy it to your Deck, then **Decky menu → gear → Developer → Install Plugin from File**.

```bash
unzip "decky-digimon-sts-team-builder-v1.0.1.zip" -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```

infernokun/syncdeck.name: SyncDeck 1.2.1
infernokun/syncdeck.body:
Security fixes. Recommended for anyone using the PC auto-add option.

- The PC's Syncthing API key was being written to the plugin log in plain text. It no longer is. If you set up the PC option on an earlier version, clear ~/homebrew/logs/SyncDeck/ and consider regenerating the key in your PC's Syncthing.
- Folders that hold credentials (~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, and Decky's own directory, which contains this plugin's settings file) can no longer be picked as a save folder.
- Hardened the systemd unit the plugin writes for Syncthing autostart against unusual directory names.
- A corrupt appinfo.vdf no longer empties the game list.

The README now has a Security section describing how API keys are handled, what the plugin will not touch, and the fact that the connection to your PC's Syncthing does not verify TLS because its certificate is self-signed.

koua29/decky-stwebsrv.name: v0.3.0-beta.1 — Created and modified dates, sortable columns
koua29/decky-stwebsrv.body:
**Test build**: the file list now shows **when each file was created and last changed**, and every column can **sort the folder**.

## What's new
- 📅 **Two new columns**: **Created** and **Modified**, with the date and the time.
- ↕️ **Sorting**: click a column heading — Name, Size, Created, Modified — to sort the folder; click it again to reverse the order. Folders stay on top. Your choice follows you into the next folders and is remembered for your next visits.
- 📱 **On a phone**: the Created column is hidden and only the day is shown, so the file names keep their room.
- ❓ **`—` instead of a date**: the creation date is read from the filesystem (through `statx`), and some of them simply do not record it. The modification date is always there.

## How to update
STWebSRV panel → Options → **Beta versions** on → **Check for updates**. Settings are kept.
To go back to the stable version, turn **Beta versions** off and reinstall 0.2.0 from the [Releases](https://github.com/koua29/decky-stwebsrv/releases) page.

## Download
**`STWebSRV.zip`** — Decky Loader plugin for SteamOS.

koua29/decky-stwebsrv.name: v0.2.0 — Verified uploads, Add to Steam, steam_appid.txt
koua29/decky-stwebsrv.body:
**STWebSRV 0.2.0 is the new stable version.** Everything tested in the betas is now on the stable channel: sending big files without fear, choosing which address the QR code shows, adding a program to your Steam library from the web page, and creating the `steam_appid.txt` file some games need.

## What's new since 0.1.0

### Uploads you can trust
- 📦 **Resumable, verified uploads**: files are sent in 8 MB chunks, each checked with CRC32 and sent again if it arrives damaged. If the network drops, the upload retries by itself; if you close the page, sending the same file again resumes where it stopped.
- 🛡️ A file only gets its real name once complete and its checksum verified, so **an existing file is never damaged**. Free space is checked before starting, and abandoned uploads are cleaned up after 24 hours.
- 📊 **Transfer progress**: for each file and for the whole batch — sent / total, percentage, **speed** and **time left**, with a **Cancel** button.

### Your library, from the browser
- ▶️ **Add to Steam**: a button on programs (`.exe`, `.bat`, `.msi`, `.sh`, `.AppImage`…) creates a **non-Steam game shortcut**, without restarting Steam. Editable name, **Proton turned on by default for Windows programs**, optional launch options, Linux programs made executable if needed. A notification shows up on the console; tapping it opens the game's page.
- 🆔 **`steam_appid.txt`**: some Steam games started from a non-Steam shortcut do not launch without this file. The **ID** button in the toolbar creates it in the open folder, and a checkbox creates it next to the program in "Add to Steam". Type the App ID, the **game's name** (searched on the Steam Store) or a Store link; for a DLC the page offers the base game's ID.

### Several networks at once
- 🌐 Ethernet + Wi-Fi, USB dock: the server answers on **all** of them. Each address is shown with its type (Wired, Wi-Fi, Other), **wired first**, and the **Address shown** menu picks the one used for the QR code. The choice is remembered; unplug that adapter and the automatic order comes back.

## How to update

### From v0.1.0 or a beta (built-in updates)
1. Open STWebSRV in the Decky menu and press **Check for updates** (bottom of the panel).
2. Press **Update to 0.2.0**.
3. Decky shows its confirmation window, checks the zip's checksum and reloads the plugin.

Beta users get this version too, and can turn **Beta versions** off to stay on stable from now on.

### If your panel has no "Check for updates" button: install by hand, once
An older build can't update itself. Install 0.2.0 over it:
1. Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Decky → ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL**, paste this link and confirm:
   ```
   https://github.com/koua29/decky-stwebsrv/releases/latest/download/STWebSRV.zip
   ```
   Or download `STWebSRV.zip` below and use **Install plugin from ZIP file**.
3. From then on, new versions show up right in the panel.

Your password and settings are kept either way.

## Download
**`STWebSRV.zip`** — Decky Loader plugin for SteamOS (Steam Deck, Legion Go, ROG Ally…).

koua29/decky-stwebsrv.name: v0.2.0-beta.4 — Create steam_appid.txt
koua29/decky-stwebsrv.body:
**Test build**: the web page now creates the **`steam_appid.txt`** file that some Steam games need to start from a non-Steam shortcut.

## What's new
- 🆔 **"ID" button** in the toolbar: creates `steam_appid.txt` in the open folder. Clicking an existing `steam_appid.txt` opens the same window.
- 🔎 **Three ways to name the game**: its Steam App ID, its **name** (searched on the Steam Store) or a **Store link**. The game's name is shown so you can catch a typo.
- 🧩 **DLC**: if the ID belongs to a DLC, the page offers the base game's ID, which is the one the game expects.
- ▶️ **With "Add to Steam"**: a checkbox also creates the file next to the program.
- 🛡️ An existing file is only replaced after confirmation; an ID unknown to the Store also asks first. Without Internet, the ID can still be written.

Reminder: the file must be in the folder the game starts from (usually the one holding the .exe), Steam must be running and your account must own the game.

## How to update
STWebSRV panel → Options → **Beta versions** on → **Check for updates**. Also includes what's new in betas 1 to 3. Settings are kept.

## Download
**`STWebSRV.zip`** — Decky Loader plugin for SteamOS.

koua29/decky-stwebsrv.name: v0.2.0-beta.3 — Resumable, verified uploads with transfer progress
koua29/decky-stwebsrv.body:
**Test build**: big files are now sent **in verified chunks**, the upload **resumes after a connection drop**, and the page shows **the amount sent, the speed and the time left**.

## What's new
- 🔁 **Resumable uploads**: the file is sent in 8 MB chunks. If the network drops, the page retries by itself (up to 8 times, waiting longer each time). If you close the page, **send the same file again**: the upload resumes where it stopped.
- 🛡️ **No damaged files**:
  - each chunk is checked with **CRC32** and sent again if it arrives damaged;
  - the server refuses any chunk that would leave a gap or overlap another one;
  - before resuming, the page checks that the part already received matches the local file, otherwise the upload starts over;
  - the file only gets its real name **once complete and its checksum verified**: an existing file with the same name stays intact until then.
- 📊 **Transfer progress**: for each file and for the whole batch, **amount sent / total**, percentage, **speed** (5 s average) and **time left**, then a summary at the end.
- ✋ **Cancel** button (deletes what was already sent of the current file), and a warning if you close the page during an upload.
- 💾 **Free space** is checked before starting; abandoned uploads are deleted after 24 hours.
- 🇫🇷 Sizes in Mo / Go on the French page.
- Also includes what's new in betas 1 and 2: **Add to Steam** and **address choice** (wired / Wi-Fi).

## How to update
With **Options → Beta versions** on: **Check for updates** → **Update to 0.2.0-beta.3**. Settings and password are kept.

## Download
**`STWebSRV.zip`** — pre-release, for testing.

koua29/decky-stwebsrv.name: v0.2.0-beta.2 — Choose the address when the console has several networks
koua29/decky-stwebsrv.body:
**Test build**: when the console is connected **by cable and Wi-Fi** (or through a USB dock), the panel shows each address with its type, puts **the wired one first**, and lets you **choose the address used for the QR code**.

## What's new
- 🔌 **Several networks**: each address is shown with its type (**Wired**, **Wi-Fi**, **Other** for VPNs or containers). The faster wired connection comes first.
- 🎯 **"Address shown" menu** (when there are several addresses): Automatic (cable first) or a specific adapter. The choice is remembered; if that adapter is unplugged, the automatic order comes back.
- 🧪 Also includes what's new in 0.2.0-beta.1: **Add to Steam** from the web page.

The server still answers on every network: this setting only changes the address shown and the QR code.

## How to update
With **Options → Beta versions** on: **Check for updates** → **Update to 0.2.0-beta.2**. Settings and password are kept.

## Download
**`STWebSRV.zip`** — pre-release, for testing.

rayekkk/ayaneo3companion.body:
### ✨ Added

**TDP**
- Game profiles like on the Legion, per game and optionally with separate battery and charger values.
- Global keeps a game's profile unused instead of deleting it.
- CPU energy preference (EPP) next to CPU Boost, globally or per game and charger state; Uninstall restores
  both.

**Fan**
- Your own fan curve with eight points from 0 to 100°C in the fan's own percent, three starting curves
  (Silent, Balanced, Aggressive) and a full-screen editor.
- The graph shows the live temperature and measured RPM; below 10% the fan stops, and the 100°C point never
  goes below 40%.
- Optionally a curve per TDP preset: Silent, Balanced, Performance and Custom can each use their own, others
  use the global one.
- A separate watchdog returns the fan to the console's automatic curve if Companion stops, crashes or the
  console goes to sleep, and sets full speed at 100°C even if Companion is frozen.
- A fan that does not spin up or stop as asked turns Fan Control off and shows the reason.

### 🔧 Changed

**TDP**
- New presets measured on the console: Silent 10/15/20, Balanced 15/25/30 and Performance 30/43/45 W
  (SPL/SPPT/FPPT); Custom goes from 5 W up to the Performance ceilings.
- Minimum, Low power and Max are gone: Low power becomes Silent, the others keep their limits as Custom.
- The firmware lowers SPL to 28 W whenever the charger is plugged in or unplugged, so Companion now writes
  the limits again after every change and after sleep.
- RyzenAdj is kept outside the plugin folder, so updates no longer download it again.
- **Show details** shows the package power draw.

**Display**
- **Restart Gaming Mode** on the OLED Display page when gamescope has not loaded the current definition
  yet.

**Panel**
- Navigation like LegionGo2Companion: icons on every row, the row you came from is selected again, and a
  page stays open when Quick Access closes or a menu opens.
- Status reads pause while the Companion tab is hidden.
- Each row says how old its values are while a refresh is retried.

**Lighting**
- RGB is now called Lighting.

**Logs**
- A private diagnostic log in `/var/log/ayaneo3companion` limits repeated messages to one a minute, and
  Decky's own plugin logs are pruned to the newest ten.

**Plugin**
- Helper programs no longer inherit Decky's bundled libraries.
- Decky 3.2's stop hang no longer delays restoring the hardware.
- The background monitors no longer rescan every device twice a second, and the controller's memory is
  written once per change.

### 🐛 Fixed

**TM Guard**
- After an accidental TM button press it now recognises the mode and brings the controller back in
  about ten seconds by briefly cutting its power; before, it never noticed TM mode.
- The power cut also clears an arrow key that leaving TM mode could leave held.
- After three tries it asks you to press TM until the light is white instead of restarting the
  controller again and again.
- A USB keyboard with the same chip no longer sets it off.

**Buttons**
- LC1 and RC1 work again after TM mode, because TM Guard programs their bindings again.
- LC/RC no longer show up in Steam as LC1/RC1; all four buttons appear under their own names.
- With Fix Key Binding on, the button table sends the firmware's own QAM key; the previous one never
  opened the menu.
- Uninstall and Install Plugin from ZIP no longer leave LC1/RC1 silent while the switch shows them
  enabled.

**Display**
- The OLED display definition now lives in `~/.config/gamescope/scripts`, which SteamOS updates keep;
  before, an update removed it and the screen stayed washed out until a restart.
- Turning the display definition off now asks for the Gaming Mode restart it needs and puts back a
  definition Companion had replaced.
- The HDR fix can be switched on again while SteamOS's own display profile is in use.
- The overview no longer shows 800 nits before the display has been read.

**Lighting**
- Your lighting and vibration are kept on first install: Companion shows what the controller already
  uses and changes nothing until you do; Uninstall puts back what it found.

**Install**
- Speaker-calibration and display backups move to `/home/.ayaneo3companion-backups`, so they survive
  SteamOS updates.

**Audio**
- Speaker tuning in the background never interrupts playback and stops retrying when the tuning does not
  take.

**TDP**
- A change right after plugging in the charger no longer leaves 28 W.
- A CPU Boost change during a profile switch no longer loses the game's profile.
- CPU Boost and EPP are left to PowerStation while it runs.
- **Retry** appears when the RyzenAdj helper breaks while running.

**Fan**
- Fan Control no longer takes the fan from another fan tool at startup.
- An edited curve can still be saved after Fan Control turned off on an error.

**Battery**
- Uninstall turns charge bypass off whenever the hardware has it on, even when the saved settings say
  otherwise.

**Magic Modules**
- **Reset Magic Modules** works again after a module was pushed back in after Eject.

### 🗑️ Removed
- **Fan:** the fixed 60–100% manual speed and its systemd timer; a manual speed left by an earlier version is returned
  to automatic.

### ✨ Added
- **Fan:** see the fan's speed in RPM, keep the console's automatic curve, or choose a manual speed from 60% to
  100%, when supported by the console's kernel.
- **Fan:** an independent timer restores automatic control if Companion stops responding; stopping the plugin or
  resuming the console also returns the fan to Auto.

### 🔧 Changed

**Panel**
- Faster startup and smoother menus; speaker checks, slow settings saves and other background work are
  less likely to hold up unrelated controls.
- Reopening a page or quickly switching games no longer piles up repeated battery and profile checks;
  Companion refreshes the page or game you are currently using.
- Temporary read failures are shown alongside the last confirmed values and clear after a successful
  refresh, while separate failed actions keep their own explanation.

**Downloads**
- Update and hardware-helper downloads have time limits.

**Updates**
- An update installs the exact version shown in the menu.

**Plugin**
- Companion uses newer AYANEO system controls when available and keeps the fallback needed by older
  SteamOS kernels.

### 🐛 Fixed

**TDP**
- Changing games quickly no longer lets the previous game's response replace the current game's preset or
  power limits.
- Saving or deleting a profile while reopening the menu no longer brings back the old preset or incorrectly
  re-enables Per Game Profile.
- Custom values and the selected preset survive closing and reopening the menu for the same game, and failed
  preset changes preserve unsaved edits.
- Rapid slider changes followed by Apply use the latest values, including the extra power allowed for short
  boosts.
- When PowerStation controls TDP, Companion explains why its own TDP controls are unavailable, retries
  pending game profiles when control is released, and keeps other hardware controls usable.
- A temporary profile lookup failure retries automatically, and its error clears after recovery without
  hiding an unrelated failed action.

**Fan**
- Auto remains available during slow TDP or audio operations and after a temporary fan status failure, and
  its status can be read on kernels that do not allow reading manual speed in automatic mode.
- Rapid manual fan changes and delayed responses no longer interfere with monitoring the latest setting.
- The safety timer can still restore Auto if Companion gets stuck, and retries when the fan interface is
  unavailable.
- Moving the manual fan slider and immediately pressing Apply uses the latest speed.

**Battery**
- Read failures no longer leave a spinner running indefinitely or silently present old readings as
  current; the error clears once readings are available again.
- Charging bypass is checked independently of TDP, including after plugging in a charger or resuming
  the console.

**Lighting**
- Fast changes to color, brightness, vibration strength and FF Gain no longer overwrite one another,
  and the latest choices are kept when leaving the page.

**Controller**
- Failed controller changes restore the previous settings, and vibration tests wait for pending
  adjustments and never run with unconfirmed values.
- Saved FF Gain is restored after startup, resume or controller reconnection, waiting for the
  built-in controller instead of using an external pad.
- Unavailable controller features are clearly marked and recover when the required interface
  returns.

**Magic Modules**
- Power, RGB and vibration settings are recovered more reliably after removal, reinsertion, or
  startup with the controller powered off.

**Audio**
- Speaker setup no longer delays unrelated controls, and recalibration becomes available after both
  speakers are confirmed ready.

**Display**
- The OLED fix and key-binding switches remember your choice and restore their system files when a
  SteamOS update replaces them.

**Buttons**
- InputPlumber is reloaded only when its button mapping needs to change.

**Install**
- The desktop installer handles folders with spaces and special characters.
- Installation finds the correct Decky folder, checks the full update package and verifies that the
  required services start.
- Failed installations restore the previous plugin and button mappings, and if recovery cannot finish
  safely, the backup files are kept for repair.

**Updates**
- Incomplete update packages are rejected, and concurrent installations cannot replace each other's
  files.

**Settings**
- Settings and calibration tools better protect existing files from accidental replacement.

**Plugin**
- Shutdown handles unfinished work more reliably.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Settings**
- Complete settings are committed atomically with a last-good recovery copy, and unsafe paths or
  unreadable settings are refused instead of overwriting your choices.

**Controller**
- Hardware writes stay serialized through cancellation and plugin shutdown, and the previous setting
  is restored when a write or save step fails.
- Hardware write readbacks are verified, partial button-map changes are recovered, and repeated
  interface failures back off while resume and drift recovery stay in place.

**TDP**
- Edits captured for a game that is no longer active are rejected.

**Lighting**
- Pending RGB and vibration changes are preserved when closing a page, rapid slider changes are
  merged, and stale status replies no longer revert saved controls.

**Panel**
- Native dropdown selections stay on their current page, confirmed overview and update results are
  retained, and overlapping or hidden status polls stop.
- Delayed app notifications are cleared on unload, and temporary profile lookup errors recover without
  reopening the menu.

**Updates**
- The exact GitHub release ZIP is validated, including its SHA-256 digest and archive contents;
  downloads are published atomically and duplicate checks or downloads are avoided.

**Audio**
- Audio-session and gamescope EDID paths are resolved from the Decky user account, including accounts
  with names or UIDs other than deck/1000.

**Display**
- EDID status reads are bounded, and a failed calibration-history save is reported separately from a
  completed hardware calibration, keeping the recovery backup path.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Controller**
- AYANEO vendor-HID writes are verified against the firmware's current report and retried when
  stale.
- FF_GAIN is restored whenever the physical rumble input node is recreated, and virtual or unrelated
  external controllers are ignored.

**Lighting**
- RGB or vibration settings that drift after startup, resume or controller-device recreation are
  repaired automatically.
- RGB, firmware vibration and FF_GAIN changes go through one queue, so rapid adjustments cannot
  overwrite one another with stale controller state.

**Magic Modules**
- Ejection is isolated from background recovery and plugin unload, and controller settings are
  restored after a real module reconnection without an unnecessary firmware save or mechanical reset.

**Display**
- The original public Gamma 2.2 OLED definition is recognized as Companion-owned.
- Unknown existing definitions now require explicit replacement confirmation and are backed up and
  verified before the Companion definition is installed.

### ✨ Added
- **TDP:** a persistent CPU Boost switch on the TDP page, restored after startup.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Controller**
- AYANEO vendor-HID commands retry the complete transaction after an unanswered request instead of
  repeatedly waiting on a command that was already lost.
- The proposed kernel `hid-ayaneo` sysfs interface is detected, and competing direct-HID commands are
  blocked instead of racing the kernel driver.

**Magic Modules**
- A timed-out eject leaves controller power enabled, so an incomplete latch movement is not
  interrupted by the power cut.

**Display**
- A successfully changed OLED display definition stays enabled when gamescope's temporary EDID file
  cannot be normalized at the same time; the background monitor retries without reporting the switch as failed.
- Display-definition removal no longer blocks Decky, and definitions not owned by AYANEO 3 Companion are
  not removed.

wolfg1969/retroarch-ai-translate.name: v1.0.0 — RetroArch AI 实时翻译服务
wolfg1969/retroarch-ai-translate.body:
RetroArch AI Translation 的首个正式发布版本。在 RetroArch 模拟器上按快捷键，即可将游戏截图中的日文实时翻译为中文，并以画面叠加层显示。支持 Docker 多用户部署和 Steam Deck Decky 插件。

## 核心功能

- **Vision LLM OCR + 机器翻译**：截图 → 视觉模型识别日文 → 翻译模型输出中文，延迟约 1 秒
- **画面叠加层**：翻译结果以半透明底色 + 白色中文文字渲染在游戏画面上，自动识別角色名和对话
- **LRU 翻译缓存**：智能裁剪截图边缘（排除光标/状态栏），相同对话不重复翻译
- **游戏专属配置**：YAML 格式的术语表、角色语气、标志性台词、场景模式，翻译风格贴合原作
- **多设备独立**：Docker 模式下通过 IP 区分不同 RetroArch 客户端，各自选择不同游戏

## 内置游戏配置

逆转裁判（gyakuten）、火焰纹章（fire_emblem）、塞尔达传说 缩小帽（zelda_minish）、弹丸论破（danganronpa）

## Web 管理界面

浏览器打开 `http://localhost:4404/`：
- 首页：切换游戏配置，实时生效
- API 设置：配置 OCR / 翻译 API 密钥，保存后无需重启

## Steam Deck 插件

通过 Decky Loader 在 QAM 中直接管理：
- 启动 / 停止翻译服务
- 切换游戏、配置 API 密钥、查看实时日志
- 开机自动启动

## 部署方式

| 方式 | 适用场景 |
|------|----------|
| Docker Compose | NAS / 家庭服务器，多用户共享 |
| Python 直接运行 | 本机，与 RetroArch 同机 |
| Decky 插件 | Steam Deck，QAM 一键管理 |

## 许可证

GPLv3


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/wolfg1969/retroarch-ai-translate/commits/v1.0.0

rayekkk/deckyeq.name: DeckyEQ 1.1.0
rayekkk/deckyeq.body:
### ✨ Added

**Panel**
- The main screen holds **Enable EQ**, **Volume boost**, **Preset**, the curve, and **Bass**,
  **Treble** and **Stereo width**; **Save** and **Discard** appear there while the sound has unsaved changes.
- Rows under **More** open **Equalizer**, **Presets**, **Output** and **About**, each with a
  one-line summary; **B** goes back one page and the row you came from is selected again.

**Curve editor**
- Drag a dot of the curve up or down, or press **A** and use the D-pad: **←/→** choose the
  band, **↑/↓** change it in 0.5 dB steps, **X** sets it flat.
- **Edit full screen** shows the curve larger with the preset list, **Five sliders**,
  **Save**, **Discard** and **Done**; there **LT/RT** make a band wider or narrower and **Y** changes its
  filter type.

**Five sliders**
- Five sliders instead of ten, each moving two neighbouring bands; switching never changes
  your sound, and the choice belongs to this console, not to a preset.

**Games**
- While a game runs, **Own sound for <game>** gives it its own preset and edits, which come
  back whenever the game runs.
- **Presets → Games with their own sound** lists them with a **Forget** button; up to 200 games
  are kept.

**Volume boost**
- Up to +12 dB more for every preset and game, for speakers that are too quiet at full
  volume.

**Stereo width**
- From mono (0%) to twice as wide (200%), applied live.

**Limiter**
- An always-on limiter turns loud peaks down smoothly instead of letting them crackle, so boosts
  can stay loud; the bass has its own limiter, so a bass hit no longer turns down voices.

**Presets**
- New built-in presets **Clear voices** (brings dialogue forward), **More bass** (fuller low end)
  and **Legion Go 2** (a speaker tuning made by ear from the Legion Go S preset; choosing it also sets
  **Volume boost** to 9 dB).
- **About this preset** describes each built-in preset.
- Every preset uses the same ten bands, 31.5 Hz to 16 kHz, so the sliders and dots stay the same
  whichever preset you pick.

### 🔧 Changed

**Updating from 1.0**
- A band's frequency can no longer be changed; a band you moved in 1.0 keeps its own
  frequency and is named by it, and only its gain (in full screen also its width and type) changes.
- Going back from 1.1 to 1.0 may fail to read settings that use stereo width or other
  1.1-only settings, so export your presets first.

**Volume and output**
- Steam's volume and output stay untouched; the equalizer is now a WirePlumber smart
  filter in front of the output you choose, and the volume slider and buttons work exactly as without EQ.
- DeckyEQ no longer sets your speakers to 100%, changes the default output or moves
  streams; when Steam plays to another output, EQ waits (**Standby**).
- If the filter stops, playback continues on the output at your volume.

**Output**
- While EQ is on, Steam lists **DeckyEQ** as an output; choosing it is the same as choosing the
  output EQ applies to.
- Requires WirePlumber 0.5 or newer (SteamOS 3.7 and newer).
- **Speaker port only** is now **Speakers only**, and **Output** holds just **Apply EQ to** and
  **Speakers only**.
- **Refresh / reconnect EQ** is now **Reconnect EQ**.

**Headroom**
- The **Automatic headroom** switch is gone; headroom is always on and lowers the level only
  for EQ boosts above +6 dB, leaving the rest to the limiter.
- Most presets play louder than in 1.0, and presets that had the switch off may play slightly
  quieter (the Go S preset by about 0.6 dB); your **Input level**, **Volume boost** and stereo width are never
  taken back.

**Bands**
- Band frequencies are fixed and the frequency slider is gone; in full screen a band's width and
  filter type can still be changed.

**Presets**
- Import and export sit under **Show import or export** in **Presets**: **Export this sound**,
  **Export your presets** and **Export this sound to…**.
- **Save as new…** starts with the current preset's name, and a repeated name gets " (2)".
- **Legion Go S · Original** is now called **Legion Go S**.

**Panel**
- The **View** dropdown is gone.

**Updates**
- Only a ZIP that a GitHub Actions run in this repository uploaded to a release is offered; releases
  carry a build-provenance attestation that `gh attestation verify` can check.

**Messages**
- Errors stay on the page that caused them and also appear as a toast; outcomes such as an export
  path appear as a toast.
- While EQ is not live, the pages say why.

**Performance**
- No CPU is used while nothing plays; the filter sleeps with its output, and with EQ off DeckyEQ
  no longer runs audio tools in the background.

**Install**
- The plugin ZIP is about 200 KB instead of 2.7 MB.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Volume**
- In 1.0 the speakers could stay at 100% when Decky crashed, when you picked the speakers in Steam,
  or after headphones or Bluetooth came and went; DeckyEQ no longer touches volumes.
- A volume that 1.0 still owed is restored once at startup when its device returns.

**Bluetooth**
- Playback no longer moves to the speakers when you turn EQ on.

**Switching**
- The filter starts and stops flat and then moves to your settings, so turning EQ on or off is
  smooth.

**Stability**
- A slow audio tool (for example while a game loads) no longer pauses EQ, and a PipeWire restart
  rebuilds the filter.
- A filter that keeps failing retries after 8, 16, 32 and then 60 seconds instead of constantly.

**Errors**
- A change that cannot be applied puts back the previous sound, and a change lost in transit keeps
  its notice instead of silently reverting.

**File pickers**
- Import and Export to a folder open again after an earlier error, and closing the picker is
  no longer reported as an error.

**Presets**
- **Edited** no longer flickers on Flat, and Delete and Discard act on the preset they were opened
  for.

**Updates**
- A Downloads folder that is a link, read-only, full or not writable gets its own message.
- After a download About says **Ready to install**, and partial downloads left by an interrupted
  run are removed.

**Settings**
- Damaged settings fall back to the last good copy.
- Preset names with invisible characters that broke saving are refused, and frequencies where
  PipeWire's filters become unstable snap to 20 Hz or 20 kHz.

**Startup**
- DeckyEQ refuses to run as root, which would lock you out of your own settings.

**Unloading**
- Unloading no longer stalls on Decky 3.3.

### ✨ Added

**Plugin**
- First public release.

**Equalizer**
- Ten bands, with changes applied while audio plays.

**Tone**
- **Bass** and **Treble** sliders, each from -9 to +9 dB.

**Filters**
- Bell, low shelf or high shelf for each band, with gain, frequency and width.

**Presets**
- Your own presets, up to 64; update, rename, copy, delete or revert to the saved sound.
- Built-in presets Flat and GAZuOOT's community **Legion Go S · Original**.

**Import and export**
- Single sounds or the whole library as JSON files, to `~/Documents/DeckyEQ/` or a
  folder you choose.

**Drafts**
- Your latest edits survive closing the menu or restarting Decky.

**Input level**
- With optional automatic headroom for boosts.

**Output**
- Output selection, with **Speaker port only** bypass on by default.

**Volume**
- The physical output is set to 100% and your volume moves to the virtual **DeckyEQ** output, and
  back when EQ is turned off.

**Panel**
- A compact panel with a **View** dropdown for **Equalizer**, **Presets**, **Output** and **About**.

**Updates**
- Check GitHub for a newer release and download its verified ZIP to your Downloads folder.

branchingjade/reboot-to-windows.name: Reboot to Windows 1.0.1
branchingjade/reboot-to-windows.body:
## 中文

**修复：点了「重启进 Windows」只排队、不重启。**

- **根因**：Decky Loader 是 PyInstaller onefile 程序，它给插件进程注入的 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 指向自己的 `/tmp/_MEIxxxx/` 解包目录，里面自带一个旧版 `libcrypto.so.3`。插件后端以 root 直接调用 `/usr/bin/systemctl reboot` 时，动态加载器发现系统 `libsystemd-shared` 需要 `OPENSSL_3.4.0`，`systemctl` 在联系 logind **之前**就中止了：

  ```
  /usr/bin/systemctl: /tmp/_MEI.../libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.4.0' not found
  (required by /usr/lib/systemd/libsystemd-shared-257.7-*.so)
  ```

  `efibootmgr` 不依赖 OpenSSL，所以设置 `BootNext` 一直成功 —— 于是只有一次性启动项被写好、机器却从不重启，面板看起来就像"已排队"。旧代码用裸 `Popen`、不读退出码，错误被完全吞掉还返回成功。
- **修复**：所有特权子进程（`efibootmgr` / `systemctl`）一律剥掉 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`、`LD_PRELOAD`、`LD_AUDIT`、`LD_DEBUG`；重启改为回收子进程并校验退出码，直连失败自动回退 `sudo -n`（sudo 自身会清理环境），真失败以 `reboot_failed` 上报面板，不再假装成功。
- 面板新增 `reboot_failed` 的中英文案（中文：「重启命令没有生效，本次切换未完成」）。

**验证（SteamOS 213 实机，Decky Loader v3.2.10-pre1）**

- 复现对照：`LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/_MEI… systemctl --version` → rc=1 同一报错；剥掉该变量 → rc=0。
- 部署后把 reboot 换成探针脚本实测：父进程 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 有毒时，子进程拿到的是干净环境；换成不存在的二进制时返回 `{'ok': False, …}` 而不是成功。
- 用 Decky 自己的 `loader/reload_plugin` 重载后端：新进程以 root 启动，日志 `loaded (euid=0, …, rule=already present)`。

---

## English

**Fix: pressing "Restart into Windows" only queued the switch and never rebooted.**

- **Root cause**: Decky Loader is a PyInstaller one-file build. It exports `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` pointing at its own `/tmp/_MEIxxxx/` bundle, which ships an older `libcrypto.so.3`. When the root plugin backend called `/usr/bin/systemctl reboot` directly, the dynamic loader saw that the system's `libsystemd-shared` needs `OPENSSL_3.4.0` and aborted **before** `systemctl` ever reached logind:

  ```
  /usr/bin/systemctl: /tmp/_MEI.../libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.4.0' not found
  (required by /usr/lib/systemd/libsystemd-shared-257.7-*.so)
  ```

  `efibootmgr` does not use OpenSSL, so writing the one-shot `BootNext` kept succeeding — the boot entry was set, the machine never restarted, and the panel looked like it had merely "queued" the switch. The old code used a bare `Popen`, never checked the exit status, and reported success anyway.
- **Fix**: every privileged child (`efibootmgr` / `systemctl`) now runs with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_AUDIT` and `LD_DEBUG` stripped; the reboot command is reaped and its exit status checked, a failing direct exec falls back to `sudo -n` (sudo sanitizes the environment itself), and a real failure is reported to the panel as `reboot_failed` instead of a silent success.
- The panel gained a localized `reboot_failed` message in Chinese and English.

**Verified** on the real SteamOS 213 machine (Decky Loader v3.2.10-pre1) — reproduction, env-stripping probe, failure reporting, and a backend reload through Decky's own `loader/reload_plugin` route.

branchingjade/reboot-to-windows.name: Reboot to Windows v1.0.0 — 一键切到 Windows 11（一次性）/ one-shot switch
branchingjade/reboot-to-windows.body:
# Reboot to Windows v1.0.0

[English below](#english)

## 简体中文

Decky Loader 插件：在 SteamOS 游戏模式下**一键重启进入 Windows 11**，而且只生效一次 ——
下次开机自动回到 SteamOS，不会把机器卡在 Windows 里。

### 功能

- 面板一键切换：把 UEFI 的**一次性**启动项（`BootNext`）指向 Windows 引导条目，随后立即重启。
- **一次性**：`BootNext` 用完即清，下一次开机仍是正常的启动顺序（SteamOS）。
- 重启前有确认弹窗；误触了也能在面板里**取消**已排队的切换。
- 面板显示引导状态：是否存在 Windows 引导条目、是否已排队。
- **中英双语面板**，默认中文，可在面板里切换，选择会被记住。
- 自我修复：后端重建免密 sudo 规则，SteamOS 镜像更新抹掉 `/etc/sudoers.d/*` 后不会失效。

### 权限说明（重要）

Decky 3.x 默认把插件后端跑成桌面用户（`uid 1000`），这个身份不能写 UEFI 启动项。
因此本插件在 `plugin.json` 中声明了 `"flags": ["root"]`，Decky 会把后端以 **root** 启动
（已实测：后端进程 euid=0）。这样即使免密 sudo 规则被 SteamOS 更新抹掉，插件下次加载也会自己写回。

### 安装

1. 下载本页的 **RebootToWindows.zip**。
2. Decky → 设置 → 通用 → **从文件安装插件**，选择该 zip。
   （也可以解压到 `~/homebrew/plugins/reboot-to-windows/` 后重启 Decky。）

### 前置条件

机器是 Windows + SteamOS 双系统，且 Windows 引导条目编号为 `Boot0000`。
如果不是，请修改 `main.py` 里的 `WINDOWS_BOOT_ENTRY`。

配合 Decky Loader v3.2.10-pre1 实测通过：`status()` 返回
`{"ok": true, "has_windows": true, "boot_next": null, "is_root": true}`。

---

## English

A Decky Loader plugin that reboots a SteamOS machine **into Windows 11 with a single click** — as a
*one-shot* switch, so the next boot returns to SteamOS automatically.

### Features

- One click in the panel: points the UEFI **one-shot** boot variable (`BootNext`) at the Windows
  entry and reboots immediately.
- **One-shot by design**: `BootNext` is consumed on that boot, so the following power-on uses the
  normal boot order (SteamOS).
- A confirmation dialog before rebooting, and the queued switch can be **cancelled** from the panel.
- The panel reports the boot state: whether a Windows entry exists and whether a switch is queued.
- **Bilingual panel** (Chinese default, English), switchable and remembered.
- Self-healing: the backend recreates its passwordless sudo rule, so a SteamOS image update wiping
  `/etc/sudoers.d/*` no longer breaks it.

### Privileges (important)

Decky 3.x starts plugin backends as the desktop user (`uid 1000`) by default, which cannot write the
UEFI boot variables. This plugin therefore declares `"flags": ["root"]` so Decky starts the backend
as **root** (verified on-device: backend euid=0). That way, even if the passwordless sudo rule is
wiped by a SteamOS update, the plugin writes it back on its next load.

### Install

1. Download **RebootToWindows.zip** from this release.
2. Decky → Settings → General → **Install Plugin from file**, pick the zip.
   (Or unzip it into `~/homebrew/plugins/reboot-to-windows/` and restart Decky.)

### Requirements

A Windows + SteamOS dual-boot machine where the Windows entry is `Boot0000`. If yours differs, change
`WINDOWS_BOOT_ENTRY` in `main.py`.

Verified on-device with Decky Loader v3.2.10-pre1: `status()` returns
`{"ok": true, "has_windows": true, "boot_next": null, "is_root": true}`.

garicst/autowhite.name: AutoWhite 1.0.0
garicst/autowhite.body:
Первый публичный выпуск. / First public release.

**Возможности / Features**

- Автоматическая подстройка точки белого по датчику освещённости (ALS) через виртуальную
  точку белого gamescope — `GAMESCOPE_DISPLAY_VIRTUAL_WHITE` (CIE 1931 x/y).
  / Ambient-light adaptive white point driven through gamescope's virtual white point.
- Плавное сглаживание перехода: тик 0.2 с, опрос датчика раз в 1 с, мёртвая зона 0.0005 —
  без рывков и ступенек. / Smooth exponential transitions — no jumps.
- Применение сразу при старте консоли; при выключении возвращается нейтральная D65.
  / Applied at boot; disabling restores neutral D65.
- Панель: тумблер, ползунок «Холоднее — Теплее», статус (освещённость и текущая точка).
  / Panel: toggle, Cooler — Warmer slider, live status.
- Русский и английский интерфейс — автоматически по языку системы.
  / Russian and English UI, picked from the system language.
- Самодостаточность: нужны только Decky Loader, `xprop`, `runuser`, gamescope и ALS.
  / Self-contained: Decky Loader, `xprop`, `runuser`, gamescope, ALS.
- Самовосстановление: точка белого сверяется каждые 5 с, поэтому сброс после перезагрузки
  консоли или чужое вмешательство исправляются автоматически.
  / Self-healing: the white point is verified every 5 s, so a reset after a reboot or an
  external change is corrected automatically.
- Кнопка **«Проверить обновление»** в панели: спрашивает у GitHub последний релиз.
  / **Check for updates** button in the panel: asks GitHub for the latest release.
- Переносимость: пользователь сессии берётся из `DECKY_USER` (не жёстко «deck»),
  X-дисплей определяется автоматически, поддерживаются разные названия каналов датчика.
  / Portability: the session user comes from `DECKY_USER` (not a hard-coded `deck`),
  the X display is auto-detected, and several ALS channel names are supported.

**Установка / Install**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GaricST/AutoWhite/main/install.sh | sh
```

**Проверено на / Verified on:** Lenovo Legion Go 2 (SteamOS), датчик `als` в
`/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device1`.

**Зависимости / Requirements:** Decky Loader, gamescope, `xprop`, `runuser`.

**Лицензия / License:** MIT.

bassobr/decky-wowup.name: v0.2.0
bassobr/decky-wowup.body:
A central full-screen view, removing addons, and sorted addon suggestions.

### What's new
- **Central full-screen view** (Quick Access menu → Open WoW Addons), laid out like Steam's settings:
  - **Installed**: update, check, or remove addons for each WoW version.
  - **Get addons**: search and suggestions.
  - **WoW versions**, **Undo**, **WowUp-CF** and **Notes** (warnings and diagnostics).

  The Quick Access menu keeps an overview, **Update all** (now for every WoW version at once) and the plugin update.
- **Remove addons**: deletes their folders and WowUp records like WowUp does.
  - Required dependencies that no other addon needs can be removed along with an addon.
  - Folders another addon still uses are kept.
  - Folders WowUp does not manage can be removed too.
  - A snapshot is taken first, and **Undo** puts removed addons back.
- **Sort addon suggestions and search results** by best match, popular, most downloads, most favorites
  (WoWInterface), recently updated or name. Results show favorites and the date of the last update.
- WowUp's own `wowup_data_addon` folder is no longer listed as "not managed".

### Update
Offered inside the plugin (Quick Access menu → Maintenance), or run `install.sh` again:

```bash
curl -sL https://github.com/bassobr/decky-wowup/raw/main/install.sh -o /tmp/wow-addons-install.sh && sudo bash /tmp/wow-addons-install.sh
```

### Integrity
`SHA256SUMS` is signed with minisign (key `5FB2410E9B9A14EB`, [`minisign.pub`](https://github.com/bassobr/decky-wowup/blob/main/minisign.pub)); `install.sh` and the in-app updater verify it:
`minisign -Vm SHA256SUMS -p minisign.pub`

Unofficial – not affiliated with WowUp, CurseForge/Overwolf or Blizzard Entertainment.

bassobr/decky-wowup.name: v0.1.1
bassobr/decky-wowup.body:
Fixes a case where WowUp-CF installed addons into a folder the game no longer uses.

### What's new
- WowUp installations whose folder is gone or holds only `Interface/AddOns` (e.g. a deleted Proton prefix
  of an old Battle.net shortcut) are marked and never updated: WowUp would otherwise recreate the folder
  and install addons there, where the game never loads them.
- **Move to the installed game** (Quick Access menu and "WoW versions"): points such an installation at the
  detected WoW folder, keeps its addon list, copies the addon folders and replaces an empty entry for the
  same folder. The old folder is left untouched. CLI: `relocate <installation id> <folder>`.
- Leftover AddOns folders are no longer detected as WoW versions.

### Update
Offered inside the plugin (Maintenance → Check for plugin update), or run `install.sh` again:


bassobr/decky-wowup.name: v0.1.0
bassobr/decky-wowup.body:
First release of **WoW Addons**, a Decky plugin that updates World of Warcraft addons from Game Mode by driving [WowUp-CF](https://github.com/WowUp/WowUp.CF) headlessly.

### What's in it
- Headless WowUp-CF runs from Game Mode (`gamescope --backend headless`): update all, check only,
  update a single addon; flags and notification setting restored after each run (journal).
- Detects every WoW version in Battle.net Proton prefixes (`product.db`, `.build.info`) and lets
  WowUp import the missing ones.
- Installs, adopts and updates the WowUp-CF AppImage with checksum verification and a canary run.
- Hardlink snapshots before each update with "Undo last update".
- TOC compatibility check against the installed game version.
- Signed releases, `install.sh`, in-app plugin updates via Decky Loader.
- Full-screen "Get addons" page: search WoWInterface and WowUp Hub (popular/featured without a query),
  install from CurseForge by project ID, open WowUp-CF's own window for CurseForge search; installs run
  through WowUp-CF, required CurseForge dependencies are added automatically.
- Progress bar no longer pushed to the right (raw ProgressBar instead of ProgressBarWithInfo).
- WoW versions from every route: Steam/Proton (incl. NonSteamLaunchers), Bottles, Lutris, Heroic, Wine,
  CrossOver, search folders, SD cards/USB drives and folders picked by hand; added to WowUp directly in
  WowUp's own format (no duplicates with WowUp's own import). New full-screen page "WoW versions".

### Install
With Decky Loader installed, open Konsole in Desktop Mode:

```bash
curl -sL https://github.com/bassobr/decky-wowup/raw/main/install.sh -o /tmp/wow-addons-install.sh && sudo bash /tmp/wow-addons-install.sh
```

Then open the Quick Access menu → Decky → WoW Addons. Later versions are offered inside the plugin.

### Integrity
`SHA256SUMS` is signed with minisign (key `5FB2410E9B9A14EB`, [`minisign.pub`](https://github.com/bassobr/decky-wowup/blob/main/minisign.pub)); `install.sh` and the in-app updater verify it:
`minisign -Vm SHA256SUMS -p minisign.pub`

Unofficial – not affiliated with WowUp, CurseForge/Overwolf or Blizzard Entertainment.

branchingjade/boot-volume.name: BootVolume v1.4.0 — 睡眠唤醒修复 + 中英双语面板 / resume fix + bilingual panel
branchingjade/boot-volume.body:
# BootVolume v1.4.0

[English below](#english)

## 简体中文

Decky Loader 插件：**SteamOS 开机动画播放期间自动压低系统音量**，动画结束后恢复原值。
本版本加入了「睡眠唤醒后第一次启动动画」的修复，并把面板做成中英双语（默认中文）。

### 新增

- **睡眠唤醒后的第一次启动动画也会被压低。** 之前插件只在 Decky 自身加载时、以及
  `steamwebhelper` 的 pid 变化时触发；而唤醒后那次动画是同一个 Steam UI 进程在放（pid 不变），
  所以插件根本没被触发，表现就是「长时间睡眠后第一次开机动画不响、第二三次才正常」。
  现在通过 `time.time() - time.monotonic()` 的差值跳变检测 resume，唤醒后立刻开压。
- **中英双语面板**，默认中文，可在面板底部切换，选择会被记住。

### 优化与修复

- 开压前不再扫描全部 17 个动画文件（冷缓存下会拖慢约 1 秒），改用加载时测好的时长，
  动画开头几秒不再漏压。
- 压低期间每秒复查一次音频输出：唤醒后重新枚举出来的 USB / HDMI 设备（满音量）也会被一起压低，
  结束时正确还原。
- 音频图未就绪时短暂重试，不再直接报 `no hardware sinks found` 退出。
- 面板「当前输出」显示真实的默认输出及其音量（带设备名）。

### 安装

1. 下载本页的 **BootVolume.zip**。
2. Decky → 设置 → 通用 → **从文件安装插件**，选择该 zip。
   （也可以解压到 `~/homebrew/plugins/` 后重启 Decky。）

配合 Decky Loader v3.2.10-pre1 实测通过：开机压低 3 路输出到 40%、保持 14.01 秒后原样还原。

---

## English

A Decky Loader plugin that **lowers the system volume while the SteamOS boot animation plays** and
restores the previous values afterwards. This release fixes the first startup movie after a resume
from sleep and makes the panel bilingual (Chinese by default).

### Added

- **The first startup movie after a resume from sleep is ducked.** The plugin used to trigger only on
  Decky's own load and on a `steamwebhelper` pid change, but the movie played right after a resume
  comes from the *same* Steam UI process, so nothing fired — hence "the first boot animation after a
  long sleep is quiet, the second and third are fine". The resume is now detected from the jump in
  `time.time() - time.monotonic()` and the duck starts immediately.
- **Bilingual panel** (Chinese default, English), switchable at the bottom of the panel and remembered.

### Improved / fixed

- No `ffprobe` scan on the hot path (it delayed the duck by ~1 s with a cold cache): the duration
  measured at load time is reused, so the first seconds of the animation are covered.
- The sink list is re-checked once per second during the duck, so USB/HDMI outputs re-enumerated at
  full volume after a resume are ducked too and restored correctly.
- Briefly retry when the audio graph is not up yet instead of logging `no hardware sinks found`.
- The panel's "current output" now shows the real default output and its volume, with the device name.

### Install

1. Download **BootVolume.zip** from this release.
2. Decky → Settings → General → **Install Plugin from file**, pick the zip.
   (Or unzip it into `~/homebrew/plugins/` and restart Decky.)

Verified on-device with Decky Loader v3.2.10-pre1: three outputs ducked to 40 % for 14.01 s on boot,
then restored to their previous volumes.

xiaominghui/deckyally.name: DeckyAlly v0.1.2
xiaominghui/deckyally.body:
DeckyAlly 0.1.2 实验版。

本版调整恢复策略，解决正常解锁后重复刷新手柄以及锁屏变慢的问题：

- SteamOS 锁屏期间不采集设备状态、不读取服务日志，也不重启 InputPlumber。
- 休眠开始时立即取消正在进行的基线探测，并关闭恢复闸门。
- 唤醒后等待 Steam UI 明确确认已解锁，再给予 SteamOS 8 秒自行恢复时间。
- 输入链路结构正常时不干预；检测状态不确定时也不重启。
- 仅在物理接口或 InputPlumber 合成链路连续 3 次异常时重启一次服务。
- 旧版保存的“每次唤醒都尝试恢复”设置会自动迁移为条件恢复。

本版已通过 TypeScript 类型检查、前端构建、38 项自动化测试及安装包验证。

安装请下载 `DeckyAlly-0.1.2.zip`，不要下载 GitHub 自动生成的 Source code 压缩包。覆盖解压后重启 `plugin_loader.service`。

限制：InputPlumber 没有提供“Steam 已收到实际按键”的无侵入健康状态。因此若设备结构完整但按键仍无响应，本版会保守地不重启，请保留诊断日志供后续改进。

wankyo83/decky-ai.name: Decky AI v0.1.6
wankyo83/decky-ai.body:
## Decky AI v0.1.6

음성 입력을 Gemini API 방식에서 완전한 로컬 Whisper 음성 타이핑으로 변경한 릴리스입니다.

### 주요 변경 사항

- 음성 인식에서 Gemini API 호출을 완전히 제거했습니다.
- `whisper.cpp`와 한국어 지원 다국어 `small-q5_1` 모델을 기기에서 직접 실행합니다.
- 최초 사용 시 필요한 약 200MB 다운로드를 미리 안내합니다.
- 다운로드 중 받은 용량과 전체 용량을 메시지 입력창 위에 표시합니다.
- 음성 인식 결과는 메시지 입력란에만 추가되며 자동으로 질문을 전송하거나 검색하지 않습니다.
- Gemini 무료 사용량을 소진해도 로컬 음성 타이핑을 사용할 수 있습니다.
- 변환할 때만 최대 CPU 4스레드를 사용하고 완료 시 Whisper 프로세스를 종료합니다.

### 파일과 개인정보

- 녹음된 WAV와 임시 변환 TXT는 성공·실패·취소 후 자동 삭제됩니다.
- 중단된 다운로드 임시 파일도 자동 삭제됩니다.
- 다음 음성 입력에 필요한 whisper.cpp 실행 파일 약 9MB와 모델 약 190MB만 설정 폴더에 유지됩니다.
- 녹음된 음성은 Gemini, Google 또는 다른 외부 서버로 전송되지 않습니다.

### 설치

1. 아래 `decky-ai-plugin-v0.1.6.zip`을 다운로드합니다.
2. Decky Loader의 Developer 메뉴에서 `Install Plugin from Zip File`을 선택합니다.
3. 다운로드한 ZIP을 선택합니다.
4. 업데이트 후 이전 화면이 남으면 Decky Loader 또는 Steam을 다시 시작합니다.

Gemini API 키 설정과 검색 모드별 차이, YouTube 공략 검색 방식은 저장소의 README를 참고하세요.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/wankyo83/Decky-AI/compare/v0.1.4...v0.1.6

vahn84/decky-hostsleep.name: v0.5.0 — wake retries until the host is confirmed awake
vahn84/decky-hostsleep.body:
## Changed
- **Wake is now closed-loop.** Broadcast WOL delivery to a sleeping wired NIC through a client-isolating router turned out to be stochastic — byte-identical packets sometimes wake the host, sometimes vanish (verified with packet captures). Instead of firing a blind burst, the plugin now sends a volley, listens on a raw socket for the host to announce itself (gratuitous ARP/DHCP broadcast on resume), and retries every 3 s for up to 45 s.
- **Honest feedback.** The Test button and resume toast now report the real outcome: *confirmed awake in N s* or *no response from host* — never a blind "sent".
- **Resume robustness.** Wake no longer aborts if the first sends fail while the Deck's Wi-Fi is still reassociating after resume — it keeps retrying through the window.

## Notes
- `sol.json` (attached, unchanged from v0.4.2) is still the recommended host-side config for sleep-on-lan.
- On non-root/non-Linux environments the plugin falls back to the previous fire-and-forget burst.

vahn84/decky-hostsleep.name: v0.4.2 — fix wake-then-resleep (buffered sleep packets)
vahn84/decky-hostsleep.body:
## Fixed
- **PC no longer goes straight back to sleep after waking.** The plugin used to send the reversed-MAC sleep packet 3× for redundancy; the extra packets were buffered through the suspend transition and replayed by sleep-on-lan on resume, immediately re-sleeping the host regardless of wake source (WOL, controller, mouse). Sleep is now sent exactly once — the host NIC is awake at that point, so redundancy isn't needed. See [SR-G/sleep-on-lan#22](https://github.com/SR-G/sleep-on-lan/issues/22).

## Changed
- **Wake burst stretched: 8 packets over ~5 s** (was 3 over 0.6 s). Broadcast delivery to a sleeping wired NIC through a client-isolating router is flaky; the longer window makes wake reliable.

## Recommended host-side hardening
Download the attached `sol.json` and drop it next to `sol.exe` on the host PC (then restart the SleepOnLAN scheduled task or reboot). It enables `AvoidDualUDPSending`, so duplicate sleep packets can never re-sleep the PC, whatever the sender does.

vahn84/decky-hostsleep.name: HostSleep v0.4.1
vahn84/decky-hostsleep.body:
**Wake now broadcasts to the /24 directed address too.** On routers that isolate wireless from wired clients and only flood the directed subnet broadcast (e.g. `192.168.0.255`) across the boundary — not global `255.255.255.255` — WOL wake previously never reached the sleeping wired host. Wake and sleep now share the same broadcast logic, hitting the global, configured, and directed-/24 broadcasts on UDP 9 and 7.

Install: download `HostSleep.zip` → Decky → Settings → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP.

vahn84/decky-hostsleep.name: HostSleep v0.4.0
vahn84/decky-hostsleep.body:
**UDP sleep now uses broadcast** — fixes hosts behind routers that isolate wireless from wired clients.

On such routers, unicast from a wireless Deck to a wired host is dropped, so the HTTP sleep and the old unicast UDP sleep never arrived — but layer-2 broadcast still floods across. UDP sleep now sends the reversed-MAC magic packet to the /24 directed broadcast and the global broadcast on UDP 9 and 7, the same envelope WOL wake already uses.

If your host is on Wi-Fi or your router doesn't isolate clients, HTTP mode still works and gives you delivery confirmation; switch to **UDP** mode only if HTTP times out.

Install: download `HostSleep.zip` → Decky → Settings → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP.

vahn84/decky-hostsleep.name: HostSleep v0.3.0
vahn84/decky-hostsleep.body:
First public release.

**HostSleep** sleeps your Steam Remote Play host PC when the Deck suspends and wakes it (Wake-on-LAN) when the Deck resumes — without closing the running game.

- Sleep-on-suspend / wake-on-resume toggles
- "Only when using Remote Play" gating (detects the Deck's `streaming_client` process; wake only fires if the plugin slept the host)
- Sleep transport: HTTP (`sleep-on-lan` REST, default) or reversed-MAC UDP packet
- Manual **Sleep host now** / **Wake host now** test buttons
- **Debug mode**: in-panel timestamped event log (every hook fire, gating decision, packet/request sent, error) + debug toasts on resume

**Install:** download `HostSleep.zip` on the Deck → Decky → Settings → Developer → *Install plugin from ZIP*.
**Host setup:** run [sleep-on-lan](https://github.com/SR-G/sleep-on-lan) on the Windows PC (defaults work). See the README for details.

vaddum/vkbasalt-decky.name: vkBasalt Manager (v1.3.0)
vaddum/vkbasalt-decky.body:
## vkBasalt Manager — Decky Loader Plugin (v1.3.0)

### ✨ Added

- **Profiles**: create as many named configurations as you want! Each profile has its own shader toggles, built-in effect sliders, and toggle key. The "Copy launch option" button adapts automatically: `ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command%` for the Default profile, or `VKBASALT_CONFIG_FILE="..." ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command%` for a named one (vkBasalt's native per-config mechanism)
- **5 more external shaders with sliders**: Border, ColorMatrix, Clarity, Monochrome, and DPX join the 13 already adjustable — 18 external shaders total now expose their most impactful parameter (or two, for GaussianBlur/FakeHDR/Vignette) directly in the Quick Access Menu
- **Collapsible sections**: Built-in Effects and the three external categories (Light/Medium/Heavy) are now toggle buttons with a small squared +/− indicator, collapsed by default — much less scrolling to reach what you actually want to change
- **Reset All Effects to Default** button (Settings, marked with a red ⚠️): resets the active profile's shader toggles and built-in effect sliders, and also resets every external shader's parameter(s) back to their coded default directly in the `.fx` file. Note the split scope: toggles/built-in sliders reset only the active profile, while external shader parameters reset globally across all profiles, since those values live in the shared `.fx` file rather than in a per-profile config
- **Default value shown on every slider**: each of the 22 adjustable parameters (4 built-in + 18 external) now displays its min–max range and default value under its name

### 🎨 Changed

- Category color squares replaced with colored text: shader names and section headers are now tinted (green/orange/red/blue) directly, no separate swatch
- Removed the visual separators between Profiles / Built-in Effects / External Shaders / Settings for a more compact, continuous layout
- Unified font size (13px) across every label, shader name, section header, and button in the plugin
- The "Copy launch option" button wraps and shrinks its text instead of overflowing the panel width

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Profile selection silently reverting to Default**: the dropdown-based selector could revert to the first entry after picking another profile. Replaced with a button-per-profile list (the same reliable pattern already used for Install/Uninstall/Create/Delete elsewhere in the plugin)
- **Broken launch command for profile names containing spaces**: the `VKBASALT_CONFIG_FILE` path is now quoted
- **TypeScript build warning**: removed a `placeholder` prop that isn't part of `TextFieldProps` in `@decky/ui`

### 📦 Installation

Same as before — download `vkbasalt-manager.zip` below, then in Gaming Mode: Quick Access Menu → **Settings** → **Developer** → **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.

See the [README](https://github.com/Vaddum/vkbasalt-manager/blob/main/decky-plugin/README.md) for the full shader list, profile usage, and troubleshooting.

## vkBasalt Manager — Decky Loader Plugin (v1.1.0)

### ✨ Added

- **27 new external ReShade shaders** with dedicated names, categories, and descriptions: 4xBRZ, AdaptiveSharpen, Border, Cartoon, Clarity, ColorMatrix, Comic, CRT, Curves, Daltonize, Defring, DPX, FakeHDR, FilmicAnamorphSharpen, FilmicPass, GaussianBlur, HQ4X, LumaSharpen, Monochrome, Nostalgia, Sepia, SmartVibrance, Technicolor, Technicolor2, Tonemap, Vibrance, Vignette
- **Automatic depth capture**: `depthCapture` in vkBasalt's config now toggles on/off by itself depending on whether a depth-dependent shader (Comic, FilmicAnamorphSharpen) is active — no manual setting to remember
- **Category grouping for external shaders**: split into 🟩 Light, 🟧 Medium, 🟥 Heavy sections (color-matched headers), each sorted alphabetically

### 🎨 Changed

- Category indicators switched from round dots to colored squares (🟦🟩🟧🟥) throughout the UI
- "Toggle key" setting redesigned as a full-width field, consistent with the other buttons in Settings
- "Copy ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command%" now shows a green checkmark on success instead of text feedback

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Case-insensitive shader file matching**: multi-word shader filenames (e.g. `AdaptiveSharpen.fx`) previously failed to be written into `vkBasalt.conf` due to a naive capitalization guess; the plugin now matches filenames properly regardless of case
- **Clipboard copy reliability**: added a fallback to the legacy `execCommand("copy")` method, since the modern Clipboard API is often blocked in Steam's embedded browser context
- **AUR mirror requests**: added a browser-like User-Agent to `curl`/`wget` calls to avoid being blocked by anti-bot mirror rules
- **`OPENSSL_x.x.x not found` errors**: the Decky backend's PyInstaller-bundled libraries were leaking into subprocess calls (`curl`/`wget`/`tar`); `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is now stripped before running them

### 🗑️ Removed

- **Global activation mode**: the plugin no longer offers a toggle between global and per-game activation — it's per-game only now (`ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command%`), which is safer and more predictable. Existing installs that were set to global mode are migrated automatically on first load.
- **Per-shader external parameter editing**: dropped for simplicity; edit a shader's `.fx` file directly if you need to change its defaults
- **"Copy DISABLE_VKBASALT=1" button**: removed as redundant now that global mode is gone
- A few shaders were dropped from the bundle after review: FineSharp (multiple techniques in one file, unsupported by vkBasalt), FilmGrain, FilmGrain2, HighPassSharpen, HSLShift, Levels, LevelsPlus, LiftGammaGain, SmartSharp, Colourfulness, SuperEagle

### 📦 Installation

Same as before — download `vkbasalt-manager.zip` below, then in Gaming Mode: Quick Access Menu → **Settings** → **Developer** → **Install Plugin from ZIP File**.

See the [README](https://github.com/Vaddum/vkbasalt-manager/blob/main/decky-plugin/README.md) for the full shader list and troubleshooting.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Vaddum/vkbasalt-decky/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

## Fix
Clear stale helper installation errors when status polling confirms the Zapret2 helper is available. Previously, installing the helper from a terminal or Desktop Mode after a failed in-plugin installation could leave an outdated **Helper setup** message visible in Gaming Mode.

The UI now hides this outdated setup message for an available helper. Actual service failures remain visible, and setup errors are retained when the helper is still unavailable.

## Update
Install **decky-egpu-helper.zip** using Decky's ZIP installation option. A working helper does **not** need reinstalling for this fix. Existing ON/OFF persistence is unchanged.

## Validation
72 automated tests, TypeScript checks, frontend build and ZIP verification passed, including regression tests for external installation recovery and preserving runtime failures. Tests use mocked Linux services; this fix has not been validated in a live Gaming Mode session.

m15t/decky-egpu-helper.name: v0.2.2 - eGPU Helper
m15t/decky-egpu-helper.body:
## Changes
- Add **Tools → Install helper** to install the bundled Zapret2 helper directly from the plugin.
- Automatically detect the non-root Decky account. Linux handles administrator authentication through pkexec; the plugin never collects or stores your password.
- Keep status responsive during setup, prevent duplicate installation requests, and report cancelled authentication, unavailable authentication dialogs and installation failures.
- Preserve the ON/OFF setting across reboot and power cycles from v0.2.1.

## Install
Download **decky-egpu-helper.zip** and install it using Decky's ZIP installation option. Open **Tools → Install helper**, approve the Linux administrator prompt, then turn DPI bypass ON if wanted. New helper installations default OFF.

The install button requires x86_64 Linux, pkexec and a working polkit authentication agent for the calling session, plus the helper's Python/systemd/nftables/kernel prerequisites. Gaming Mode or service-hosted Decky may not provide an authentication dialog. If no prompt is available, try Desktop Mode or follow the terminal setup in the included README. Missing nftables still requires installation through your distribution's package mechanism.

Existing helper installations are not overwritten. A working v0.2.1 helper does not need reinstalling for this UI update. Development v0.2.0 helper installations still require the migration described in the README.

## Validation
69 automated tests, TypeScript checks, frontend build and ZIP/runtime checksum verification passed. Authentication, systemd and firewall behavior use mocked tests; the native authentication dialog, live Linux/Decky behavior and ISP effectiveness still need testing on the device. Decky remains non-root.

m15t/decky-egpu-helper.name: v0.2.1 - eGPU Helper
m15t/decky-egpu-helper.body:
## Changes
- Add a Zapret2 DPI bypass toggle for TCP HTTP/HTTPS in Tools.
- Remember ON/OFF across reboot and power cycles. The system service restores ON without opening Decky; OFF stays OFF.
- Show saved preference separately from actual runtime status and report service failures.
- Keep Decky non-root, with narrowly scoped start/stop permission for the dedicated helper service.
- Bundle the pinned upstream Zapret2 v1.0.5.2 runtime with SHA-256 verification and its license. No runtime downloads or automatic updates.

## Install
Download **decky-egpu-helper.zip** and install using Decky's ZIP installation option.

**The Zapret2 helper also requires one-time installation on x86_64 Linux.** Extract the ZIP, open `egpu-gamescope/zapret2`, and run:

```sh
sudo /usr/bin/python3 install.py --user YOUR_DECKY_USER
```

Replace `YOUR_DECKY_USER` with the non-root account running Decky. See the included README for nftables/systemd/polkit prerequisites, diagnostics and removal instructions.

If you installed the development 0.2.0 helper, remove it using the README instructions and install the new helper once; updating the ZIP alone does not update the privileged service. New installations default OFF; select ON to enable automatic restoration after reboot.

## Validation and limits
62 automated tests, TypeScript checks, frontend build and ZIP/runtime checksum checks passed. Systemd and firewall tests use mocks; live Linux/Decky behavior, reboot restoration and ISP effectiveness still need device validation. The initial preset handles TCP ports 80/443, not QUIC or DNS, and is not a VPN. Checksums pin runtime bytes; they are not a complete security audit.

revenpl/decky-gpu-picker.name: GPU Picker v0.2.0
revenpl/decky-gpu-picker.body:
## What's in this release

- **Fix: Legion Go / SteamOS showed `Phoenix1` (lspci fallback) instead of the Vulkan device.**
  Root cause: the Decky Loader is a PyInstaller bundle whose dir sits in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`
  and ships its own `libstdc++`/`libz`/`libffi` — the radeon ICD's dependencies resolved
  to those copies → `VK_ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER` → 0 devices. Fixed with a clean-env
  subprocess fallback for Vulkan enumeration (verified on the device).
- Diagnostics now written to the first writable location (`~/.gpu_diag.txt`, `/tmp/gpu_diag.txt`)
  + backend log, instead of a root-owned plugin dir that silently swallowed errors.
- `plugin.json` now declares an explicit `version` (0.2.0).

### Install
1. Decky → Plugins → **Install Plugin** → URL:
   https://github.com/revenpl/decky-gpu-picker/releases/download/v0.2.0/decky-gpu-picker.zip
   (or download the ZIP below and install from file)
2. Open **GPU Picker** — you should see the Vulkan device name and a
   `MESA_VK_DEVICE_SELECT="<vendor:device>!" %command%` launch command.

jacobdonahoe/decky-game-optimizer.body:
## Game Optimizer v0.1.0

Automatically fetches and applies community-sourced optimal settings for your installed Steam Deck games.

### Features
- Scans all installed Steam games across all library locations
- Fetches hardware settings (TDP, GPU clock, refresh rate, FSR mode) from **SteamDeckHQ**
- Fetches compatibility ratings from **ProtonDB**
- Applies settings per-game: launch options, Proton version, and hardware tuning via PowerTools
- SQLite cache with 24h TTL for offline use after initial sync
- Optional auto-apply when a game launches
- Optional restore to defaults when a game exits

### Requirements
- [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz)
- [PowerTools](https://git.ngni.us/NG-SD-Plugins/PowerTools) (optional, for TDP/GPU clock control)

### Installation
1. Download `decky-game-optimizer-v0.1.0.zip`
2. Extract to `~/homebrew/plugins/game-optimizer/` on your Steam Deck
3. Restart the Decky plugin loader
4. Open Quick Access Menu → Game Optimizer

### Data Sources
- [SteamDeckHQ](https://steamdeckhq.com) — hardware settings
- [ProtonDB](https://protondb.com) — compatibility tiers

danielcamilo1/decky-cloud-saves.name: v0.1.0
danielcamilo1/decky-cloud-saves.body:
First release.

- Finds non-Steam games from Steam's `shortcuts.vdf` and locates each one's Proton prefix
  under `steamapps/compatdata`.
- Bundled database of save locations for 51 games, with path templates that resolve both
  inside a Proton prefix and against a real Windows profile.
- Google Drive backup using the `drive.file` scope only, so the plugin can never see
  anything in your Drive that it did not create itself.
- Sign-in via the OAuth device-code flow, which works in Gaming Mode without a browser.
- Snapshot-based sync: each backup is one timestamped zip, with configurable history.
- Steam Cloud style conflict resolution — when both sides changed, you pick, and the copy
  you do not keep is archived locally first.
- Automatic sync when a tracked game starts and exits.
- Windows companion app sharing the same engine, shipped as a single .exe.

## Installing

**Steam Deck** — install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running [Decky Bazaar](https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar)? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-cloud-saves` to it and let it update itself.

**Windows** — download `DeckCloudSaves.exe` and run it. Sign in with the same Google account you linked on the Deck.

Both ends need a Google OAuth client the first time; see the README for the five-minute setup.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-cloud-saves/commits/v0.1.0
