miguellara999/decky-apdetail.name: v0.1.0 — first release
miguellara999/decky-apdetail.body:
First release.

APDetail shows which WiFi access point (BSSID) your Steam Deck is connected to, and lets you
switch to a different AP on the same SSID — useful on mesh networks where the Deck gets stuck
on a distant access point.

### Features

- Current connection: SSID, BSSID, AP vendor, live signal in dBm and %, band, channel, link rate, IP.
- All APs on your SSID sorted by signal, each with vendor, MAC, band, channel, dBm/% and the age
  of the reading. A toggle lists every visible network instead.
- Tap an AP to switch to it — a fast reassociation that does not drop the connection.
- Vendor lookup from an embedded IEEE OUI database (works offline).
- UI follows the Steam language: Spanish when Steam is in Spanish, English otherwise.

### Install

Download `APDetail-v0.1.0.zip` below, then on the Deck: Decky → ⚙ → Developer →
**Install plugin from zip**.

### SteamOS note

SteamOS uses **iwd**, which only allows choosing an access point in developer mode. The first time
you open the plugin, press **Enable iwd developer mode**: it adds a systemd drop-in and restarts
iwd (WiFi drops for a few seconds and reconnects by itself). The same button reverts it, and
uninstalling the plugin reverts it automatically. See the
[README](https://github.com/miguellara999/Decky-APDetail#steamos-and-iwd) for the details.

Tested on SteamOS with a two-AP network sharing one SSID.

logic-mle/decky-guide.name: Decky Guide v1.0.0 · 首个正式版
logic-mle/decky-guide.body:
## Decky Guide 1.0.0 · 首个正式版

在 Steam Deck 游戏模式中自动识别当前游戏，搜索游民星空攻略，并在 Decky 侧栏直接阅读图文内容。

### 主要功能

- 自动匹配中文游戏名称，支持手动搜索并按游戏记住别名。
- 图文阅读、章节目录与关键词筛选、上一页 / 下一页和原文入口。
- 按游戏保存阅读进度，支持继续阅读、三档字号和图片放大至 200%。
- LB / RB 按住滚动，X 打开目录，Y 打开阅读设置，B 分层返回。

### 安装

1. Steam Deck 需先安装 [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader#installation)。本项目以 3.2.8 接口为基准，其他版本兼容性需实机确认。
2. 在本页 Assets 下载 **DeckyGuide-v1.0.0.zip**，无需解压或编译。
3. 在 Decky 设置中启用开发者模式，使用从 ZIP 安装；若界面提供从 URL 安装，可使用下方直链。
4. 安装完成后打开 Decky Guide，启动游戏或手动输入中文游戏名搜索。

[下载安装 ZIP](https://github.com/Logic-mle/decky-guide/releases/download/v1.0.0/DeckyGuide-v1.0.0.zip)

GitHub 自动生成的 Source code 压缩包不含编译产物，不能作为插件安装包。`.zip.sha256` 用于校验下载完整性，不需要安装。

### 从测试版升级

这是基于 0.6.5 功能整理的首个正式开源版本，补齐文档、版本和发布流程。直接覆盖安装；本地存储键保持一致，保留 Steam UI 本地存储时无需迁移。清理本地存储会删除记录。

### 验证与已知限制

发布流程自动执行类型检查、5 项阅读状态测试和构建，并校验 ZIP 内容。未在本次发布流程中执行 Steam Deck 实机兼容性测试；浏览器模拟不能替代原生手柄焦点验证。

需要联网，游民星空页面变化可能影响搜索或解析；重名及非 Steam 游戏可能需要手动匹配。视频、互动地图与脚本内容可能需打开原文查看。阅读进度不跨设备同步。

插件代码采用 MIT 许可证；攻略文字、图片及商标归各自权利人所有。本项目不是 Valve、Decky Loader 或游民星空官方产品。

[完整使用说明](https://github.com/Logic-mle/decky-guide#readme) · [更新日志](https://github.com/Logic-mle/decky-guide/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [问题反馈](https://github.com/Logic-mle/decky-guide/issues/new/choose)

## DSU server manager — now called Gyro DSU

The plugin is no longer tied to a single DSU server and has been renamed from
**Legion Go Gyro DSU** to **Gyro DSU**.

- Check whether a DSU (Cemuhook) server answers on the default port 26760,

**Legion Go Gyro DSU** plugin in Decky.

edinh86/memoryeditor.name: MemoryEditor v0.5.0 — Memory Workbench
edinh86/memoryeditor.body:
The big one: a **Memory Workbench** that brings a Cheat-Engine-style workflow to the Steam Deck.

### 🧰 Memory Workbench (new)
Attach to a game, then press **Open Memory Workbench** in the Quick Access panel for a full-screen page with:

- **Address list** — add addresses by absolute value (`0x…`) or by **module + offset**, give each a label and a type, and watch its **live value**. Per row: set a new value, freeze/unfreeze, view in the hex viewer, or remove.
- **Memory viewer** — a **hex + ASCII** dump of any address.
- **Cheat tables** — **Save / Reload / Delete** a table of addresses per game, keyed by its **Steam App ID**, so your list is there next time.
- **Static tagging** — addresses inside a loaded module are labelled with the module name.
- **Add to Workbench** — send any search result straight into the saved table.

### Everything from before
Async scans with progress + cancel · live value refresh · value freezing + frozen panel · undo · hex/negative numpad entry · range + string search · auto-detect the running game.

### Install (Desktop Mode)
Download `memoryeditor-0.5.0.zip` below, copy it to the Deck, then:

    sudo rm -rf ~/homebrew/plugins/memory-deck ~/homebrew/plugins/memoryeditor
    sudo unzip memoryeditor-0.5.0.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
    sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader

Requires [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader). Personal project — not on any plugin store; install the attached zip manually.

### Notes
- Found addresses aren't guaranteed to be the same after a game restart (ASLR). Saved tables keep your labels and types; re-find the address in a new session, or use `module + offset` for addresses inside a module. (Pointer scanning, which makes cheats survive restarts, is the next planned step.)
- This plugin reads and writes another process's memory. It can crash games. Use at your own risk.

edinh86/memoryeditor.name: MemoryEditor v0.4.1
edinh86/memoryeditor.body:
A revived and modernised fork of [Memory Deck](https://github.com/CameronRedmore/memory-deck) — a scanmem-based memory scanner/editor for the Steam Deck, as a Decky Loader plugin.

### What's in this release
- Modern Decky toolchain (`@decky/ui` + `@decky/api`, `api_version` 1)
- Async scans that no longer freeze the backend, with a live progress bar and a Cancel button
- Live value refresh in the results list (values tick in real time)
- Value freezing, with a dedicated **Frozen Values** panel
- Undo last change
- Hex / range / string search, plus negative and hex entry on the numpad
- Auto-detect the running game (🎮 one-tap attach)
- Correctness pass: fixed float search, the match-array walk, and `set N=` indexing
- Review cleanups: basename-based process filter, hex on signed types, quieter logging

### Install (Desktop Mode)
Download `memoryeditor-0.4.1.zip` below, copy it to the Deck, then:

    sudo rm -rf ~/homebrew/plugins/memory-deck ~/homebrew/plugins/memoryeditor
    sudo unzip memoryeditor-0.4.1.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
    sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader

Requires [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader). This is a personal project and is not published to any plugin store — install the attached zip manually.

### Warning
This plugin directly reads and writes another process's memory. It can crash games and cause other issues. Use at your own risk.

ddordie/newfreedeck-arm64.name: NewFreedeck v0.3 — armada (ARM64)
ddordie/newfreedeck-arm64.body:
armada 掌机（ARM64 / Fedora bootc）适配版，基于上游 NewFreedeck v0.3 release 包。

## 适配改动

- `defaults/bin/7zz`、`defaults/bin/aria2c` → **ARM aarch64 原生二进制**（独立子进程，原生执行最快）
- `py_modules/libnewfreedeck_core.so` → **保持 x86_64**（被宿主 PluginLoader 以 ctypes 加载；armada 的 decky 宿主是 x86_64 + FEX，动态库必须同架构）
- `main.py` → 修复 `_auto_extract` 重复触发导致的两个 7zz 并发解压同一目录（IO 翻倍、系统卡顿）
- 启动前缀 → `/usr/libexec/armada/armada-game-launch %command%`（默认开启，设置项改名「自动添加 armada 启动包装」）

## 安装

```bash
sudo rm -rf ~/homebrew/plugins/NewFreedeck
sudo unzip -o NewFreedeck-v0.3-arm64-fixed5.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```

## 说明

- 仅对新导入的游戏注入启动前缀；已导入的需手动改启动选项或重新导入
- 模拟器 AppImage 需自行从天翼云盘下载（插件不附带），且需 arm64 版本

## What's new

- **Smaller delete button:** each recording in Quick Access now has a compact red trash-can button instead of a full-width "Delete" button. It still asks before deleting.
- **No more lost recorders:** if Showreel's backend stopped while GPU Screen Recorder was starting, the recorder kept running and nothing could find it. Showreel now tracks the recorder from launch and finishes it after a reload.

## Install

michpalm/showreel.name: Showreel 0.1.0
michpalm/showreel.body:
First release.

## What it does

- **One button:** Record, then Stop, in the Quick Access menu. Everything on screen is recorded, Quick Access and Decky panels included, to H.264 MP4 at the screen's own resolution and 60 fps (about 5–6 MB per minute at 1080p on the Steam UI). No audio.
- **Files** go to `~/Videos/Showreel/`, and `latest.mp4` always points to the newest one.
- **Download page** (off by default): switch it on and open `http://<device-ip>:8790/` on another device. Tools can fetch `/recordings.json` and `/latest.mp4`. It is read-only.
- **Steam UI only:** Record is unavailable while a game runs, and a game that starts mid-recording stops it. On SteamOS 3.8, stopping a full-size screen capture while a game draws can crash gamescope.
- **Works with [Ambideck](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck) 1.2.0+**, which steps aside while Showreel records (capture lock described in the README).

## Requirements

SteamOS in Game Mode with Decky Loader, and the GPU Screen Recorder flatpak (`flatpak install flathub com.dec05eba.gpu_screen_recorder`, or Discover in Desktop Mode).

## Install

Download `showreel.zip` below, then Decky → Settings → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**.

Tested on a ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA) with SteamOS 3.8. Nothing in it is device-specific, so it should work on any SteamOS handheld (Steam Deck, ROG Ally, Legion Go…); reports welcome.

nucat176/decky-16x10-fixes.name: v0.1.19-rc.1 — Resonance camera test
nucat176/decky-16x10-fixes.body:
## Camera test for Final Fantasy Resonance

This prerelease tests a possible correction for the image compression or reduced horizontal view reported with v0.1.18 at 1920x1200 on Legion Go 2. It changes the upstream mod's camera policy from preserving vertical field of view to preserving horizontal field of view. The expected result is the original horizontal scene width plus additional scenery above and below. The result has not yet been verified on the device.

HUD constraining stays disabled, the upstream movie correction stays enabled, and the same pinned full-game mod v0.3.0 is used. Only one byte of the mod changes; both original and adjusted hashes are checked before installation.

## Try it

1. Close the game and install `16x10-fixes.zip` from this prerelease through Decky.
2. Open 16:10 Fixes, press **Rescan**, select **Final Fantasy Resonance (Experimental)** and press **Reinstall Fix**. Updating the plugin alone does not replace the game mod.
3. Keep the game at **1920x1200** and SteamOS scaling on **Auto** or **Fit**.
4. Compare the same scene and camera position with v0.1.18. Check the left/right landmarks, extra visibility above/below, and whether characters retain their proportions.

To return to the earlier camera behavior, install the v0.1.18 plugin ZIP and press **Reinstall Fix** again. Both versions keep HUD constraining disabled.

## Validation

Seven backend tests, the Decky build/package, application typechecking with skipLibCheck, and local install/rollback using the actual upstream release ZIP passed. Character proportions, scene framing, HUD, menus, battle transitions and cutscenes still need on-device validation.

yifeplayte/rayneo-control.name: RayNeo Control v1.0.0
yifeplayte/rayneo-control.body:
A Decky Loader plugin that controls RayNeo XR glasses from the Steam Deck over USB — no phone app required.

> ### ⚠️ RayNeo GT Max only
>
> Developed and tested against the **RayNeo GT Max (雷鸟 GT Max)** and nothing else.
>
> The protocol is shared across the family, so other RayNeo / FFalcon models may work — but nothing here has been verified on them, the capability gating has only been exercised against one unit's bitmap, and the brightness table is selected by device type. Treat any other model as untested.
>
> If you try it on one, please open an issue with your `tools/rayneo_cli.py caps` output.

## Install

1. Download `RayNeo-Control.zip` below
2. Decky → **Settings → General** → turn on **开发者模式 / Developer mode**
3. Go to the new **开发者 / Developer** tab → **第三方插件 / Third-Party Plugins** → **浏览文件 / Browse** next to **从 ZIP 压缩文件安装插件 / Install Plugin from ZIP File** → pick the zip and confirm
4. Plug the glasses in over USB-C and press **Connect**

Decky hides the ZIP option behind developer mode, so step 2 is required.

No udev rules, no system packages. `plugin.json` declares `"flags": ["root"]` because the glasses' USB node is `0664 root:root` and a plugin running as `deck` cannot open it.

## What it does

| Section | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| 连接 Connection | Connect / disconnect, model + firmware readout |
| 显示 Display | 屏幕亮度 brightness, 显示模式 2D/3D, 屏幕尺寸 115 % / 100 % / 85 %, 场景模式 通用/电影/护眼/阅读, 动态画质 SDR / AI-HDR, 色彩增强 |
| 声音 Sound | 音量 volume, 音效 标准/轻语/空间环绕, 导音鳍 Sound Tube |

Every control is gated on the capability bitmap the glasses report, so unsupported options grey out rather than failing a write.

## Notable in this release

* **Both sliders write on every tick**, matching the official app, and brightness commits once at the end of a drag. Median round trip measured at **11 ms**, down from 515 ms in the first working version.
* **The panel never assumes a change landed.** Every silent command is confirmed against the status read-back, and a refusal moves the control back to where the hardware actually is rather than showing the requested value.
* **It recovers on its own.** Three unanswered polls release the handle and it keeps looking for the glasses, so replugging needs no button press — while a disconnect *you* asked for is left alone, not undone.
* **Debug mode** (one switch at the bottom of the panel) hides the diagnostic tools and silences the per-frame trace, the startup protocol tables and the timing notes. Errors and warnings are never silenced.

## Known limitations

* **Brightness tops out at 12 steps while the panel may reflect fewer.** The glasses stop reporting brightness above the current display strategy mode's band even though the write is accepted — the same reason the official app's slider appears to fall back on its own. The mode is not on the wire, so the ceiling is fixed rather than learned.
* **阅读 (reading) mode refuses colour enhancement in hardware** and reports success anyway; the toggle is greyed out there rather than trusting the read-back.
* **`0x0D` (brightness save) is sent but has never been observed to do anything** on this hardware. It is kept because the official app sends it.
* **Refresh rate is not exposed** — the protocol supports 60/120 Hz and the device reports 120 Hz, but the official app offers no such setting on this model, so neither does the plugin.
* Changing 3D mode briefly blanks the glasses and shows a split screen. That is the device's normal behaviour.

## How it was built

The official Android app (雷鸟 XR 眼镜 v2.1.2) was decompiled and the native library carrying all device traffic, `libFFalconXRServer.so`, was reverse-engineered to recover the USB framing and the full command set. Nothing from the app is redistributed; this is an independent implementation of the wire protocol.

The command table was recovered twice by two independent methods (raw disassembly and Ghidra's decompiler), which agree on all 33 opcodes. The write-up is in [`docs/PROTOCOL.md`](docs/PROTOCOL.md), and the engineering notes behind the behaviour above are in [`docs/NOTES.md`](docs/NOTES.md).

## Requirements

* Steam Deck with Decky Loader
* RayNeo GT Max glasses

---

MIT licensed. Not affiliated with or endorsed by RayNeo or FFalcon.

m2aadhil/decky-xbox-wireless-helper.name: v1.2.1 – First release
m2aadhil/decky-xbox-wireless-helper.body:
**Xbox Wireless Helper**, a Decky Loader plugin that makes the Xbox Wireless Adapter behave on Bazzite, SteamOS, and other Linux gaming setups.

## ✨ Features

- **Fixes the controller after sleep.** No more unplugging and replugging the adapter. After every wake, the plugin waits for USB to settle and resets the adapter in software. If the gentle reset fails, it escalates: re-authorize → USB port power-cycle → USB reset.
- **Wake the PC with the Xbox button.** One toggle enables wake on the adapter, its hubs, the USB controller, and the matching firmware (ACPI) wake entries. It's re-applied after every reset and replug, and your original settings are restored when you turn it off or uninstall.
- **Pairing button.** Put the adapter into pairing mode from the Quick Access menu, without reaching behind the PC.
- **Live status.** The panel shows the adapter, connected controllers and how each is connected (adapter / Bluetooth / cable), wake status, and the last reset result.
- **Keep USB powered in sleep** (last resort). Switches sleep to s2idle for boards that cut USB power in deep sleep. ⚠️ May keep the fans running.

**Requirements:** Decky Loader, and the `xone` driver for the adapter (default on Bazzite). Pairing and wake-from-sleep need `xone`.

## ⚠️ Known limitations

- Bluetooth-connected controllers can't wake the PC on Linux. Use the adapter or a cable.
- "Keep USB powered in sleep" (s2idle) keeps most desktop boards in their "on" power state, so the fans keep spinning.
- BIOS options vary a lot between manufacturers. Please open an issue with your board model if wake doesn't work for you.

Tested on Bazzite with the Xbox Wireless Adapter for Windows.

## What's Changed
* Bump @types/react-dom from 19.1.1 to 19.3.0 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/m2aadhil/decky-xbox-wireless-helper/pull/7


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/m2aadhil/decky-xbox-wireless-helper/compare/v1.0.0...v1.2.1

## English release

- English CPU, fan, power and startup-restore interfaces, backend status/error messages and installer diagnostics.

No hardware settings were changed for this release. English UI/controller behavior in Steam, real reboot restoration and sustained-load thermal performance still require device validation.

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.1.0
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
## New

- **Security warnings on plugins.** Discover and a plugin's Manage window now show what [Decky Extended Plugins' automated audit](https://decky-extended-plugins.beallio.com/audit) found in the release you'd install, next to Runs as root: **Reads private data**, **Changes system startup**, **Code not in its repo**, **Hidden code**, **Skips HTTPS checks**, **Runs downloaded scripts**, **Known vulnerabilities**, or **Blocked by audit** (not recommended for installation). Routine things many plugins need, like sudo or mount, don't get a warning. A warning isn't proof of harm, and no warning isn't proof of safety.
- **"What the badges on plugins mean"**, a notice at the top of Discover: tap **More** to read what every badge means, with a link to the audit.
- **Fork badge.** DeckyHub's list now includes forks that carry a plugin on after its original stopped (archived, gone, or no release since), but only while the fork is the active one. They show **Fork**, and the card names the original.
- **Six more languages**: Italian, Polish, Turkish, Dutch, Czech and Portuguese (Portugal), 17 in all. A system language set to Portuguese (Portugal) picks it automatically. Translations other than English are made automatically and may have mistakes; Settings → General says so.
- **Hide DeckyHub's Quick Access tab**: Settings → General → **DeckyHub tab in Quick Access**. With it off, open DeckyHub from Decky's plugin list; update notices still come.
- **Registry Channel**, in DeckyHub's own **Manage** window (Quick Access → DeckyHub → **Manage**): **Pre-release** shows plugins and list changes still being tested, and Discover and Updates say **Pre-release registry** while it's on. **Stable** stays the default, and DeckyHub falls back to it if the pre-release list can't be loaded.

## Changed

- DeckyHub reads its plugin list from the registry's published releases, with the same list as before as a fallback, and accepts a bigger list (up to 4 MB) so it can keep growing.

## Fixed

- **The D-pad works again after opening a plugin's GitHub page.** Coming back from Steam's browser (Manage → Repository, a card's Menu button, or the links in Settings), nothing had controller focus until you touched the screen. Focus now returns to the button you came from.

## Under the hood

- Browser tests for the warnings, the Fork badge and the Registry Channel, and a test that every translation keeps its placeholders.
- Docs brought up to date, and DeckyHub is called a plugin hub, not a store.

## Try it on your Deck

- Discover: tap **More** on "What the badges on plugins mean" and check every badge is explained; plugins with audit warnings show orange badges (red for Blocked).
- Open a plugin's **Manage** window, press **Repository**, then **B**: you're back on its **Manage** button and the D-pad works.
- Settings → General: pick one of the new languages, then turn **DeckyHub tab in Quick Access** off and on.
- Updating from 3.0.0 keeps all your settings, custom repositories and registries.

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.1.0-rc.4
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
## New

- **Hide DeckyHub's Quick Access tab**: Settings → General → **DeckyHub tab in Quick Access**. With it off, open DeckyHub from Decky's plugin list. Update notices still come.

## Changed

- DeckyHub reads its plugin list from the registry's published releases. **Stable** gets the newest stable list and **Pre-release** the newest list of all. If a release can't be read, DeckyHub uses the same list as before, so nothing you see changes.

## Try it on your Deck

- Turn **DeckyHub tab in Quick Access** off: the icon leaves the Quick Access tab strip, and DeckyHub still opens from Decky's plugin list. Turn it back on.
- Restart with the tab off: it stays hidden.
- Switch Registry Channel (DeckyHub → **Manage**) to Pre-release and back; the list reloads both times.

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.1.0-rc.3
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
## Changed

- **Registry Channel** has moved from Settings → Repositories to DeckyHub's own **Manage** window (Quick Access → DeckyHub → **Manage**), next to the Update Channel. It works the same: **Pre-release** shows plugins still being tested, and the list reloads as soon as you switch.

## Try it on your Deck

- Open Quick Access → DeckyHub → **Manage** and reach **Registry Channel** with the D-pad.
- Switch it to Pre-release: Discover shows the **Pre-release registry** badge. Switch back: the badge is gone.
- Settings → Repositories no longer shows the channel.

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.1.0-rc.2
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
A pre-release for testing. Install it from DeckyHub's update window on the Pre-release channel.

## New

- **Fork badge.** The plugin list now includes forks that carry a plugin on after its original stopped (the original is archived, gone, or hasn't released since). They show a **Fork** badge next to Runs as root; on a card it names the original, and **More** on Discover's notice explains it.
- **Pre-release registry badge.** With **Settings → Repositories → Registry Channel** set to **Pre-release**, Updates and Discover say **Pre-release registry**, so you know you're looking at the list still being tested.

## Fixed

- **The D-pad works again after viewing a plugin's GitHub page.** Coming back from Steam's browser (Manage → Repository, a card's Menu button, or the links in Settings), nothing had controller focus until you touched the screen. DeckyHub now puts focus back on the button you came from.

## Under the hood

- Browser tests for the audit warnings, the Registry Channel and the Fork badge.
- Docs brought up to date: audit warnings, the Registry Channel, the plugin list's release file now refreshed every hour.

## Try it on your Deck

- Open a plugin's **Manage** window, press **Repository**, then **B**: you're back on that plugin's **Manage** button and the D-pad moves.
- On a card, press the **Menu** button to open its GitHub page, then **B**: focus is on the same button.
- Switch **Registry Channel** to **Pre-release**: the **Pre-release registry** badge shows on Discover, and forks such as ProtonDB Badges show **Fork**. Switch back to **Stable**: the badge is gone.

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.1.0-rc.1
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
A pre-release for testing. Install it from DeckyHub's update window on the Pre-release channel.

## New

- **Security warnings on plugins.** Discover and a plugin's Manage window now warn when [Decky Extended Plugins' automated audit](https://decky-extended-plugins.beallio.com/audit) found something worth knowing in the release you'd install, shown next to Runs as root: **Reads private data**, **Changes system startup**, **Code not in its repo**, **Hidden code**, **Skips HTTPS checks**, **Runs downloaded scripts**, **Known vulnerabilities**, or **Blocked by audit** (not recommended for installation). Routine things many plugins need, like sudo or mount, don't get a warning. Tap **More** on Discover's notice to read what each one means. A warning isn't proof of harm, and no warning isn't proof of safety.
- **Registry Channel** (Settings → Repositories). Choose **Pre-release** to see plugins and registry changes still being tested before everyone gets them. **Stable** stays the default; if the pre-release list can't be loaded, DeckyHub uses the stable one.

## Changed

- DeckyHub accepts a bigger plugin list (up to 4 MB), so the registry can keep growing.

## Try it on your Deck

- Discover: plugins with warnings show the orange badges (red for Blocked) next to Runs as root; open **More** on the notice and check every warning is explained and readable.
- Settings → Repositories: switch Registry Channel to Pre-release and back. The list reloads each time, and your settings, custom repositories and registries stay as they were.
- Updating from 3.0.0 keeps all your settings.
